   154 ## Settled KSG mathematics and bounded numerics
   155 
   156 Domain and maps:
   157 
   158 - `n >= 2`, `1 <= k < n`;
   159 - exclusive KSG has `k-1 <= nx,ny < n` and passes `x=nx+1`, `y=ny+1`;
   160 - inclusive Ehrlich has `k <= x,y <= n` after its declared shell checks and passes them directly;
   161 - only coefficients `(+1,+1,-1,-1)` are eligible; the non-cancelling heuristic remains on general
   162   digamma arithmetic.
   163 
   164 Under the typed positive-integer premise `psi(m)=H_(m-1)-gamma`, exact algebra gives
   165 
   166 ```text
   167 T = H_(k-1)+H_(n-1)-H_(x-1)-H_(y-1)
   168   = (H_(n-1)-H_(max(x,y)-1))-(H_(min(x,y)-1)-H_(k-1)).
   169 ```
   170 
   171 With `D=H_(n-1)-H_(k-1)`, monotonicity gives `-D <= T <= D`. This is an exact-real local-term
   172 bound, permits negative values, and is not a binary64-error, MI, redundancy, PID-atom, estimator
   173 bias, calibration, support, or application bound.

   467 Settled facts and live discrepancies to preserve:
   468 
   469 - For positive integer `m`, `psi(m)=H_(m-1)-gamma`; hence for `n>=2`, `1<=k<n`, and valid
   470   integer arguments `x,y`, the four-term score is
   471   `H_(k-1)+H_(n-1)-H_(x-1)-H_(y-1)` with coefficients `(+1,+1,-1,-1)` in nats.
   472 - Exclusive KSG counts require `k-1<=nx,ny<n` and use `x=nx+1`, `y=ny+1`. Inclusive Ehrlich
   473   shared-exclusions counts require `k<=x,y<=n` and pass the arguments without a successor. These
   474   domains and mappings are not interchangeable.
   475 - The selected Neumaier-prefix plus symmetric-range binary64 implementation has, on the frozen
   476   8,198-cell Decimal corpus, maximum absolute error `8*EPSILON` nats, 40 maximum-error ties, and
   477   zero source-swap asymmetries. The allowed `32*EPSILON` absolute gate is bounded evidence, not an
   478   ULP bound, a correct-rounding theorem, or a universal error theorem.
   479 - The exact `Fraction` route covers 6,920 feasible tuples through `n=16`. Lean proves 14 narrow
   480   exact algebra theorems conditional on the typed integer-digamma premise. Z3 checks three
   481   premise-explicit QF_UFLIRA obligations with uninterpreted harmonic values. Lean and Z3 share the
   482   analytic premise and the human sign/index mapping; neither proves binary64 or estimator validity.
   483 - The v1 route memo incorrectly labelled 16/764 maximum-error cells as compensated. The retained
   484   erratum records the actual comparison: plain 8/0/39, Neumaier 8/0/39, selected symmetric range
   485   8/0/40. The extra selected tie is first `(4096,1,2048,2048)`.
   486 - Live source/checker work now closes six gates that revision 2 records open: maximum-tie custody,
   487   generator drift and reseal custody, and three source dataflow shadows. The self-test therefore
   488   rejects 91 mutations (`4+2+19+66`), while revision-2 public text still says 85. Do not rewrite
   489   revision 2 after observing this result; issue a new revision or explicitly retain the six gates
   490   open.
   491 - Four release families eventually combine KSG and PID2 revision strings. A PID2-first commit is
   492   false because parent `626ded7` lacks the KSG implementation. The KSG milestone must use the
   493   intermediate KSG-only revision for those four families; the later PID2 milestone advances them
   494   to the combined revision.
   495 
   496 Exact stop point: PID2 source/checker hardening passes on the combined dirty tree with 129
   497 registered mutations, two bidirectional scope-isolation preflights, 18 distinct compiled tests in
   498 debug and release (36 invocations), focused Rust tests, Rustdoc, catalog, release, review-evidence,
   499 and identity gates. It is deliberately held uncommitted until a coherent KSG parent exists. Two
   500 external hostile reviews independently confirmed the PID2 arithmetic but found that two inventory
   501 mutations read live artifacts while public prose says copied artifacts; that wording defect must
   502 be corrected before PID2 release. One review additionally requested revision-1 custody, per-scope
   503 copied-root baselines, and two pin mutations; another requested a compiled-test name mutation and
   504 toolchain receipt. These are open hardening decisions, not silently accepted conclusions.
   505 
   506 The active next action is to finish hostile KSG mathematical and release-slice audits, decide and
   507 author a non-destructive revision 3 if required, harden the 91-mutation suite against false-green
   508 diagnostics, construct KSG-only intermediate release identities, and validate the exact staged
   509 snapshot before a small unsigned push. The full-tree clippy run is currently red only in an
   510 unrelated uncommitted Imin boundary test (`needless_range_loop`); no KSG/PID2 scientific conclusion
   511 is inferred from that failure.

```text
     1 # Claim `KSG-INTEGER-HARMONIC-001`, revision 4
     2 
     3 ## Status, chronology, and evidence class
     4 
     5 Revision 4 is the active **post-result integration** revision. It was written after the exact
     6 identity, schema-2 corpus, formal extensions, and modular residues were observed; it is not a
     7 preregistration. It preserves revisions 1--3 byte-for-byte. Revision 3 remains a frozen
     8 pre-closure **NO-GO** because its custody and completion statements were not simultaneously true.
     9 
    10 The exact positive-integer arithmetic core, the scoped Lean/Z3 obligations, and the bounded
    11 8,198-row modular classification are **GO on their stated domains**. Repository/publication
    12 integration is **NO-GO** until the open gates in `integration-disposition-v4.md` close on one
    13 isolated settled tree. No final revision-4 evidence matrix or decision is asserted yet.
    14 
    15 ## Exact object, domain, range, and units
    16 
    17 Let
    18 
    19 ```text
    20 H_0 = 0
    21 H_j = sum_(r=1)^j 1/r
    22 T = psi(k) + psi(n) - psi(x) - psi(y)
    23 D = H_(n-1) - H_(k-1).
    24 ```
    25 
    26 Information quantities are in **nats**. The rectangular positive-integer arithmetic domain fed by
    27 the inventoried estimator mappings is
    28 
    29 ```text
    30 n >= 2
    31 1 <= k < n
    32 k <= x <= n
    33 k <= y <= n.
    34 ```
    35 
    36 Exclusive KSG counts satisfy `k-1 <= nx,ny < n` and map to `x=nx+1,y=ny+1`. Inventoried
    37 anchor-inclusive Ehrlich ISX/PID3 counts satisfy `k <= x,y <= n` after their declared shell checks
    38 and are passed directly. These inequalities are an outer box, not a claim that every tuple is
    39 realizable by unique-shell neighbour geometry. Only the coefficient vector
    40 `(+1,+1,-1,-1)` is eligible.
    41 
    42 Under the typed analytic premise
    43 
    44 ```text
    45 psi(m) = H_(m-1) - gamma
    46 ```
    47 
    48 at the four positive integer arguments, exact cancellation gives
    49 
    50 ```text
    51 T = H_(k-1) + H_(n-1) - H_(x-1) - H_(y-1)
    52   = (H_(n-1) - H_(max(x,y)-1))
    53     - (H_(min(x,y)-1) - H_(k-1)).
    54 ```
    55 
    56 Harmonic monotonicity yields the sharp two-sided bound over that rectangular arithmetic domain
    57 
    58 ```text
    59 -D <= T <= D.
    60 ```
    61 
    62 The pure Lean arithmetic theorem admits the slightly larger domain `1 <= k <= n`; this does not
    63 authorize a runtime estimator to accept `k=n`. The box-domain bound permits negative terms. It is
    64 forbidden to clamp them, and it is not a bound on MI, redundancy, any PID atom, estimator bias,
    65 calibration, or application error. At the smallest rectangular boundary `n=2,k=1`, helper tuples
    66 realize `+D`, `-D`, and zero. The `-D` tuple is not asserted to be realizable by a runtime
    67 unique-shell geometry. A hostile-review set argument suggests the additional runtime constraint
    68 `x+y <= n+k` and a stronger asymmetric lower bound, but revision 4 does not promote either as a
    69 project theorem until the count-set map, exact/formal proof, compiled witnesses, mutations, and
    70 provenance routes close.
    71 
    72 ## Frozen schema-2 and binary64 result
    73 
    74 The reviewed generator/fixture/sidecar digests are:
    75 
    76 ```text
    77 a4ef8a87a154ad0e1edd84013f025462fe80c32e2012f07154bb8db8ca78143b  generator
    78 560e36346272c845ad1cd443c13741738b06b02a8035ea43c8ced06b1d80147c  fixture
    79 fb91172bdb767b3e11e15ef4e89bb0482b932c5c2450f87d566245eda87a8ec7  sidecar file
    80 ```
    81 
    82 The fixture contains 8,198 unique ordered rows: 6,920 exhaustive rectangular-arithmetic
    83 outer-box rows through `n=16` and 1,278 declared stress rows. “Exhaustive” does not mean
    84 runtime-realizable. The sufficient structural endpoint predicate is
    85 
    86 ```text
    87 (nx == k-1 and ny == n-1) or (nx == n-1 and ny == k-1).
    88 ```
    89 
    90 It identifies 354 rows, split into 240 exhaustive and 114 stress rows. On this frozen corpus only,
    91 the modular certificate proves that exact rational `T=0` **iff** this predicate holds. The
    92 structural predicate is only asserted sufficient outside this corpus; no universal
    93 harmonic-zero-classification theorem is claimed.
    94 
    95 The selected binary64 route uses a Neumaier-compensated harmonic prefix and sorted symmetric range
    96 association. On exactly these 8,198 rows it has:
    97 
    98 ```text
    99 binary64-rounded-reference maximum = 8 * f64::EPSILON nats
   100 first rounded-reference maximum    = (4096,1,2048,2048)
   101 rounded-reference maximum ties     = 40
   102 exact-rational maximum upper bound < 9.761311 * f64::EPSILON nats
   103 unique exact-rational maximum      = row 7673, (4096,4,2049,2049)
   104 selected value at exact maximum    = -0x1.6b52fe6a01407p+2
   105 allowed finite-corpus ceiling      = 32 * f64::EPSILON nats
   106 source-swap bit asymmetries        = 0
   107 selected endpoint outputs          = 354 positive zeros
   108 selected endpoint negative zeros   = 0
   109 selected endpoint nonzeros         = 0
   110 selected full-corpus outputs        = 354 positive zeros, 0 negative zeros, 7,844 nonzeros
   111 ```
   112 
   113 The `8*EPSILON` quantity first rounds each stored Decimal reference to binary64. It is not the
   114 error against the stored Decimal value or exact harmonic rational, not eight ULPs, and not an
   115 ordered-binary64-position distance. A separately implemented 160-digit directed-rounding
   116 enclosure gives the exact-rational maximum above and isolates its unique row. The strict epsilon
   117 comparison uses a downward-rounded threshold; the complete interval is retained in
   118 `failures/decimal-reference-metric-conflation-v4.md`. Its baseline-first self-test kills 29/29
   119 registered mutations in normal and optimized Python.
   120 
   121 The stored 80-digit prefix-sum strings differ textually from the exact-rational correctly rounded
   122 80-digit strings on 6,509 rows and differ numerically on 5,934 rows. The maximum numeric
   123 difference is `8.18e-77` nats at unique zero-based row 7,952, but all 8,198 pairs convert to the
   124 same binary64 value. The exact-rounded vector digest is
   125 `1d33f7f89c973a70c4e76619a4fa494ce163992509d31be7daea381bb1e9e747`.
   126 This is a retained negative result, not permission to conflate the references.
   127 
   128 Over the same selected Neumaier prefix, ordinary four-term left association is nonzero at 150/354
   129 endpoints and produces zero negative zeros. A separately constructed naive prefix has a
   130 different 121/354 result and zero negative zeros. Neither signed-zero count is a discriminating
   131 theorem; they are exact finite-corpus regression tripwires.
   132 
   133 ## Behavioral bridges
   134

   150 ## Formal and modular results
   151 
   152 The revision-4 Lean source has SHA-256
   153 `32b5d5e11aa244cb9683d71281f05b27e8093dd9a4d5e677ad4b1e68ffc76ee4`.

   166 In each selected prime field `1000033`, `1000037`, and `1000081`, all 354 endpoints have
   167 zero residue and all 7,844 nonendpoints have nonzero residue. Since every selected prime exceeds
   168 the maximum reciprocal summand denominator/index `999999`, each denominator in every `1/j`
   169 summand is invertible; a nonzero residue therefore implies the exact rational is nonzero. The

   234   described beside runtime mappings without saying that shell geometry can forbid box tuples.
   235 - **Exact separator:** at `n=2,k=1`, helper tuple `(x,y)=(2,2)` gives `-D=-1`, but a unique shell
   236   has strict marginal sets `A,B` with `|A intersect B|=k-1`, hence
   237   `x+y=|A union B|+k+1<=n+k=3`; `(2,2)` is not runtime-realizable.
   238 - **Correction:** call `[-D,D]` sharp only on the rectangular arithmetic domain and deny runtime
   239   attainability transfer.
   240 - **Follow-up hypothesis:** the same set map suggests `x+y<=n+k` and, with
   241   `a=floor((n+k)/2)`, `b=ceil((n+k)/2)`, the stronger runtime lower bound
   242   `H_(k-1)+H_(n-1)-H_(a-1)-H_(b-1)`. Neither is promoted here until exact, formal, compiled,
   243   mutation, and provenance routes close.
   244 - **Residual:** a valid arithmetic theorem can still be wrong for an estimator if its domain is
   245   treated as an exact image rather than an outer approximation.
   246 
```

     1 # Call-site and index map for KSG-INTEGER-HARMONIC-001 revision 1
     2 
     3 ## Exact special-function reduction
     4 
     5 For positive integers, the digamma recurrence and base value give
     6 
     7 ```text
     8 psi(1) = -gamma,
     9 psi(m + 1) = psi(m) + 1/m,
    10 therefore psi(m) = H_(m-1) - gamma.
    11 ```
    12 
    13 Substitution into a four-term combination with coefficients `(+1,+1,-1,-1)` cancels all four
    14 copies of `gamma`.  For harmonic indices
    15 
    16 ```text
    17 K = k - 1,
    18 N = n - 1,
    19 a = min(x_index, y_index),
    20 b = max(x_index, y_index),
    21 ```
    22 
    23 where `K <= a <= b <= N`, the exact-real term is
    24 
    25 ```text
    26 H_K + H_N - H_a - H_b = (H_N - H_b) - (H_a - H_K).
    27 ```
    28 
    29 The last form is symmetric in the two counts before binary64 subtraction.  Exact `Fraction`
    30 enumeration of every feasible tuple through `n = 16` found no identity or index failure.  The
    31 three independently hand-checked boundaries retained by the generator are `11/6`, `5/6`, and
    32 `-1/3`.
    33 
    34 ## Direct runtime sites
    35 
    36 | Function/path | Current positive-integer arguments | Harmonic indices | Classification |
    37 |---|---|---|---|
    38 | `ksg::ksg_local_mi_terms_backend`, tree branch | `psi(k)+psi(n)-psi(nx+1)-psi(ny+1)` | `k-1,n-1,nx,ny` | migrate |
    39 | `ksg::ksg_local_mi_terms_backend`, brute branch | same | same | migrate through the same helper |
    40 | `ksg::ksg_local_mi_terms_xblocks_with_budget`, tree branch | `psi(k)+psi(n)-psi(nx+1)-psi(ny+1)` | `k-1,n-1,nx,ny` | migrate |
    41 | `ksg::ksg_local_mi_terms_xblocks_with_budget`, brute branch | same | same | migrate through the same helper |
    42 | `isx::isx_local_diagnostics` (`EhrlichKsg`) | `psi(k)+psi(n)-psi(n_alpha)-psi(n_t)` | `k-1,n-1,n_alpha-1,n_t-1` | migrate |
    43 | `pid3::redundancy_for_antichain` | `psi(k)+psi(n)-psi(n_alpha)-psi(n_t)` | `k-1,n-1,n_alpha-1,n_t-1` | migrate |
    44 | `isx::isx_redundancy_heuristic_sketch` | `psi(k)+psi(n)+psi(shared)-0.5psi(s1)-0.5psi(s2)` | not applicable | retain general digamma; coefficients sum to two |
    45 
    46 The KSG marginal counts exclude the anchor.  The validated unique joint shell has exactly `k-1`
    47 strict-interior neighbors; each lies inside both marginal strict radii, so
    48 `k-1 <= nx,ny <= n-1`.  The cited shared-exclusions paths initialize their marginal counts with
    49 the anchor, hence `k <= n_alpha,n_t <= n`; subtracting one gives the same admitted harmonic-index
    50 domain.  These bounds are consequences of the existing shell validation and count construction;
    51 the arithmetic change does not validate the neighbor search independently.
    52 
    53 ## Indirectly affected paths
    54 
    55 - Hyperbolic KSG uses the same KSG kernel with a different typed metric/support mode.
    56 - `LocalMinKsg` and `DisjunctionFromLocalMi` heuristics call the KSG local-term paths and inherit
    57   the revision; `HeuristicSketch` deliberately does not.
    58 - Continuous co-information, PID2, incomplete/full PID3, hierarchy, and composed pipelines can
    59   inherit changed values through KSG or continuous shared-exclusions calls.
    60 - Python entry points are bindings to these Rust paths and do not form a separate estimator.
    61 
    62 Every release-scope family that can emit a changed scalar must therefore either migrate its own
    63 estimator revision or retain child reports whose revisions unambiguously identify all changed
    64 constituents.  Raw scalar compositions without such child identity require an explicit revision
    65 migration.
    66 
    67 ## Shared cut and residual boundaries
    68 
    69 The critical cut is the conjunction of this call-site classification and the off-by-one index map.
    70 The Decimal corpus and exact rational route share that mathematical cut.  Neighbor counts, shell
    71 semantics, support assumptions, estimator consistency, statistical calibration, application
    72 validity, and a universal binary64 error bound remain outside it.

     1 # Decimal-reference metric conflation, revision 4
     2 
     3 ## Failure
     4 
     5 The first revision-4 packet described an observed maximum of
     6 `8 * f64::EPSILON` nats with 40 ties as though it were error against the stored
     7 80-digit Decimal values. That was false. Both the Rust test and the Python

    11 The old number therefore measured

    13 ```text

    15 ```

    17 It did not measure

    20 abs(exact_value(selected_binary64) - exact_harmonic_rational).

    22 
    23 Frozen revisions 1--3 are not rewritten. This memo preserves the revision-4
    24 false statement and its correction.
    25 
    26 ## Separately implemented directed-enclosure route
    27 
    28 `scripts/check-ksg-harmonic-exact-enclosure.py` does not import pid-rs, the
    29 oracle generator, or the main revision checker. It reconstructs the 8,198-row
    30 order, then builds lower and upper harmonic-prefix bounds with separate
    31 160-digit `ROUND_FLOOR` and `ROUND_CEILING` Decimal contexts. For each
    32 nonendpoint row it propagates the signs through directed interval arithmetic.
    33 Structural endpoints are cancelled symbolically. This route assumes the Python
    34 Decimal implementation obeys its documented directed-rounding semantics; it
    35 is computational enclosure evidence, not a kernel proof.

    37 Both interval endpoints round to the same 80-digit `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` value for
    38 all 8,198 rows. The newline-delimited exact-rounded vector has SHA-256:
    39 
    40 ```text

    46 the formula, generated row order, and structural-endpoint classification with the directed route,
    47 so engine separation is not failure independence. That finite cross-check does not extend to the
    48 1,278 stress rows; those retain Python Decimal directed rounding as a computational premise.

     1 # Retained formal seams and negative controls for revision 2
     2 
     3 ## Full analytic digamma truth is not formalized
     4 
     5 The tempting stronger statement was “the complete positive-integer digamma theorem is formally
     6 verified.” It is not. The Lean route declares a proposition parameter
     7 
     8 ```text
     9 PositiveIntegerDigammaPremise psi eulerConstant
    10 ```
    11 
    12 and the SMT route asserts the four required instances. Both then prove cancellation. Neither
    13 constructs the analytic digamma function, Euler's constant, its base value, or its recurrence.
    14 The older mathematical recurrence/base derivation remains a separate evidence route and source
    15 correspondence. Therefore the permitted wording is “formally checked conditional cancellation,”
    16 not “formally verified digamma.”
    17 
    18 ## The SMT harmonic function is intentionally uninterpreted
    19 
    20 A second tempting overstatement was “both formal systems define and prove the harmonic finite
    21 sum.” Only Lean does. Z3 treats `harmonic : Int -> Real` as arbitrary. This is useful: the
    22 range/index/symmetry results are algebraic and therefore stronger than a harmonic-only instance,
    23 and the encoding does not share Lean's finite-sum machinery. It does not supply a second
    24 finite-sum recurrence proof.
    25 
    26 ## Cross-tool carrier equivalence remains a reviewed seam
    27 
    28 Lean uses `ℕ`, exact `ℚ` finite sums, and a coercion to `ℝ`; SMT uses constrained mathematical
    29 `Int`, exact `Real`, and an uninterpreted function. Each file proves its own domain consequences.
    30 There is no third machine-checked theorem equating the Lean and SMT abstract syntax or proving a
    31 translation validator. The object/sign/index table in `formal-assurance-v2.md` is the retained
    32 human correspondence layer.
    33 
    34 ## Solver UNSAT is not a kernel-checked proof certificate
    35 
    36 Z3 4.16.0 returns exact `unsat` text for each pinned quantifier-free negated obligation, but the
    37 checker does not request or replay an independently verified proof certificate. The Lean kernel
    38 route diversifies this risk for the overlapping algebra. It does not turn the Z3 executable into
    39 a verified kernel.
    40 
    41 ## Baseline-first Lean mutations
    42 
    43 The baseline compiled before mutation. All nine altered theorem sources failed to compile:

    46 |---|---|
    47 | `shift_harmonic_denominator` | the universal successor recurrence depends on the exact `i+1` denominator |
    48 | `break_range_maximum` | selecting a non-maximum endpoint breaks the exact range identity |
    49 | `break_range_minimum` | selecting a non-minimum endpoint breaks the exact range identity |
    50 | `break_four_term_coefficient` | the Euler-constant cancellation needs signs `(+1,+1,-1,-1)` |
    51 | `shift_exclusive_argument_twice` | KSG's formula argument is `count+1`, not `count+2` |
    52 | `shift_anchor_inclusive_argument` | an anchor-inclusive count receives no additional successor |
    53 | `make_exclusive_upper_bound_strict` | `count=n-1` legitimately maps to formula argument `n` |
    54 | `corrupt_exclusive_count_formula` | `(nx+1)-1` maps to `nx`, not `nx+1` |
    55 | `corrupt_source_swap_target` | symmetry is equality, not equality up to a constant |

    57 These failures test load-bearing proof content. They are not evidence that the unmutated theorem
    58 matches Rust or a publication.

    60 ## Baseline-first SMT mutations
    61 
    62 Each unmodified script first passed a satisfiable positive-theorem preflight and an unsatisfiable
    63 negated-theorem check. All eight semantic mutations then returned exact `sat` and were rejected:
    64 
    65 | Mutation | Exposed counterexample class |
    66 |---|---|
    67 | `nonzero_cancellation_offset` | exact cancellation cannot tolerate an added constant |
    68 | `misbind_y_digamma_premise` | a premise attached to the wrong argument does not support the displayed term |

    70 | `replace_min_with_left_argument` | the `x>y` branch requires the true minimum |
    71 | `replace_max_with_left_argument` | the `x<y` branch requires the true maximum |
    72 | `nonzero_exclusive_predecessor_offset` | exact predecessor recovery has no offset |
    73 | `shift_exclusive_x_twice` | a doubled KSG successor violates the declared index map |
    74 | `shift_anchor_inclusive_x` | adding a successor to an inclusive count violates the direct map |

    76 A satisfying mutant is a counterexample to that mutant, not to the baseline theorem.
    77 
    78 ## Runtime and scientific boundaries retained
    79 
    80 The formal objects contain declared counts, not neighbor coordinates or distance comparisons.
    81 Consequently they cannot detect a wrong strict/interior shell, zero radius, nonunique neighbor,
    82 wrong disjunction event, wrong anchor inclusion in runtime code, or a call site that passes another
    83 integer. Tiny compiled witnesses and final source/feature replay remain necessary.

     1 # Retained negative control: modular zero-residue collisions
     2 
     3 ## Refuted inference
     4 
     5 The inference
     6 
     7 ```text
     8 T mod p = 0  =>  exact rational T = 0
     9 ```
    10 
    11 is false even when prime `p` exceeds every reciprocal-summand denominator/index occurring in the
    12 frozen row.
    13 
    14 ## Counterexamples
    15 
    16 For rejected prime `p=1000003`, the ordered u32 big-endian residue-vector digest is
    17 
    18 ```text
    19 d90959d75ff1c84c56c3354b5b5f5d7d633fc873692266bd5d61874eb8254111.
    20 ```
    21 
    22 Four nonendpoint rows have zero residue:
    23 
    24 ```text
    25 index 8045: (1000000,3,2,3),         T =  H_999999 - H_3 > 0
    26 index 8049: (1000000,3,3,2),         T =  H_999999 - H_3 > 0
    27 index 8069: (1000000,4,3,3),         T =  H_999999 - H_3 > 0
    28 index 8093: (1000000,4,999999,999999), T = H_3 - H_999999 < 0.
    29 ```
    30 
    31 The strict signs follow because `sum_(j=4)^999999 1/j` is a nonempty sum of positive rationals.
    32 These are exact counterexamples, not binary64 observations.
    33 
    34 ## Accepted implication
    35 
    36 If `p` exceeds the maximum reciprocal-summand denominator/index, then every `1/j` summand
    37 denominator is invertible in the field. Exact rational zero must reduce to residue zero. Therefore
    38 the contrapositive is sound:
    39 
    40 ```text
    41 nonzero residue => exact rational nonzero.
    42 ```
    43 
    44 The converse is not sound. Selected primes `1000033`, `1000037`, and `1000081` happen to have
    45 nonzero residue at all 7,844 frozen nonendpoints. Combining that bounded separation with pairwise
    46 structural cancellation proves an iff only for the exact ordered 8,198-row corpus.
    47 
    48 ## Independence and non-implications
    49 
    50 The selected triple provides redundant fault diversity. It is not CRT reconstruction and the
    51 three fields are not three independent mathematical proofs: they share the row corpus, exact
    52 formula, human index map, and generator class. The result classifies no harmonic zeros outside the
    53 corpus and proves nothing about KSG neighbor geometry, MI estimation, Ehrlich shared exclusions,
    54 MGW SxPID, any PID atom, support, calibration, or applications.
    55 
    56 The pre-artifact digest
    57 `1d5f61b1135b8bb69f6cf11c377ad8e9ba3ba3b806421bdff10a1d24355120bc`
    58 is retained only as a first observation. Canonical current custody is
    59 `5c1923413edecb27bde19d388ab3365844e07bc0ba5f0fa9b28672053ef8901f`.
    60

     1 # Revision-3 pre-closure audit findings
     2 
     3 ## Classification
     4 
     5 **Result: NO-GO for revision-3 completion; retained negative assurance result.**
     6 
     7 Revision 3 was frozen before its evidence matrix or decision existed. Hostile review then found
     8 that its arithmetic core was supported but several completion and custody statements were not yet
     9 true. The frozen revision-3 files are not edited to conceal that chronology. Revision 4 must close
    10 or explicitly weaken every item below.
    11 
    12 ## Findings
    13 
    14 1. **No claim-packet custody route.** The KSG checker recognized evidence-path strings but did not
    15    hash or semantically validate the revision-3 claim, obligations, routes, formal boundary,
    16    implementation note, correction ledger, or failures. Deleting or changing those files could
    17    leave the arithmetic, catalog, and release routes green.
    18 2. **Stale revision index.** `revision-index.md` named revision 2 as active and contained no
    19    revision-3 hashes. Git retention alone did not satisfy revision 3's stronger D1 wording.
    20 3. **Formal bound overstatement.** The revision-3 prose attributed the exact `-D <= T <= D` bound
    21    to formal routes, while the frozen Lean source proved algebra/index consequences but no
    22    harmonic monotonicity or bound theorem, and the three Z3 files had no premises sufficient to
    23    derive harmonic-value bounds.
    24 4. **Historical Lean custody gap.** The only live untracked Lean path was edited after a
    25    revision-2 document had pinned its earlier SHA-256. Until identical revision-2 bytes were
    26    retained separately, Git history did not preserve the pinned source.
    27 5. **Mutation inventory drift.** The retained first result was 85 mutations, followed by observed
    28    91, 99, 129, and 133-state runs while routes were still moving. None was a final revision-3
    29    inventory, and no final result may be selected retrospectively from those runs.
    30 6. **Ambiguous W3 wording.** The 150/354 ordinary-left nonzero observation uses the selected
    31    Neumaier prefix table. With a naive prefix the corresponding count is 121/354. An unqualified
    32    “ordinary left association” therefore failed to identify the prefix path.
    33 7. **Endpoint split was trusted by consumers.** The generator recomputed the 240 exhaustive and
    34    114 stress endpoint rows, but the Python checker and Rust corpus test initially asserted split
    35    metadata rather than deriving both counts from fixture rows.
    36 8. **Ordered W1 production gap.** The external integration test independently derived row 5's
    37    ordered counts `(4,1)`, but the public local scalar is source-symmetric. No production-private
    38    diagnostic assertion initially proved that the implementation itself produced that order.
    39 9. **Release/catalog projections were incomplete.** Revision fields were checked, but unrelated
    40    fields in affected release objects, top-level release metadata, protected catalog methods,
    41    catalog references, and catalog metadata were not all exact negative controls. The 20 catalog
    42    bindings were also hard-coded without deriving the 21-node reverse dependency closure and its
    43    single non-numerical shared-config exclusion.
    44 10. **Evidence-path existence was not enforced.** Catalog validation required path strings but did
    45     not require their targets to be regular repository files.
    46 11. **KSG-only phase isolation was not machine enforced.** The ambient worktree also contained
    47     later PID2 exact-sum and I_min work. A green KSG source route did not prove that a proposed Git
    48     tree excluded those changes, including unrelated hunks in shared `stats.rs` and parallel-oracle
    49     files.
    50 12. **Audience evidence remained stale.** Generated `METHODS.md`, release-scope Markdown,
    51     review-evidence records, dispositions, assurance registry, and software-identity hashes still
    52     referred to earlier KSG evidence or pre-migration bytes.
    53 
    54 ## Required revision-4 response
    55 
    56 Revision 4 must preserve this failure, retain the exact historical Lean bytes, prove only the
    57 formal statements actually encoded (including any rational-to-real bridge it claims), add
    58 hash-first and semantic claim custody with hash-rebased semantic mutants, recompute endpoint split
    59 counts in both consumers, bind ordered W1 diagnostics in production, freeze the selected-prefix
    60 150/354 result in executable routes, use full-object release/catalog projections and derived
    61 dependency closure, require evidence targets to exist, and validate an isolated Git candidate
    62 derived from the declared parent. Generated audience and identity artifacts must be rebuilt only

    65 No item here changes the KSG estimator definition or the Makkeh--Gutknecht--Wibral PID functional.

     1 use crate::error::{PidError, PidResult};
     2 use crate::resource::{try_vec_filled, ResourceBudget};
     3 
     4 /// Mean of finite values, scaled before summation so avoidable intermediate overflow does not
     5 /// reject a representable result.
     6 pub(crate) fn finite_mean(values: &[f64], context: &'static str) -> PidResult<f64> {
     7     let (scale, mean_scaled) = scaled_mean_parts(values, context)?;
     8     let mean = scale * mean_scaled;
     9     if mean.is_finite() {
    10         Ok(mean)
    11     } else {
    12         Err(PidError::NumericalInstability { context })
    13     }
    14 }
    15 
    16 /// Population mean and standard deviation of finite values.
    17 ///
    18 /// Both passes operate after division by `max(abs(x))`. This matters for data such as
    19 /// `[0, f64::MAX]`: its mean and standard deviation are both finite, even though forming either
    20 /// the raw sum or the raw variance overflows.
    21 pub(crate) fn finite_mean_std_population(
    22     values: &[f64],
    23     context: &'static str,
    24 ) -> PidResult<(f64, f64)> {
    25     finite_mean_std(values, 0, context)
    26 }
    27 
    28 /// Sample mean and standard deviation (Bessel-corrected, denominator `n-1`).
    29 #[cfg(feature = "experimental-pipelines")]
    30 pub(crate) fn finite_mean_std_sample(
    31     values: &[f64],
    32     context: &'static str,
    33 ) -> PidResult<(f64, f64)> {
    34     finite_mean_std(values, 1, context)
    35 }
    36 
    37 fn finite_mean_std(values: &[f64], ddof: usize, context: &'static str) -> PidResult<(f64, f64)> {
    38     if values.len() <= ddof {
    39         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
    40             context,
    41             message: "not enough values for the requested variance degrees of freedom",
    42         });
    43     }
    44     let (scale, mean_scaled) = scaled_mean_parts(values, context)?;
    45     if scale == 0.0 {
    46         return Ok((0.0, 0.0));
    47     }
    48 
    49     let sum_squared_scaled = compensated_sum(values.iter().map(|value| {
    50         let deviation = value / scale - mean_scaled;
    51         deviation * deviation
    52     }));
    53     let variance_scaled = sum_squared_scaled / (values.len() - ddof) as f64;
    54     // For |x| <= scale, the exact population variance is <= scale^2. Permit a small floating
    55     // tolerance, then restore that mathematical bound so `scale * sqrt(var)` cannot spuriously
    56     // overflow at `f64::MAX`.
    57     let variance_bound = values.len() as f64 / (values.len() - ddof) as f64;
    58     let tolerance = 64.0 * f64::EPSILON * variance_bound;
    59     if !variance_scaled.is_finite()
    60         || variance_scaled < -tolerance
    61         || variance_scaled > variance_bound + tolerance
    62     {
    63         return Err(PidError::NumericalInstability { context });
    64     }
    65     let std = scale * variance_scaled.clamp(0.0, variance_bound).sqrt();
    66     let mean = scale * mean_scaled;
    67     if mean.is_finite() && std.is_finite() {
    68         Ok((mean, std))
    69     } else {
    70         Err(PidError::NumericalInstability { context })
    71     }
    72 }
    73 
    74 fn scaled_mean_parts(values: &[f64], context: &'static str) -> PidResult<(f64, f64)> {
    75     if values.is_empty() {
    76         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
    77             context,
    78             message: "need at least one value",
    79         });
    80     }
    81     if values.iter().any(|value| !value.is_finite()) {
    82         return Err(PidError::NonFiniteInput { context });
    83     }
    84     let scale = values
    85         .iter()
    86         .fold(0.0_f64, |current, value| current.max(value.abs()));
    87     if scale == 0.0 {
    88         return Ok((0.0, 0.0));
    89     }
    90 
    91     let raw_mean_scaled =
    92         compensated_sum(values.iter().map(|value| value / scale)) / values.len() as f64;
    93     let tolerance = 64.0 * f64::EPSILON;
    94     if !raw_mean_scaled.is_finite() || raw_mean_scaled.abs() > 1.0 + tolerance {
    95         return Err(PidError::NumericalInstability { context });
    96     }
    97     Ok((scale, raw_mean_scaled.clamp(-1.0, 1.0)))
    98 }
    99 
   100 /// Deterministic Neumaier compensated summation in iterator order.
   101 ///
   102 /// Callers remain responsible for ensuring that the mathematical sum is representable. Keeping
   103 /// this helper crate-visible lets estimators share one stable accumulation policy without exposing
   104 /// it as part of the public API.
   105 pub(crate) fn compensated_sum(values: impl IntoIterator<Item = f64>) -> f64 {
   106     let mut sum = 0.0;
   107     let mut correction = 0.0;
   108     for value in values {
   109         let next = sum + value;
   110         if sum.abs() >= value.abs() {
   111             correction += (sum - next) + value;
   112         } else {
   113             correction += (value - next) + sum;
   114         }
   115         sum = next;
   116     }
   117     sum + correction
   118 }
   119 
   120 /// Digamma / psi function ψ(x).
   121 ///
   122 /// Implementation: recurrence to shift into a "large x" regime + asymptotic expansion.
   123 ///
   124 /// Units: natural logarithm (nats).
   125 #[cfg(any(feature = "experimental-heuristics", test))]
   126 pub(crate) fn digamma(x: f64) -> f64 {
   127     debug_assert!(x.is_finite());
   128     debug_assert!(x > 0.0);
   129 
   130     let mut x = x;
   131     let mut acc = 0.0;
   132 
   133     // Recurrence for small x: ψ(x) = ψ(x+1) - 1/x
   134     // Shifting to 8 keeps the truncated Bernoulli expansion comfortably below 1e-13 error at
   135     // the small integer arguments retained by the non-cancelling research heuristic and
   136     // regression tests. Stopping at 6 leaves a ~9.3e-13 bias in psi(1).
   137     while x < 8.0 {
   138         acc -= 1.0 / x;
   139         x += 1.0;
   140     }
   141 
   142     // Asymptotic series (Stirling-like).
   143     // ψ(x) ≈ ln(x) - 1/(2x) - 1/(12x²) + 1/(120x⁴) - 1/(252x⁶) + 1/(240x⁸) - 1/(132x¹⁰) + 691/(32760x¹²) - ...
   144     let inv = 1.0 / x;
   145     let inv2 = inv * inv;
   146     let inv4 = inv2 * inv2;
   147     let inv6 = inv4 * inv2;
   148     let inv8 = inv4 * inv4;
   149     let inv10 = inv8 * inv2;
   150     let inv12 = inv6 * inv6;
   151 
   152     acc + x.ln() - 0.5 * inv - (1.0 / 12.0) * inv2 + (1.0 / 120.0) * inv4 - (1.0 / 252.0) * inv6
   153         + (1.0 / 240.0) * inv8
   154         - (1.0 / 132.0) * inv10
   155         + (691.0 / 32760.0) * inv12
   156 }
   157 
   158 /// Precompute ψ(i) for integer `i` in `0..=n` (with index 0 unused).
   159 ///
   160 /// The non-cancelling research heuristic calls `digamma` repeatedly at small positive integer
   161 /// count arguments. This helper preserves that general special-function path; coefficient-
   162 /// cancelling KSG and shared-exclusions paths use [`shifted_harmonic_table`] instead.
   163 #[cfg(feature = "experimental-heuristics")]
   164 pub(crate) fn digamma_int_table(n: usize) -> PidResult<Vec<f64>> {
   165     let len = n.checked_add(1).ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   166         operation: "digamma_int_table",
   167     })?;
   168     let mut out = try_vec_filled("digamma_int_table", len, 0.0f64, ResourceBudget::default())?;
   169     for (i, v) in out.iter_mut().enumerate().skip(1) {
   170         *v = digamma(i as f64);
   171     }
   172     Ok(out)
   173 }
   174 
   175 /// Precompute the positive-integer part of digamma without Euler's constant.
   176 ///
   177 /// The returned table is indexed by the positive digamma argument and stores
   178 /// `table[m] = H_(m-1)`, with index zero unused. Prefixes use deterministic Neumaier
   179 /// compensation. This has the same `n + 1` binary64 allocation shape as `digamma_int_table`,
   180 /// but it is only definition-preserving where all Euler-constant coefficients cancel.
   181 pub(crate) fn shifted_harmonic_table(n: usize) -> PidResult<Vec<f64>> {
   182     let len = n.checked_add(1).ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   183         operation: "shifted_harmonic_table",
   184     })?;
   185     let mut out = try_vec_filled(
   186         "shifted_harmonic_table",
   187         len,
   188         0.0_f64,
   189         ResourceBudget::default(),
   190     )?;
   191     let mut sum = 0.0_f64;
   192     let mut correction = 0.0_f64;
   193     // `argument` is the mathematical digamma argument and the table index; retaining that exact
   194     // correspondence makes the audited off-by-one contract visible at the write site.
   195     #[expect(
   196         clippy::needless_range_loop,
   197         reason = "the loop index is the audited digamma argument and table index"
   198     )]
   199     for argument in 2..=n {
   200         let value = 1.0 / (argument - 1) as f64;
   201         let next = sum + value;
   202         if sum.abs() >= value.abs() {
   203             correction += (sum - next) + value;
   204         } else {
   205             correction += (value - next) + sum;
   206         }
   207         sum = next;
   208         out[argument] = sum + correction;
   209     }
   210     Ok(out)
   211 }
   212 
   213 /// Evaluate a cancelling four-integer-digamma KSG term from shifted harmonic prefixes.
   214 ///
   215 /// For positive arguments satisfying `k <= x,y <= n`, this evaluates
   216 /// `psi(k) + psi(n) - psi(x) - psi(y)` as the source-symmetric range expression
   217 /// `(H_(n-1) - H_(max(x,y)-1)) - (H_(min(x,y)-1) - H_(k-1))`.
   218 /// KSG's exclusive counts therefore pass `x = nx + 1`, while inclusive shared-exclusions counts
   219 /// pass their count directly. The exact-real identity is universal on that integer domain; the
   220 /// binary64 prefix evaluation is not a universal correct-rounding guarantee.
   221 #[inline]
   222 pub(crate) fn ksg_local_harmonic_term(
   223     shifted_harmonics: &[f64],
   224     k: usize,
   225     n: usize,
   226     x: usize,
   227     y: usize,
   228 ) -> f64 {
   229     debug_assert!(k > 0);
   230     debug_assert!(k <= x && x <= n);
   231     debug_assert!(k <= y && y <= n);
   232     debug_assert!(n < shifted_harmonics.len());
   233     let lower = x.min(y);
   234     let upper = x.max(y);
   235     (shifted_harmonics[n] - shifted_harmonics[upper])
   236         - (shifted_harmonics[lower] - shifted_harmonics[k])
   237 }

   319     fn harmonic(n: usize) -> f64 {
   320         // H_n = sum_{k=1..n} 1/k, with H_0 = 0.
   321         (1..=n).map(|k| 1.0 / (k as f64)).sum()
   322     }
   323 
   324     #[test]
   325     fn digamma_matches_known_integer_values() {
   326         // ψ(1) = -γ
   327         let psi1 = digamma(1.0);
   328         assert!((psi1 + EULER_GAMMA).abs() < 1e-12, "psi(1)={psi1}");
   329 
   330         // ψ(n) = H_{n-1} - γ for integer n>=2
   331         for n in 2..=25usize {
   332             let psi_n = digamma(n as f64);
   333             let expected = harmonic(n - 1) - EULER_GAMMA;
   334             assert!(
   335                 (psi_n - expected).abs() < 5e-14,
   336                 "psi({n})={psi_n} expected={expected}"
   337             );
   338         }
   339     }

   342     fn digamma_recurrence_holds() {
   343         // ψ(x+1) = ψ(x) + 1/x
   344         let x = 3.7;
   345         let lhs = digamma(x + 1.0);
   346         let rhs = digamma(x) + 1.0 / x;
   347         assert!((lhs - rhs).abs() < 5e-13, "lhs={lhs} rhs={rhs}");
   348     }

   488         let mut naive_total = 0.0_f64;
   489         for (argument, prefix) in naive_shifted_harmonics.iter_mut().enumerate().skip(2) {
   490             naive_total += 1.0 / (argument - 1) as f64;

   493         let mut maximum_rounded_reference_error = 0.0_f64;
   494         let mut first_maximum = None;
   495         let mut maximum_error_ties = 0_usize;
   496         let mut swap_bit_asymmetries = 0_usize;
   497         let mut endpoint_positive_zero_outputs = 0_usize;
   498         let mut endpoint_direct_left_nonzeros = 0_usize;
   499         let mut endpoint_direct_left_negative_zeros = 0_usize;
   500         let mut naive_prefix_direct_left_nonzeros = 0_usize;
   501         let mut naive_prefix_direct_left_negative_zeros = 0_usize;

   515                 case.x_count + 1,
   516                 case.y_count + 1,
   517             );
   518             let source_swapped = ksg_local_harmonic_term(
   519                 &shifted_harmonics,
   520                 case.k,
   521                 case.sample_count,
   522                 case.y_count + 1,
   523                 case.x_count + 1,
   524             );
   525             let low = case.k - 1;
   526             let high = case.sample_count - 1;
   527             if (case.x_count, case.y_count) == (low, high)
   528                 || (case.x_count, case.y_count) == (high, low)
   529             {
   530                 assert_eq!(
   531                     actual.to_bits(),
   532                     0.0_f64.to_bits(),
   533                     "endpoint cancellation must follow the selected positive-zero path"
   534                 );
   535                 endpoint_positive_zero_outputs += 1;
   536                 let direct_left = ((shifted_harmonics[case.k]
   537                     + shifted_harmonics[case.sample_count])
   538                     - shifted_harmonics[case.x_count + 1])
   539                     - shifted_harmonics[case.y_count + 1];
   540                 endpoint_direct_left_nonzeros += usize::from(direct_left != 0.0);
   541                 endpoint_direct_left_negative_zeros +=
   542                     usize::from(direct_left.to_bits() == (-0.0_f64).to_bits());
   543                 let naive_direct_left = ((naive_shifted_harmonics[case.k]
   544                     + naive_shifted_harmonics[case.sample_count])
   545                     - naive_shifted_harmonics[case.x_count + 1])
   546                     - naive_shifted_harmonics[case.y_count + 1];
   547                 naive_prefix_direct_left_nonzeros += usize::from(naive_direct_left != 0.0);
   548                 naive_prefix_direct_left_negative_zeros +=
   549                     usize::from(naive_direct_left.to_bits() == (-0.0_f64).to_bits());
   550             }
   551             swap_bit_asymmetries += usize::from(actual.to_bits() != source_swapped.to_bits());
   552             let error = if actual.is_finite() && rounded_reference.is_finite() {
   553                 (actual - rounded_reference).abs()
   554             } else {
   555                 f64::INFINITY
   556             };
   557             if error > maximum_rounded_reference_error {
   558                 maximum_rounded_reference_error = error;
   559                 first_maximum = Some((
   560                     case.sample_count,
   561                     case.k,
   562                     case.x_count,
   563                     case.y_count,
   564                     actual,
   565                     rounded_reference,
   566                 ));
   567                 maximum_error_ties = 1;
   568             } else if error == maximum_rounded_reference_error {
   569                 maximum_error_ties += 1;
   570             }

     1 //! Kraskov–Stögbauer–Grassberger algorithm-1 mutual-information estimation.
     2 //!
     3 //! # Method provenance and availability
     4 //!
     5 //! **PAPER-DEFINED CORE / PROJECT-DEFINED REPORT CONTRACT.** The neighbor-count estimator is
     6 //! KSG1 (Kraskov, Stögbauer, and Grassberger, 2004). The default stable surface is report-first and
     7 //! adds pid-rs support declarations, observed-sample diagnostics, provenance, resource limits, and
     8 //! cancellation. Those contracts do not broaden the estimator's published domain.
     9 //!
    10 //! Method catalog: mutual-information.ksg1-report
    11 //!
    12 //! **PROJECT-DEFINED SENSITIVITY DIAGNOSTICS.** The k and sample-size trajectories repeatedly
    13 //! evaluate the report-first estimator under explicit resource bounds. They expose finite-sample
    14 //! sensitivity and are not convergence proofs.
    15 //!
    16 //! Method catalog: mutual-information.ksg1-sensitivity-trajectories
    17 //!
    18 //! **PROJECT-DEFINED CONFIGURATION CONTRACT.** The `experimental-continuous` namespace
    19 //! re-exports the same typed KSG settings for composed estimators. The paper supplies `k` and the
    20 //! KSG1 neighborhood/count convention. `tie_epsilon`, signed-estimate presentation,
    21 //! `support_contract`, the shared Rust type, and its namespace placement are pid-rs API contracts
    22 //! rather than a second estimator or a separately published method.
    23 //!
    24 //! Method catalog: mutual-information.ksg1-shared-config
    25 //!
    26 //! **PAPER-DEFINED CORE / RESEARCH API.** Raw scalar and local-term functions use the same KSG
    27 //! numerical
    28 //! core but omit the stable report contract. They require `experimental-continuous`; local terms
    29 //! are dependent, per-observation contributions and are not independent observations.

    31 //! Method catalog: mutual-information.ksg1-raw

    33 //! **PAPER-DERIVED RESEARCH ADAPTATION.** Hyperbolic report and trajectory entry points substitute

   111 impl NnBackend {
   112     #[inline]
   113     fn use_tree(self, metric: KernelMetric, n: usize, joint_dims: usize) -> bool {
   114         match self {
   115             NnBackend::Brute => false,
   116             NnBackend::KdTree => metric.is_chebyshev() && joint_dims > 0,
   117             NnBackend::Auto => {
   118                 metric.is_chebyshev() && kdtree_applicable(Metric::Chebyshev, n, joint_dims)
   119             }
   120         }
   121     }

   126     let available = std::thread::available_parallelism().map_or(1, std::num::NonZero::get);
   127     #[cfg(not(feature = "parallel"))]

   129     requested.min(n_tasks).min(available).max(1)

   164     pub support_contract: SupportContract,

   308 /// Owned, structurally checked caller-declared provenance attached to a [`KsgMiReport`].
   309 ///
   310 /// Provenance describes operations and assumptions that cannot be reconstructed from the numeric
   311 /// sample. Both required descriptions must contain at least one non-whitespace character. An
   312 /// embedding-training description is optional for ordinary Chebyshev KSG, but is required by
   313 /// `hyperbolic_ksg_mi_report` for the experimental Lorentz-hyperbolic path.
   314 #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
   315 pub struct KsgProvenance {
   316     preprocessing_description: String,
   317     observation_model_description: String,
   318     embedding_training_provenance: Option<String>,
   319     sampling_model_description: Option<String>,
   320     training_split_id: Option<String>,
   321     evaluation_split_id: Option<String>,
   322 }
   323 
   324 impl KsgProvenance {
   325     /// Construct owned caller-declared provenance, checking only that required text is nonempty.
   326     pub fn new(
   327         preprocessing_description: impl AsRef<str>,
   328         observation_model_description: impl AsRef<str>,
   329         embedding_training_provenance: Option<&str>,
   330     ) -> PidResult<Self> {
   331         let preprocessing_description = preprocessing_description.as_ref();
   332         if preprocessing_description.trim().is_empty() {
   333             return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   334                 context: "KsgProvenance::new",
   335                 message: "preprocessing_description must be nonempty",
   336             });
   337         }
   338         let observation_model_description = observation_model_description.as_ref();
   339         if observation_model_description.trim().is_empty() {
   340             return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   341                 context: "KsgProvenance::new",
   342                 message: "observation_model_description must be nonempty",
   343             });
   344         }
   345         for value in [preprocessing_description, observation_model_description] {
   346             validate_optional_provenance_text(
   347                 "KsgProvenance::new",
   348                 "provenance field is too long",
   349                 Some(value),
   350             )?;
   351         }
   352         if embedding_training_provenance.is_some_and(|description| description.trim().is_empty()) {
   353             return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   354                 context: "KsgProvenance::new",
   355                 message: "embedding_training_provenance must be nonempty when provided",
   356             });
   357         }
   358         validate_optional_provenance_text(
   359             "KsgProvenance::new",
   360             "embedding_training_provenance is too long",
   361             embedding_training_provenance,
   362         )?;
   363         let preprocessing_description =
   364             try_provenance_string("KsgProvenance::new", preprocessing_description)?;
   365         let observation_model_description =
   366             try_provenance_string("KsgProvenance::new", observation_model_description)?;
   367         let embedding_training_provenance = embedding_training_provenance
   368             .map(|value| try_provenance_string("KsgProvenance::new", value))
   369             .transpose()?;
   370         Ok(Self {
   371             preprocessing_description,
   372             observation_model_description,
   373             embedding_training_provenance,
   374             sampling_model_description: None,
   375             training_split_id: None,
   376             evaluation_split_id: None,
   377         })
   378     }
   379 
   380     /// Attach the declared sampling/dependence model and train/evaluation split identities.
   381     pub fn with_sampling_model_and_splits(
   382         mut self,
   383         sampling_model_description: impl AsRef<str>,
   384         training_split_id: Option<&str>,
   385         evaluation_split_id: Option<&str>,
   386     ) -> PidResult<Self> {
   387         let sampling_model_description = sampling_model_description.as_ref();
   388         if sampling_model_description.trim().is_empty() {
   389             return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   390                 context: "KsgProvenance::with_sampling_model_and_splits",
   391                 message: "sampling_model_description must be nonempty",
   392             });
   393         }
   394         for value in [
   395             Some(sampling_model_description),
   396             training_split_id,
   397             evaluation_split_id,
   398         ] {
   399             validate_optional_provenance_text(
   400                 "KsgProvenance::with_sampling_model_and_splits",
   401                 "provenance field is too long",
   402                 value,
   403             )?;
   404         }
   405         self.sampling_model_description = Some(try_provenance_string(
   406             "KsgProvenance::with_sampling_model_and_splits",
   407             sampling_model_description,
   408         )?);
   409         self.training_split_id = training_split_id
   410             .map(|value| {
   411                 try_provenance_string("KsgProvenance::with_sampling_model_and_splits", value)
   412             })
   413             .transpose()?;
   414         self.evaluation_split_id = evaluation_split_id
   415             .map(|value| {
   416                 try_provenance_string("KsgProvenance::with_sampling_model_and_splits", value)
   417             })
   418             .transpose()?;
   419         Ok(self)
   420     }
   421 
   422     pub fn preprocessing_description(&self) -> &str {
   423         &self.preprocessing_description
   424     }
   425 
   426     pub fn observation_model_description(&self) -> &str {
   427         &self.observation_model_description
   428     }
   429 
   430     pub fn embedding_training_provenance(&self) -> Option<&str> {
   431         self.embedding_training_provenance.as_deref()
   432     }
   433 
   434     pub fn sampling_model_description(&self) -> Option<&str> {
   435         self.sampling_model_description.as_deref()
   436     }
   437 
   438     pub fn training_split_id(&self) -> Option<&str> {
   439         self.training_split_id.as_deref()
   440     }
   441 
   442     pub fn evaluation_split_id(&self) -> Option<&str> {
   443         self.evaluation_split_id.as_deref()
   444     }
   445 
   446     fn heap_bytes(&self) -> PidResult<u128> {
   447         [
   448             Some(self.preprocessing_description.as_str()),
   449             Some(self.observation_model_description.as_str()),
   450             self.embedding_training_provenance.as_deref(),
   451             self.sampling_model_description.as_deref(),
   452             self.training_split_id.as_deref(),
   453             self.evaluation_split_id.as_deref(),
   454         ]
   455         .into_iter()
   456         .flatten()
   457         .try_fold(0u128, |total, value| {
   458             total
   459                 .checked_add(value.len() as u128)
   460                 .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   461                     operation: "KsgProvenance",
   462                 })
   463         })
   464     }
   465 
   466     /// Fallibly copy all owned provenance text under an aggregate resource budget.
   467     pub fn try_clone_with_budget(&self, budget: ResourceBudget) -> PidResult<Self> {
   468         budget.check(
   469             "KsgProvenance report copy",
   470             ResourceEstimate {
   471                 estimated_bytes: self.heap_bytes()?,
   472                 pairwise_distances: 0,
   473                 operations_hint: 6,
   474             },
   475         )?;
   476         Ok(Self {
   477             preprocessing_description: try_provenance_string(
   478                 "KsgProvenance report copy",
   479                 &self.preprocessing_description,
   480             )?,
   481             observation_model_description: try_provenance_string(
   482                 "KsgProvenance report copy",
   483                 &self.observation_model_description,
   484             )?,
   485             embedding_training_provenance: self
   486                 .embedding_training_provenance
   487                 .as_deref()
   488                 .map(|value| try_provenance_string("KsgProvenance report copy", value))
   489                 .transpose()?,
   490             sampling_model_description: self
   491                 .sampling_model_description
   492                 .as_deref()
   493                 .map(|value| try_provenance_string("KsgProvenance report copy", value))
   494                 .transpose()?,
   495             training_split_id: self
   496                 .training_split_id
   497                 .as_deref()
   498                 .map(|value| try_provenance_string("KsgProvenance report copy", value))
   499                 .transpose()?,
   500             evaluation_split_id: self
   501                 .evaluation_split_id
   502                 .as_deref()
   503                 .map(|value| try_provenance_string("KsgProvenance report copy", value))
   504                 .transpose()?,
   505         })
   506     }
   507 }
   508 
   509 fn validate_optional_provenance_text(
   510     context: &'static str,
   511     message: &'static str,
   512     value: Option<&str>,
   513 ) -> PidResult<()> {
   514     const MAX_PROVENANCE_BYTES: usize = 16 * 1024;
   515     if value.is_some_and(|value| value.len() > MAX_PROVENANCE_BYTES) {
   516         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig { context, message });
   517     }
   518     Ok(())
   519 }
   520 
   521 fn try_provenance_string(context: &'static str, value: &str) -> PidResult<String> {
   522     let mut owned = String::new();
   523     owned
   524         .try_reserve_exact(value.len())
   525         .map_err(|_| PidError::AllocationFailed {
   526             operation: context,
   527             requested_bytes: value.len() as u128,
   528         })?;
   529     owned.push_str(value);
   530     Ok(owned)
   531 }

   776 /// Estimate KSG mutual information and return scoped interpretation metadata and diagnostics.
   777 ///
   778 /// This is the canonical stable entry point. Scalar and local-term paths are available only in
   779 /// the default-off experimental namespace because a publication-facing number must remain coupled
   780 /// to its assumptions, provenance, diagnostics, revision identity, and resource preflight.

   867 fn ksg_mi_report_with_kernel_and_cancellation(
   868     x: MatRef<'_>,
   869     y: MatRef<'_>,
   870     cfg: &KernelKsgConfig,
   871     provenance: &KsgProvenance,
   872     resource_budget: ResourceBudget,
   873     cancellation: &CancellationToken,
   874 ) -> PidResult<KsgReportComputation> {
   875     // Preserve shape/config/support error precedence before the report-only provenance gate.
   876     validate_ksg_pair_structure_with_kernel("ksg_mi_report", x, y, cfg)?;
   877     #[cfg(feature = "experimental-hyperbolic")]
   878     if matches!(cfg.kernel_metric, KernelMetric::HyperbolicLorentz { .. })
   879         && provenance.embedding_training_provenance().is_none()
   880     {
   881         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   882             context: "ksg_mi_report",
   883             message: "Lorentz-hyperbolic reports require embedding_training_provenance",
   884         });
   885     }
   886 
   887     let effective_threads = effective_thread_count(resource_budget.max_threads, x.nrows());
   888     let resource_estimate = ksg_report_resource_estimate(x, y, provenance, effective_threads)?;
   889     resource_budget.check("ksg_mi_report", resource_estimate)?;
   890     cancellation.check("ksg_mi_report", 0, x.nrows())?;
   891     let use_tree = NnBackend::Auto.use_tree(cfg.kernel_metric, x.nrows(), x.ncols() + y.ncols());
   892     let local = with_thread_budget(effective_threads, || {
   893         ksg_local_diagnostics_backend_with_kernel_and_cancellation(
   894             x,
   895             y,
   896             cfg,
   897             NnBackend::Auto,
   898             resource_budget,
   899             cancellation,
   900         )
   901     })?;
   902     let signed_estimate =
   903         compensated_sum(local.iter().map(|value| value.term_nats)) / local.len() as f64;
   904     let estimate_nats = match cfg.negative_handling {
   905         NegativeHandling::Allow => signed_estimate,
   906         NegativeHandling::ClampToZero => signed_estimate.max(0.0),
   907     };
   908     #[cfg(feature = "experimental-continuous")]
   909     let local_terms_nats = {
   910         let mut terms =
   911             try_vec_with_capacity("ksg retained local terms", local.len(), resource_budget)?;
   912         terms.extend(local.iter().map(|value| value.term_nats));
   913         terms
   914     };
   915     let local_diagnostics =
   916         summarize_local_diagnostics_with_cancellation(&local, resource_budget, cancellation)?;
   917     let x_diagnostics = continuous_input_diagnostics_with_kernel_and_cancellation(
   918         x,
   919         cfg.k,
   920         cfg.kernel_metric,
   921         resource_budget,
   922         cancellation,
   923     )?;
   924     let y_diagnostics = continuous_input_diagnostics_with_kernel_and_cancellation(
   925         y,
   926         cfg.k,
   927         cfg.kernel_metric,
   928         resource_budget,
   929         cancellation,
   930     )?;
   931     let joint_shells = continuous_joint_shell_diagnostics_with_kernel_and_cancellation(
   932         &[x, y],
   933         cfg.k,
   934         cfg.kernel_metric,
   935         resource_budget,
   936         cancellation,
   937     )?;
   938 
   939     let mut warnings = try_vec_with_capacity("ksg warnings", 3, resource_budget)?;
   940     warnings.push(KsgReportWarning::SampleDiagnosticsCannotProveSupport);
   941     if has_shell_pathology(x_diagnostics.marginal_shells)
   942         || has_shell_pathology(y_diagnostics.marginal_shells)
   943     {
   944         warnings.push(KsgReportWarning::MarginalNeighborShellPathology);
   945     }
   946 
   947     let (method_status, x_hyperbolic_dimension, y_hyperbolic_dimension) = match cfg.kernel_metric {
   948         KernelMetric::Chebyshev => (KsgMethodStatus::RestrictedDomain, None, None),
   949         #[cfg(feature = "experimental-hyperbolic")]
   950         KernelMetric::HyperbolicLorentz { .. } => (
   951             KsgMethodStatus::Experimental,
   952             Some(x.ncols() - 1),
   953             Some(y.ncols() - 1),
   954         ),
   955     };
   956 
   957     let scientific_status = match method_status {
   958         KsgMethodStatus::RestrictedDomain => ScientificStatus::ConditionalContinuous,
   959         KsgMethodStatus::Experimental => ScientificStatus::ResearchOnly,
   960     };
   961     let metric_identity = match cfg.kernel_metric {
   962         KernelMetric::Chebyshev => "chebyshev-max-product",
   963         #[cfg(feature = "experimental-hyperbolic")]
   964         KernelMetric::HyperbolicLorentz { .. } => "lorentz-hyperboloid-curvature-minus-one",
   965     };
   966     let estimand = EstimandIdentity {
   967         family: "kraskov-stoegbauer-grassberger-mutual-information",
   968         definition_revision: "ksg1-product-small-ball-v1",
   969         estimator_revision: "strict-unique-shell-integer-harmonic-report-v4",
   970         units: InformationUnit::Nats,
   971         metric: metric_identity,
   972         source_gauge: None,
   973     };
   974     let assumption_ledger = ksg_assumption_ledger(provenance, joint_shells, resource_budget)?;
   975     let mut input_hashes_sha256 =
   976         try_vec_with_capacity("ksg report input hashes", 2, resource_budget)?;
   977     input_hashes_sha256.extend([
   978         hash_matrix_with_cancellation(x, cancellation)?,
   979         hash_matrix_with_cancellation(y, cancellation)?,
   980     ]);
   981     let provenance_hashes = ProvenanceHashes {
   982         input_hashes_sha256,
   983         preprocessing_hash_sha256: hash_text(provenance.preprocessing_description()),
   984         observation_model_hash_sha256: hash_text(provenance.observation_model_description()),
   985         training_split_id: provenance
   986             .training_split_id()
   987             .map(|value| try_provenance_string("ksg report split identity", value))
   988             .transpose()?,
   989         evaluation_split_id: provenance
   990             .evaluation_split_id()
   991             .map(|value| try_provenance_string("ksg report split identity", value))
   992             .transpose()?,
   993     };
   994     let mut report_warnings = try_vec_with_capacity("ksg report warnings", 8, resource_budget)?;
   995     report_warnings.push(WarningCode::DiagnosticsDoNotProvePopulationAssumptions);
   996     if matches!(
   997         cfg.support_contract,
   998         SupportContract::AssumeRegularFullDimensional {
   999             boundary: BoundaryModel::Unknown,
  1000             ..
  1001         }
  1002     ) {
  1003         report_warnings.push(WarningCode::BoundaryModelUnknown);
  1004     }
  1005     if provenance.sampling_model_description.is_none() {
  1006         report_warnings.push(WarningCode::DependenceDiagnosticsNotEvaluated);
  1007     }
  1008     report_warnings.extend([
  1009         WarningCode::KTrajectoryNotEvaluated,
  1010         WarningCode::SampleSizeTrajectoryNotEvaluated,
  1011         WarningCode::TransformationSensitivityNotEvaluated,
  1012         WarningCode::ObservationNoiseSensitivityNotEvaluated,
  1013     ]);
  1014     if scientific_status == ScientificStatus::ResearchOnly {
  1015         report_warnings.push(WarningCode::ExperimentalEstimator);
  1016     }
  1017 
  1018     let report = KsgMiReport {
  1019         estimate_nats,
  1020         signed_estimate_nats: signed_estimate,
  1021         n_samples: x.nrows(),
  1022         k: cfg.k,
  1023         metric: cfg.metric,
  1024         negative_handling: cfg.negative_handling,
  1025         support_contract: cfg.support_contract,
  1026         method_status,
  1027         scientific_status,
  1028         estimand,
  1029         assumption_ledger,
  1030         provenance: provenance.try_clone_with_budget(resource_budget)?,
  1031         provenance_hashes,
  1032         x_diagnostics,
  1033         y_diagnostics,
  1034         joint_shells,
  1035         local_diagnostics,
  1036         neighbor_backend: if use_tree {
  1037             KsgNeighborBackend::ExactChebyshevKdTree
  1038         } else {
  1039             KsgNeighborBackend::BruteForce
  1040         },
  1041         resource_estimate,
  1042         resource_budget,
  1043         geometry_model: KsgGeometryModel::AmbientChebyshev,
  1044         curvature: None,
  1045         x_hyperbolic_dimension,
  1046         y_hyperbolic_dimension,
  1047         warnings,
  1048         report_warnings,
  1049     };
  1050     cancellation.check("ksg_mi_report", x.nrows(), x.nrows())?;
  1051     Ok(KsgReportComputation {
  1052         report,
  1053         #[cfg(feature = "experimental-continuous")]
  1054         local_terms_nats,
  1055     })
  1056 }
  1057

  1071 pub fn hyperbolic_ksg_mi_report_with_budget(

  1073     y: MatRef<'_>,
  1074     cfg: &HyperbolicKsgConfig,
  1075     provenance: &KsgProvenance,
  1076     resource_budget: ResourceBudget,
  1077 ) -> PidResult<HyperbolicKsgMiReport> {

  1079     hyperbolic_ksg_mi_report_with_budget_and_cancellation(

  1089 /// Compute a Lorentz-model KSG report with resource and cancellation controls.
  1090 #[cfg(feature = "experimental-hyperbolic")]
  1091 pub fn hyperbolic_ksg_mi_report_with_budget_and_cancellation(
  1092     x: MatRef<'_>,
  1093     y: MatRef<'_>,
  1094     cfg: &HyperbolicKsgConfig,
  1095     provenance: &KsgProvenance,
  1096     resource_budget: ResourceBudget,
  1097     cancellation: &CancellationToken,
  1098 ) -> PidResult<HyperbolicKsgMiReport> {
  1099     let kernel_config = cfg.kernel_config();
  1100     // Preserve structural/support and provenance error precedence before resource preflight.
  1101     validate_ksg_pair_structure_with_kernel("ksg_mi_report", x, y, &kernel_config)?;
  1102     validate_hyperbolic_ksg_provenance(provenance)?;
  1103     let resource_estimate = hyperbolic_ksg_report_resource_estimate(
  1104         x,
  1105         y,
  1106         provenance,
  1107         effective_thread_count(resource_budget.max_threads, x.nrows()),
  1108     )?;
  1109     resource_budget.check("hyperbolic_ksg_mi_report", resource_estimate)?;
  1110     let report = ksg_mi_report_with_kernel_and_cancellation(
  1111         x,
  1112         y,
  1113         &kernel_config,
  1114         provenance,
  1115         resource_budget,
  1116         cancellation,
  1117     )?
  1118     .report;
  1119 
  1120     let warning_count = report
  1121         .warnings
  1122         .len()
  1123         .checked_add(1)
  1124         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
  1125             operation: "hyperbolic_ksg_mi_report",
  1126         })?;
  1127     if warning_count > HYPERBOLIC_KSG_WARNING_CAPACITY {
  1128         return Err(PidError::SizeOverflow {
  1129             operation: "hyperbolic_ksg_mi_report",
  1130         });
  1131     }
  1132     let mut warnings = try_vec_with_capacity(
  1133         "hyperbolic KSG warnings",
  1134         HYPERBOLIC_KSG_WARNING_CAPACITY,
  1135         resource_budget,
  1136     )?;
  1137     for warning in report.warnings {
  1138         warnings.push(match warning {
  1139             KsgReportWarning::SampleDiagnosticsCannotProveSupport => {
  1140                 HyperbolicKsgReportWarning::SampleDiagnosticsCannotProveSupport
  1141             }
  1142             KsgReportWarning::MarginalNeighborShellPathology => {
  1143                 HyperbolicKsgReportWarning::MarginalNeighborShellPathology
  1144             }
  1145         });
  1146     }
  1147     warnings.push(HyperbolicKsgReportWarning::ConsistencyNotEstablished);
  1148 
  1149     Ok(HyperbolicKsgMiReport {
  1150         estimate_nats: report.estimate_nats,
  1151         signed_estimate_nats: report.signed_estimate_nats,
  1152         n_samples: report.n_samples,
  1153         k: report.k,
  1154         metric: cfg.metric,
  1155         negative_handling: report.negative_handling,
  1156         support_contract: HyperbolicSupportContract::AssumeSmoothManifold,
  1157         method_status: report.method_status,
  1158         scientific_status: report.scientific_status,
  1159         estimand: report.estimand,
  1160         assumption_ledger: report.assumption_ledger,
  1161         provenance: report.provenance,
  1162         provenance_hashes: report.provenance_hashes,
  1163         x_diagnostics: report.x_diagnostics,
  1164         y_diagnostics: report.y_diagnostics,
  1165         joint_shells: report.joint_shells,
  1166         local_diagnostics: report.local_diagnostics,
  1167         neighbor_backend: report.neighbor_backend,
  1168         resource_estimate,
  1169         resource_budget: report.resource_budget,
  1170         geometry_model: HyperbolicKsgGeometryModel::LorentzHyperboloid,
  1171         curvature: cfg.metric.curvature,
  1172         x_hyperbolic_dimension: x.ncols() - 1,
  1173         y_hyperbolic_dimension: y.ncols() - 1,
  1174         warnings,
  1175         report_warnings: report.report_warnings,
  1176     })
  1177 }

  1179 #[cfg(feature = "experimental-hyperbolic")]
  1180 fn validate_hyperbolic_ksg_provenance(provenance: &KsgProvenance) -> PidResult<()> {
  1181     if provenance.embedding_training_provenance().is_none() {
  1182         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
  1183             context: "ksg_mi_report",
  1184             message: "Lorentz-hyperbolic reports require embedding_training_provenance",
  1185         });
  1186     }
  1187     Ok(())
  1188 }
