    88 pub enum IsxMethod {
    89     /// KSG-style kNN estimator for continuous shared-exclusions redundancy described by:
    90     /// Ehrlich et al. (2024), Phys. Rev. E 110, 014115 (arXiv:2311.06373v3).
    91     ///
    92     /// Implements the bivariate redundancy `I^sx_∩(S1,S2;T)` via the KSG-style estimator
    93     /// (Appendix H, Algorithms 3–6) under the L∞/Chebyshev metric:
    94     ///
    95     /// I^sx_∩ = ψ(k) + ψ(n) - ⟨ ψ(n_α(i)) + ψ(n_T(i)) ⟩_i
    96     ///
    97     /// where:
    98     /// - ε_i is the kNN radius in the joint (source-disjunction, target) space,
    99     /// - n_α(i) counts neighbors in the *source disjunction* within ε_i,
   100     /// - n_T(i) counts neighbors in target space within ε_i.
   101     ///
   102     /// Note: This is the default method for `IsxConfig`.
   103     EhrlichKsg,
   104     /// Experimental heuristic sketch estimator.
   105     ///
   106     /// Provided as an explicit, clearly-labelled research baseline only. Synthetic checks can
   107     /// characterize bounded cases but do not make it an estimator of the cited functional.
   108     #[cfg(feature = "experimental-heuristics")]
   109     HeuristicSketch,
   110     /// Approximate shared-exclusions redundancy by taking the samplewise minimum
   111     /// of KSG local MI terms for (S1,T) and (S2,T), then averaging.
   112     #[cfg(feature = "experimental-heuristics")]
   113     LocalMinKsg,
   114     /// Experimental **unweighted inclusion–exclusion heuristic** over pointwise KSG local-MI
   115     /// terms:
   116     ///
   117     /// r(s1,s2;t) = log( exp(i(s1;t)) + exp(i(s2;t)) - exp(i(s1,s2;t)) )
   118     ///
   119     /// **This is NOT the shared-exclusions disjunction identity.** The true forms are:
   120     /// - discrete (Makkeh–Gutknecht–Wibral 2021):
   121     ///   `i^sx = log[(p(s1)e^{i1} + p(s2)e^{i2} − p(s1,s2)e^{i12}) / (p(s1)+p(s2)−p(s1,s2))]`
   122     ///   (probability-weighted);
   123     /// - Ehrlich et al.'s continuous functional under its declared relative source gauge
   124     ///   (2024, Def. 2; evaluated for matched standard-normal marginals and a common partition in
   125     ///   `tests/sxpid_gaussian_oracle.rs`):
   126     ///   `i^sx = log[w1·e^{i1} + w2·e^{i2}]` with density weights
   127     ///   `w_a = f_{S_a}(s_a) / (f_{S1}(s1) + f_{S2}(s2))` and **no** joint term (the discrete
   128     ///   joint-term weight `p(s1,s2)` vanishes under that refining-partition construction).
   129     ///
   130     /// This variant sets all weights to 1 and retains a full-weight joint term, so it estimates
   131     /// a *different* functional and does not converge to `I^sx_∩` as estimation error → 0; its
   132     /// log argument can also be non-positive (surfacing as `NumericalInstability`), whereas the
   133     /// true `i^sx` argument `P(∪|t)/P(∪)` is always positive. Baseline/diagnostic use only.
   134     #[cfg(feature = "experimental-heuristics")]
   135     DisjunctionFromLocalMi,
   136 }

   156 /// Caller-declared source gauges, preprocessing, sampling, and split provenance for ISX.
   157 #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
   158 #[non_exhaustive]
   159 pub struct IsxProvenance {
   160     source1_gauge_description: String,
   161     source2_gauge_description: String,
   162     target_preprocessing_description: String,
   163     observation_model_description: String,
   164     sampling_model_description: Option<String>,
   165     training_split_id: Option<String>,
   166     evaluation_split_id: Option<String>,
   167 }
   168 
   169 impl IsxProvenance {
   170     pub fn new(
   171         source1_gauge_description: impl AsRef<str>,
   172         source2_gauge_description: impl AsRef<str>,
   173         target_preprocessing_description: impl AsRef<str>,
   174         observation_model_description: impl AsRef<str>,
   175         sampling_model_description: impl AsRef<str>,
   176         training_split_id: Option<String>,
   177         evaluation_split_id: Option<String>,
   178     ) -> PidResult<Self> {
   179         let source1_gauge_description = source1_gauge_description.as_ref();
   180         let source2_gauge_description = source2_gauge_description.as_ref();
   181         let target_preprocessing_description = target_preprocessing_description.as_ref();
   182         let observation_model_description = observation_model_description.as_ref();
   183         let sampling_model_description = sampling_model_description.as_ref();
   184         for value in [
   185             source1_gauge_description,
   186             source2_gauge_description,
   187             target_preprocessing_description,
   188             observation_model_description,
   189             sampling_model_description,
   190         ] {
   191             if value.trim().is_empty() || value.len() > 16 * 1024 {
   192                 return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   193                     context: "IsxProvenance::new",
   194                     message: "provenance descriptions must be nonempty and at most 16 KiB",
   195                 });
   196             }
   197         }
   198         for value in [training_split_id.as_deref(), evaluation_split_id.as_deref()]
   199             .into_iter()
   200             .flatten()
   201         {
   202             if value.is_empty() || value.len() > 16 * 1024 {
   203                 return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   204                     context: "IsxProvenance::new",
   205                     message: "split identifiers must be nonempty and at most 16 KiB",
   206                 });
   207             }
   208         }
   209         Ok(Self {
   210             source1_gauge_description: try_owned_text(
   211                 "IsxProvenance::new source1 gauge",
   212                 source1_gauge_description,
   213             )?,
   214             source2_gauge_description: try_owned_text(
   215                 "IsxProvenance::new source2 gauge",
   216                 source2_gauge_description,
   217             )?,
   218             target_preprocessing_description: try_owned_text(
   219                 "IsxProvenance::new target preprocessing",
   220                 target_preprocessing_description,
   221             )?,
   222             observation_model_description: try_owned_text(
   223                 "IsxProvenance::new observation model",
   224                 observation_model_description,
   225             )?,
   226             sampling_model_description: Some(try_owned_text(
   227                 "IsxProvenance::new sampling model",
   228                 sampling_model_description,
   229             )?),
   230             training_split_id,
   231             evaluation_split_id,
   232         })
   233     }

   263     fn heap_bytes(&self) -> PidResult<u128> {
   264         [
   265             Some(self.source1_gauge_description.as_str()),
   266             Some(self.source2_gauge_description.as_str()),
   267             Some(self.target_preprocessing_description.as_str()),
   268             Some(self.observation_model_description.as_str()),
   269             self.sampling_model_description.as_deref(),
   270             self.training_split_id.as_deref(),
   271             self.evaluation_split_id.as_deref(),
   272         ]
   273         .into_iter()
   274         .flatten()
   275         .try_fold(0u128, |total, value| {
   276             total
   277                 .checked_add(value.len() as u128)
   278                 .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   279                     operation: "ISX provenance",
   280                 })
   281         })
   282     }
   283 
   284     fn try_clone_for_report(&self) -> PidResult<Self> {
   285         Ok(Self {
   286             source1_gauge_description: try_owned_text(
   287                 "ISX report provenance",
   288                 &self.source1_gauge_description,
   289             )?,
   290             source2_gauge_description: try_owned_text(
   291                 "ISX report provenance",
   292                 &self.source2_gauge_description,
   293             )?,
   294             target_preprocessing_description: try_owned_text(
   295                 "ISX report provenance",
   296                 &self.target_preprocessing_description,
   297             )?,
   298             observation_model_description: try_owned_text(
   299                 "ISX report provenance",
   300                 &self.observation_model_description,
   301             )?,
   302             sampling_model_description: self
   303                 .sampling_model_description
   304                 .as_deref()
   305                 .map(|value| try_owned_text("ISX report provenance", value))
   306                 .transpose()?,
   307             training_split_id: self
   308                 .training_split_id
   309                 .as_deref()
   310                 .map(|value| try_owned_text("ISX report provenance", value))
   311                 .transpose()?,
   312             evaluation_split_id: self
   313                 .evaluation_split_id
   314                 .as_deref()
   315                 .map(|value| try_owned_text("ISX report provenance", value))
   316                 .transpose()?,
   317         })
   318     }

   320     pub(crate) fn new_with_optional_sampling(
   321         source1_gauge_description: &str,
   322         source2_gauge_description: &str,
   323         target_preprocessing_description: &str,
   324         observation_model_description: &str,
   325         sampling_model_description: Option<&str>,
   326         training_split_id: Option<&str>,
   327         evaluation_split_id: Option<&str>,
   328     ) -> PidResult<Self> {
   329         let explicit_sampling = sampling_model_description.unwrap_or("sampling model undeclared");
   330         let mut provenance = Self::new(
   331             source1_gauge_description,
   332             source2_gauge_description,
   333             target_preprocessing_description,
   334             observation_model_description,
   335             explicit_sampling,
   336             training_split_id
   337                 .map(|value| try_owned_text("ISX training split", value))
   338                 .transpose()?,
   339             evaluation_split_id
   340                 .map(|value| try_owned_text("ISX evaluation split", value))
   341                 .transpose()?,
   342         )?;
   343         if sampling_model_description.is_none() {
   344             provenance.sampling_model_description = None;
   345         }
   346         Ok(provenance)
   347     }
   348 }
   349 
   350 fn try_owned_text(operation: &'static str, value: &str) -> PidResult<String> {
   351     let mut owned = String::new();
   352     owned
   353         .try_reserve_exact(value.len())
   354         .map_err(|_| PidError::AllocationFailed {
   355             operation,
   356             requested_bytes: value.len() as u128,
   357         })?;
   358     owned.push_str(value);
   359     Ok(owned)
   360 }

   431 /// Continuous shared-exclusions redundancy I^sx_∩(S1,S2;T).
   432 ///
   433 /// This is the core Wibral-group PID quantity (Makkeh et al. 2021; Ehrlich et al. 2024).
   434 ///
   435 /// By default (`IsxMethod::EhrlichKsg`), this uses the KSG-style kNN construction described by
   436 /// Ehrlich et al. (2024, Appendix H).
   437 ///
   438 /// # Units
   439 /// Returns redundancy in **nats** (natural log).
   440 ///
   441 /// # Important: can be negative
   442 /// `I^sx_∩` is a well-defined functional of the joint distribution, but it is **not guaranteed
   443 /// to be non-negative** under all desiderata (see the PID inconsistency/impossibility results
   444 /// discussed in Makkeh et al. 2021 and Matthias et al. 2025). Do not clamp this value to 0.
   445 ///
   446 /// # Assumptions / failure modes (estimator-level)
   447 /// The default estimator is kNN-based and inherits the usual kNN MI pathologies:
   448 /// - The default support contract is unspecified and fails closed. Callers must explicitly assert
   449 ///   full-dimensional absolute continuity for every marginal and joint law used by the estimator.
   450 ///   Exact coordinate ties are incompatible with ideal i.i.d., unrounded continuous-sample
   451 ///   conditions but do not identify their cause or population support; all-unique finite
   452 ///   observations do not prove the model.
   453 /// - Assumes i.i.d. samples from a continuous distribution; trajectory autocorrelation and
   454 ///   quantization/duplicates can collapse the kNN radius or create an ambiguous positive boundary.
   455 ///   Adding jitter changes the estimated distribution and is appropriate only under an explicit
   456 ///   observation-noise model or as a seeded, reported noise-scale sensitivity analysis; otherwise
   457 ///   use a discrete, quantized, or mixed-support estimator.
   458 /// - Can fail in high ambient/intrinsic dimension due to distance concentration.
   459 /// - Can require prohibitive samples under strong dependence (very large true MI).
   460 /// - Exact deterministic continuous maps have infinite MI and fall outside the estimator's domain.
   461 ///   An explicit observation-noise model defines a different noisy population law. Finite MI
   462 ///   remains a separate population assumption. Otherwise, use a suitable discrete or mixed
   463 ///   estimator.
   464 /// - The two source matrices must have the same ambient column count. The small-ball
   465 ///   disjunction compares their raw neighborhood radii, whose asymptotic scaling depends on
   466 ///   dimension; unequal-dimensional source balls therefore do not share the estimator's
   467 ///   required reference scaling. Equal ambient dimensions are only a necessary guard: they do
   468 ///   **not** prove equal intrinsic dimensions, compatible reference measures, or comparable
   469 ///   neighborhood geometry.
   470 /// - Relative source units and preprocessing define the comparison between source neighborhoods
   471 ///   and are part of the continuous `I^sx_∩` estimand. Record the full scheme and do not compare
   472 ///   or pool results across different source scalings/projections.
   473 ///
   474 /// Other `IsxMethod` variants are included only as explicit experimental baselines / cross-checks
   475 /// against the default estimator, and should not be trusted without validation.
   476 pub(crate) fn isx_redundancy(
   477     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   478     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   479     t: MatRef<'_>,
   480     cfg: &IsxConfig,
   481 ) -> PidResult<f64> {
   482     isx_redundancy_with_budget(s1, s2, t, cfg, ResourceBudget::default())
   483 }
   484 
   485 pub(crate) fn isx_redundancy_with_budget(
   486     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   487     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   488     t: MatRef<'_>,
   489     cfg: &IsxConfig,
   490     budget: ResourceBudget,
   491 ) -> PidResult<f64> {
   492     const CONTEXT: &str = "isx_redundancy";
   493     validate_isx_structure(CONTEXT, s1, s2, t, cfg)?;
   494     validate_support_contract(CONTEXT, cfg.support_contract, cfg.metric)?;
   495     let threads = effective_thread_count(budget.max_threads, s1.nrows());
   496     let estimate = isx_resource_estimate_for_method(s1, s2, t, cfg.method, threads)?;
   497     budget.check(CONTEXT, estimate)?;
   498     validate_observed_sample_conditions_with_budget(
   499         CONTEXT,
   500         cfg.support_contract,
   501         &[s1, s2, t],
   502         budget,
   503     )?;
   504     match cfg.method {
   505         IsxMethod::EhrlichKsg => crate::par::with_thread_budget(threads, || {
   506             isx_redundancy_ehrlich_ksg(s1, s2, t, cfg, budget)
   507         }),
   508         #[cfg(feature = "experimental-heuristics")]
   509         IsxMethod::HeuristicSketch => isx_redundancy_heuristic_sketch(s1, s2, t, cfg, budget),
   510         #[cfg(feature = "experimental-heuristics")]
   511         IsxMethod::LocalMinKsg => isx_redundancy_local_min_ksg(s1, s2, t, cfg, budget),
   512         #[cfg(feature = "experimental-heuristics")]
   513         IsxMethod::DisjunctionFromLocalMi => {
   514             isx_redundancy_disjunction_from_local_mi(s1, s2, t, cfg, budget)
   515         }
   516     }
   517 }
   518 
   519 fn validate_isx_structure(
   520     context: &'static str,
   521     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   522     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   523     t: MatRef<'_>,
   524     cfg: &IsxConfig,
   525 ) -> PidResult<()> {
   526     if s1.nrows() != s2.nrows() || s1.nrows() != t.nrows() {
   527         return Err(PidError::RowCountMismatch {
   528             context,
   529             left_rows: s1.nrows(),
   530             right_rows: if s2.nrows() != s1.nrows() {
   531                 s2.nrows()
   532             } else {
   533                 t.nrows()
   534             },
   535         });
   536     }
   537     if s1.ncols() == 0 || s2.ncols() == 0 || t.ncols() == 0 {
   538         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   539             context,
   540             message: "inputs must have at least 1 column",
   541         });
   542     }
   543     if s1.ncols() != s2.ncols() {
   544         return Err(PidError::SourceDimensionMismatch {
   545             context,
   546             left_cols: s1.ncols(),
   547             right_cols: s2.ncols(),
   548         });
   549     }
   550     if cfg.tie_epsilon != 0.0 {
   551         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   552             context,
   553             message: "tie_epsilon must be exactly 0; strict counting uses next-down semantics",
   554         });
   555     }
   556     if cfg.k == 0 || s1.nrows() <= cfg.k {
   557         return Err(PidError::InvalidK {
   558             k: cfg.k,
   559             n_samples: s1.nrows(),
   560         });
   561     }
   562     // The cited continuous `I^sx_∩` construction is restricted to its documented L∞/Chebyshev
   563     // convention. This is metric-domain validation, not a general consistency claim.
   564     // Do not silently “swap the geometry” (e.g., hyperbolic distances) and still call it `I^sx_∩`.
   565     if cfg.method == IsxMethod::EhrlichKsg && cfg.metric != Metric::Chebyshev {
   566         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   567             context,
   568             message:
   569                 "IsxMethod::EhrlichKsg is restricted to the cited Metric::Chebyshev (L∞) convention; other metrics are research-gated",
   570         });
   571     }
   572     Ok(())
   573 }
   574 
   575 /// Compute the cited restricted-domain estimator with neighborhood, scaling, overlap, assumption,
   576 /// provenance, and resource diagnostics attached.
   577 pub fn isx_redundancy_report(
   578     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   579     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   580     target: MatRef<'_>,
   581     config: &IsxConfig,
   582     provenance: &IsxProvenance,
   583     budget: ResourceBudget,
   584 ) -> PidResult<IsxReport> {
   585     Ok(isx_redundancy_report_with_local_terms(s1, s2, target, config, provenance, budget)?.report)
   586 }
   587 
   588 pub(crate) fn isx_redundancy_report_with_local_terms(
   589     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   590     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   591     target: MatRef<'_>,
   592     config: &IsxConfig,
   593     provenance: &IsxProvenance,
   594     budget: ResourceBudget,
   595 ) -> PidResult<IsxReportComputation> {
   596     validate_isx_structure("isx_redundancy_report", s1, s2, target, config)?;
   597     if config.method != IsxMethod::EhrlichKsg {
   598         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   599             context: "isx_redundancy_report",
   600             message: "report-first ISX is defined only for the cited EhrlichKsg construction",
   601         });
   602     }
   603     validate_support_contract(
   604         "isx_redundancy_report",
   605         config.support_contract,
   606         config.metric,
   607     )?;
   608     let threads = effective_thread_count(budget.max_threads, s1.nrows());
   609     let resource_estimate = isx_report_resource_estimate(s1, s2, target, provenance, threads)?;
   610     budget.check("isx_redundancy_report", resource_estimate)?;
   611     validate_observed_sample_conditions_with_budget(
   612         "isx_redundancy_report",
   613         config.support_contract,
   614         &[s1, s2, target],
   615         budget,
   616     )?;
   617     let local = crate::par::with_thread_budget(threads, || {
   618         isx_local_diagnostics(s1, s2, target, config, budget)
   619     })?;
   620     let estimate_nats =
   621         compensated_sum(local.iter().map(|term| term.term_nats)) / local.len() as f64;
   622     let local_diagnostics = summarize_isx_local(&local, budget)?;
   623     let assumption_ledger = isx_assumption_ledger(provenance, budget)?;
   624     let combined_preprocessing = combined_preprocessing_description(provenance)?;
   625     let mut input_hashes_sha256 = try_vec_with_capacity("ISX report input hashes", 3, budget)?;
   626     input_hashes_sha256.extend([hash_matrix(s1), hash_matrix(s2), hash_matrix(target)]);
   627     let mut warnings = try_vec_with_capacity("ISX report warnings", 7, budget)?;
   628     warnings.extend([
   629         WarningCode::DiagnosticsDoNotProvePopulationAssumptions,
   630         WarningCode::ExperimentalEstimator,
   631         WarningCode::KTrajectoryNotEvaluated,
   632         WarningCode::SampleSizeTrajectoryNotEvaluated,
   633         WarningCode::TransformationSensitivityNotEvaluated,
   634         WarningCode::ObservationNoiseSensitivityNotEvaluated,
   635     ]);
   636     if provenance.sampling_model_description.is_none() {
   637         warnings.push(WarningCode::DependenceDiagnosticsNotEvaluated);
   638     }
   639     let report = IsxReport {
   640         estimate_nats,
   641         n_samples: s1.nrows(),
   642         k: config.k,
   643         source_dimensions: [s1.ncols(), s2.ncols()],
   644         target_dimension: target.ncols(),
   645         estimand: EstimandIdentity {
   646             family: "ehrlich-wibral-continuous-isx",
   647             definition_revision: "common-coordinate-radius-v1",
   648             estimator_revision: "strict-unique-shell-integer-harmonic-isx-v4",
   649             units: InformationUnit::Nats,
   650             metric: "chebyshev-common-coordinate-radius",
   651             source_gauge: Some("caller-declared-source-gauges"),
   652         },
   653         scientific_status: ScientificStatus::ExperimentalRestrictedDomain,
   654         support_contract: config.support_contract,
   655         provenance: provenance.try_clone_for_report()?,
   656         provenance_hashes: ProvenanceHashes {
   657             input_hashes_sha256,
   658             preprocessing_hash_sha256: hash_text(&combined_preprocessing),
   659             observation_model_hash_sha256: hash_text(provenance.observation_model_description()),
   660             training_split_id: provenance
   661                 .training_split_id
   662                 .as_deref()
   663                 .map(|value| try_owned_text("ISX report split identity", value))
   664                 .transpose()?,
   665             evaluation_split_id: provenance
   666                 .evaluation_split_id
   667                 .as_deref()
   668                 .map(|value| try_owned_text("ISX report split identity", value))
   669                 .transpose()?,
   670         },
   671         assumption_ledger,
   672         local_diagnostics,
   673         resource_estimate,
   674         resource_budget: budget,
   675         warnings,
   676     };
   677     Ok(IsxReportComputation { report, local })
   678 }
   679 
   680 /// Conservative peak-memory and pairwise-work estimate for report-first two-source ISX.
   681 pub fn isx_resource_estimate(
   682     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   683     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   684     target: MatRef<'_>,
   685 ) -> PidResult<ResourceEstimate> {
   686     isx_resource_estimate_for_threads(
   687         s1,
   688         s2,
   689         target,
   690         effective_thread_count(ResourceBudget::default().max_threads, s1.nrows()),
   691     )
   692 }
   693 
   694 /// ISX preflight including one scratch buffer and explicit stack reservation per active worker.
   695 pub fn isx_resource_estimate_for_threads(
   696     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   697     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   698     target: MatRef<'_>,
   699     max_threads: usize,
   700 ) -> PidResult<ResourceEstimate> {
   701     const OPERATION: &str = "isx_redundancy_report";
   702     if max_threads == 0 {
   703         return Err(PidError::ResourceLimitExceeded {
   704             operation: OPERATION,
   705             resource: "threads",
   706             requested: 1,
   707             limit: 0,
   708         });
   709     }
   710     if s1.nrows() != s2.nrows() || s1.nrows() != target.nrows() {
   711         return Err(PidError::RowCountMismatch {
   712             context: OPERATION,
   713             left_rows: s1.nrows(),
   714             right_rows: if s2.nrows() != s1.nrows() {
   715                 s2.nrows()
   716             } else {
   717                 target.nrows()
   718             },
   719         });
   720     }
   721     let n_usize = s1.nrows();
   722     let n = n_usize as u128;
   723     let dimensions = s1
   724         .ncols()
   725         .checked_add(s2.ncols())
   726         .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(target.ncols()))
   727         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   728             operation: OPERATION,
   729         })? as u128;
   730     let pairs = n
   731         .checked_mul(n.saturating_sub(1))
   732         .and_then(|value| value.checked_div(2))
   733         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   734             operation: OPERATION,
   735         })?;
   736     // The coefficient-cancelling Ehrlich path stores H_(m-1) at positive integer argument m.
   737     // Its table retains the previous n+1 binary64 allocation shape.
   738     let harmonic_bytes = n
   739         .checked_add(1)
   740         .and_then(|value| value.checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<f64>() as u128))
   741         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   742             operation: OPERATION,
   743         })?;
   744     let local_bytes = n
   745         .checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<IsxLocalDiagnostic>() as u128)
   746         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   747             operation: OPERATION,
   748         })?;
   749     let summary_bytes = n
   750         .checked_mul(
   751             6u128
   752                 .checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<f64>() as u128)
   753                 .and_then(|value| {
   754                     value.checked_add(6u128.checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<usize>() as u128)?)
   755                 })
   756                 .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   757                     operation: OPERATION,
   758                 })?,
   759         )
   760         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   761             operation: OPERATION,
   762         })?;
   763     let active_threads = effective_thread_count(max_threads, n_usize) as u128;
   764     let worker_scratch = active_threads
   765         .checked_mul(n.saturating_sub(1))
   766         .and_then(|value| value.checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<DistIsx2>() as u128))
   767         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   768             operation: OPERATION,
   769         })?;
   770     #[cfg(feature = "parallel")]
   771     let worker_stacks = active_threads
   772         .checked_mul(WORKER_STACK_BYTES as u128)
   773         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   774             operation: OPERATION,
   775         })?;
   776     #[cfg(not(feature = "parallel"))]
   777     let worker_stacks = 0;
   778     #[cfg(feature = "parallel")]
   779     let ordered_map_intermediate = n
   780         .checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<PidResult<IsxLocalDiagnostic>>() as u128)
   781         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   782             operation: OPERATION,
   783         })?;
   784     #[cfg(not(feature = "parallel"))]
   785     let ordered_map_intermediate = 0;
   786     let estimator_peak = harmonic_bytes
   787         .checked_add(local_bytes)
   788         .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(ordered_map_intermediate))
   789         .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(worker_scratch))
   790         .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(worker_stacks))
   791         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   792             operation: OPERATION,
   793         })?;
   794     let summary_peak = local_bytes
   795         .checked_add(summary_bytes)
   796         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   797             operation: OPERATION,
   798         })?;
   799     let support_peak = [s1, s2, target]
   800         .into_iter()
   801         .map(continuous_cardinality_estimate)
   802         .try_fold(ResourceEstimate::ZERO, |peak, estimate| {
   803             let estimate = estimate?;
   804             Ok::<_, PidError>(ResourceEstimate {
   805                 estimated_bytes: peak.estimated_bytes.max(estimate.estimated_bytes),
   806                 pairwise_distances: 0,
   807                 operations_hint: peak
   808                     .operations_hint
   809                     .checked_add(estimate.operations_hint)
   810                     .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   811                         operation: OPERATION,
   812                     })?,
   813             })
   814         })?;
   815     let operations_hint = pairs
   816         .checked_mul(2)
   817         .and_then(|value| value.checked_mul(dimensions.checked_add(16)?))
   818         .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(support_peak.operations_hint))
   819         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   820             operation: OPERATION,
   821         })?;
   822     Ok(ResourceEstimate {
   823         estimated_bytes: estimator_peak
   824             .max(summary_peak)
   825             .max(support_peak.estimated_bytes),
   826         pairwise_distances: pairs,
   827         operations_hint,
   828     })
   829 }

   831 /// Complete ISX report preflight including retained provenance, hashes, and metadata.
   832 pub fn isx_report_resource_estimate(
   833     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   834     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   835     target: MatRef<'_>,
   836     provenance: &IsxProvenance,
   837     max_threads: usize,
   838 ) -> PidResult<ResourceEstimate> {
   839     const OPERATION: &str = "isx_redundancy_report";
   840     let mut estimate = isx_resource_estimate_for_threads(s1, s2, target, max_threads)?;
   841     let retained = provenance
   842         .heap_bytes()?
   843         .checked_mul(2)
   844         .and_then(|value| {
   845             value.checked_add(
   846                 provenance.source1_gauge_description.len() as u128
   847                     + provenance.source2_gauge_description.len() as u128
   848                     + provenance.target_preprocessing_description.len() as u128
   849                     + 27,
   850             )
   851         })
   852         .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(std::mem::size_of::<IsxReport>() as u128))
   853         .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(5 * 64))
   854         .and_then(|value| {
   855             value.checked_add(
   856                 12u128.checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<AssumptionLedgerEntry>() as u128)?,
   857             )
   858         })
   859         .and_then(|value| {
   860             value.checked_add(7u128.checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<WarningCode>() as u128)?)
   861         })
   862         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   863             operation: OPERATION,
   864         })?;
   865     estimate.estimated_bytes =
   866         estimate
   867             .estimated_bytes
   868             .checked_add(retained)
   869             .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   870                 operation: OPERATION,
   871             })?;
   872     Ok(estimate)
   873 }
   874 
   875 fn continuous_cardinality_estimate(input: MatRef<'_>) -> PidResult<ResourceEstimate> {
   876     const OPERATION: &str = "ISX support cardinalities";
   877     let n = input.nrows() as u128;
   878     let dimensions = input.ncols() as u128;
   879     let coordinates = n.checked_mul(dimensions).ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   880         operation: OPERATION,
   881     })?;
   882     let log_n = if input.nrows() <= 1 {
   883         1u128
   884     } else {
   885         (usize::BITS - (input.nrows() - 1).leading_zeros()) as u128
   886     };
   887     Ok(ResourceEstimate {
   888         estimated_bytes: coordinates
   889             .checked_mul(2 * std::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u128)
   890             .and_then(|value| {
   891                 value.checked_add(n.checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<Vec<u64>>() as u128)?)
   892             })
   893             .and_then(|value| {
   894                 value.checked_add(
   895                     dimensions.checked_mul(
   896                         std::mem::size_of::<CoordinateCardinalityDiagnostics>() as u128,
   897                     )?,
   898                 )
   899             })
   900             .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   901                 operation: OPERATION,
   902             })?,
   903         pairwise_distances: 0,
   904         operations_hint: coordinates
   905             .checked_mul(log_n)
   906             .and_then(|value| value.checked_mul(2))
   907             .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   908                 operation: OPERATION,
   909             })?,
   910     })
   911 }
   912 
   913 fn combined_preprocessing_description(provenance: &IsxProvenance) -> PidResult<String> {
   914     const PREFIX_BYTES: usize = "source1=; source2=; target=".len();
   915     let capacity = provenance
   916         .source1_gauge_description
   917         .len()
   918         .checked_add(provenance.source2_gauge_description.len())
   919         .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(provenance.target_preprocessing_description.len()))
   920         .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(PREFIX_BYTES))
   921         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   922             operation: "ISX preprocessing provenance",
   923         })?;
   924     let mut combined = String::new();
   925     combined
   926         .try_reserve_exact(capacity)
   927         .map_err(|_| PidError::AllocationFailed {
   928             operation: "ISX preprocessing provenance",
   929             requested_bytes: capacity as u128,
   930         })?;
   931     combined.push_str("source1=");
   932     combined.push_str(&provenance.source1_gauge_description);
   933     combined.push_str("; source2=");
   934     combined.push_str(&provenance.source2_gauge_description);
   935     combined.push_str("; target=");
   936     combined.push_str(&provenance.target_preprocessing_description);
   937     Ok(combined)
   938 }

   940 pub(crate) fn isx_resource_estimate_for_method(
   941     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   942     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   943     target: MatRef<'_>,
   944     method: IsxMethod,
   945     max_threads: usize,
   946 ) -> PidResult<ResourceEstimate> {
   947     let base = isx_resource_estimate_for_threads(s1, s2, target, max_threads)?;
   948     match method {
   949         IsxMethod::EhrlichKsg => Ok(base),
   950         #[cfg(feature = "experimental-heuristics")]
   951         IsxMethod::HeuristicSketch => scale_isx_work(base, target.nrows(), 5, 5),
   952         #[cfg(feature = "experimental-heuristics")]
   953         IsxMethod::LocalMinKsg => scale_isx_work(base, target.nrows(), 2, 2),
   954         #[cfg(feature = "experimental-heuristics")]
   955         IsxMethod::DisjunctionFromLocalMi => scale_isx_work(base, target.nrows(), 3, 3),
   956     }
   957 }
   958 
   959 #[cfg(feature = "experimental-heuristics")]
   960 fn scale_isx_work(
   961     base: ResourceEstimate,
   962     n: usize,
   963     passes: u128,
   964     retained_vectors: u128,
   965 ) -> PidResult<ResourceEstimate> {
   966     const OPERATION: &str = "experimental ISX heuristic";
   967     let retained_bytes = (n as u128)
   968         .checked_mul(retained_vectors)
   969         .and_then(|value| value.checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<f64>() as u128))
   970         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   971             operation: OPERATION,
   972         })?;
   973     Ok(ResourceEstimate {
   974         estimated_bytes: base.estimated_bytes.checked_add(retained_bytes).ok_or(
   975             PidError::SizeOverflow {
   976                 operation: OPERATION,
   977             },
   978         )?,
   979         pairwise_distances: base.pairwise_distances.checked_mul(passes).ok_or(
   980             PidError::SizeOverflow {
   981                 operation: OPERATION,
   982             },
   983         )?,
   984         operations_hint: base.operations_hint.checked_mul(passes).ok_or(
   985             PidError::SizeOverflow {
   986                 operation: OPERATION,
   987             },
   988         )?,
   989     })
   990 }
   991 
   992 fn isx_redundancy_ehrlich_ksg(
   993     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   994     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   995     t: MatRef<'_>,
   996     cfg: &IsxConfig,
   997     budget: ResourceBudget,
   998 ) -> PidResult<f64> {
   999     let terms = isx_local_diagnostics(s1, s2, t, cfg, budget)?;
  1000     let sum = compensated_sum(terms.iter().map(|term| term.term_nats));
  1001     Ok(sum / terms.len() as f64)
  1002 }
  1003 
  1004 fn isx_local_diagnostics(
  1005     s1: MatRef<'_>,
  1006     s2: MatRef<'_>,
  1007     t: MatRef<'_>,
  1008     cfg: &IsxConfig,
  1009     budget: ResourceBudget,
  1010 ) -> PidResult<Vec<IsxLocalDiagnostic>> {
  1011     if s1.nrows() != s2.nrows() || s1.nrows() != t.nrows() {
  1012         return Err(PidError::RowCountMismatch {
  1013             context: "isx_redundancy_ehrlich_ksg",
  1014             left_rows: s1.nrows(),
  1015             // Report the count that actually mismatches s1 (s2's if it differs, else t's).
  1016             right_rows: if s2.nrows() != s1.nrows() {
  1017                 s2.nrows()
  1018             } else {
  1019                 t.nrows()
  1020             },
  1021         });
  1022     }
  1023     let n = s1.nrows();
  1024     let k = cfg.k;
  1025     if k == 0 || n <= k {
  1026         return Err(PidError::InvalidK { k, n_samples: n });
  1027     }
  1028 
  1029     // This is the bivariate antichain α = {{1},{2}}; the disjunction distance in source space is:
  1030     // d_S_disj(i,j) = min( d(S1_i,S1_j), d(S2_i,S2_j) ).
  1031     //
  1032     // With Chebyshev/L∞ and a shared target ball, the joint disjunction distance is:
  1033     // d_ST_disj(i,j) = max( d(T_i,T_j), d_S_disj(i,j) ).
  1034     let shifted_harmonics = shifted_harmonic_table(n)?;
  1035 
  1036     // Per-point local term. Each point is independent and allocates its own scratch, so the
  1037     // closure is pure and can run data-parallel. Results are collected **in index order** and
  1038     // reduced with the same deterministic compensated summation in both paths, so the `parallel`
  1039     // path is bit-for-bit identical to the serial path (see `map_index_ordered`).
  1040     let local = |i: usize| -> PidResult<IsxLocalDiagnostic> {
  1041         let mut scratch = try_vec_with_capacity(
  1042             "ISX per-query distance scratch",
  1043             n.saturating_sub(1),
  1044             budget,
  1045         )?;
  1046         let s1i = s1.row(i);
  1047         let s2i = s2.row(i);
  1048         let ti = t.row(i);
  1049         for j in 0..n {
  1050             if i == j {
  1051                 continue;
  1052             }
  1053             let ds1 = cfg.metric.checked_distance(
  1054                 s1i,
  1055                 s1.row(j),
  1056                 "isx_redundancy_ehrlich_ksg: s1 distance",
  1057             )?;
  1058             let ds2 = cfg.metric.checked_distance(
  1059                 s2i,
  1060                 s2.row(j),
  1061                 "isx_redundancy_ehrlich_ksg: s2 distance",
  1062             )?;
  1063             let dt = cfg.metric.checked_distance(
  1064                 ti,
  1065                 t.row(j),
  1066                 "isx_redundancy_ehrlich_ksg: target distance",
  1067             )?;
  1068             let ds = ds1.min(ds2);
  1069             scratch.push(DistIsx2 {
  1070                 joint: dt.max(ds),
  1071                 dt,
  1072                 ds,
  1073                 ds1,
  1074                 ds2,
  1075             });
  1076         }
  1077 
  1078         let kth = k - 1;
  1079         scratch.select_nth_unstable_by(kth, |a, b| a.joint.total_cmp(&b.joint));
  1080         let eps_raw = scratch[kth].joint;
  1081         if eps_raw == 0.0 {
  1082             return Err(PidError::NumericalInstability {
  1083                 context: "isx_redundancy_ehrlich_ksg: kNN radius is non-positive; jitter changes the estimated distribution and is valid only under an explicit observation-noise model or a reported noise-scale sensitivity analysis; otherwise use a discrete, quantized, or mixed-support estimator",
  1084             });
  1085         }
  1086         let (interior_count, boundary_count) =
  1087             kth_neighbor_shell_counts(scratch.iter().map(|distance| distance.joint), eps_raw);
  1088         validate_kth_neighbor_shell(
  1089             "isx_redundancy_ehrlich_ksg",
  1090             i,
  1091             k,
  1092             eps_raw,
  1093             interior_count,
  1094             boundary_count,
  1095         )?;
  1096         let eps = strict_radius(eps_raw);
  1097 
  1098         // Counts exclude self; the estimator needs counts including self.
  1099         let mut n_t = 1usize;
  1100         let mut n_alpha = 1usize;
  1101         let mut n_s1 = 0usize;
  1102         let mut n_s2 = 0usize;
  1103         let mut n_overlap = 0usize;
  1104         let mut n_s1_half = 0usize;
  1105         let mut n_s2_half = 0usize;
  1106         let mut n_overlap_half = 0usize;
  1107         let half_radius = eps_raw * 0.5;
  1108         for d in &scratch {
  1109             if d.dt <= eps {
  1110                 n_t += 1;
  1111             }
  1112             if d.ds <= eps {
  1113                 n_alpha += 1;
  1114             }
  1115             let in_s1 = d.ds1 <= eps;
  1116             let in_s2 = d.ds2 <= eps;
  1117             n_s1 += usize::from(in_s1);
  1118             n_s2 += usize::from(in_s2);
  1119             n_overlap += usize::from(in_s1 && in_s2);
  1120             let in_s1_half = d.ds1 < half_radius;
  1121             let in_s2_half = d.ds2 < half_radius;
  1122             n_s1_half += usize::from(in_s1_half);
  1123             n_s2_half += usize::from(in_s2_half);
  1124             n_overlap_half += usize::from(in_s1_half && in_s2_half);
  1125         }
  1126 
  1127         Ok(IsxLocalDiagnostic {
  1128             term_nats: ksg_local_harmonic_term(&shifted_harmonics, k, n, n_alpha, n_t),
  1129             joint_radius: eps_raw,
  1130             source_union_count: n_alpha,
  1131             target_count: n_t,
  1132             source1_count: n_s1,
  1133             source2_count: n_s2,
  1134             overlap_count: n_overlap,
  1135             source1_half_count: n_s1_half,
  1136             source2_half_count: n_s2_half,
  1137             overlap_half_count: n_overlap_half,
  1138         })
  1139     };
  1140 
  1141     crate::par::map_index_ordered(n, local)
  1142 }
  1143 
  1144 fn summarize_isx_local(
  1145     local: &[IsxLocalDiagnostic],
  1146     budget: ResourceBudget,
  1147 ) -> PidResult<IsxLocalDiagnosticsSummary> {
  1148     let mut radii = try_vec_with_capacity("ISX radius summary", local.len(), budget)?;
  1149     let mut source_union = try_vec_with_capacity("ISX union-count summary", local.len(), budget)?;
  1150     let mut target = try_vec_with_capacity("ISX target-count summary", local.len(), budget)?;
  1151     let mut source1 = try_vec_with_capacity("ISX source1-count summary", local.len(), budget)?;
  1152     let mut source2 = try_vec_with_capacity("ISX source2-count summary", local.len(), budget)?;
  1153     let mut overlap = try_vec_with_capacity("ISX overlap-count summary", local.len(), budget)?;
  1154     let mut overlap_half =
  1155         try_vec_with_capacity("ISX half-overlap-count summary", local.len(), budget)?;
  1156     let mut overlap_ratio =
  1157         try_vec_with_capacity("ISX overlap-ratio summary", local.len(), budget)?;
  1158     let mut overlap_half_ratio =
  1159         try_vec_with_capacity("ISX half-overlap-ratio summary", local.len(), budget)?;
  1160     let mut source1_slopes =
  1161         try_vec_with_capacity("ISX source1-slope summary", local.len(), budget)?;
  1162     let mut source2_slopes =
  1163         try_vec_with_capacity("ISX source2-slope summary", local.len(), budget)?;
  1164     let mut terms = try_vec_with_capacity("ISX local-term summary", local.len(), budget)?;
  1165     for value in local {
  1166         radii.push(value.joint_radius);
  1167         source_union.push(value.source_union_count);
  1168         target.push(value.target_count);
  1169         source1.push(value.source1_count);
  1170         source2.push(value.source2_count);
  1171         overlap.push(value.overlap_count);
  1172         overlap_half.push(value.overlap_half_count);
  1173         let union = value
  1174             .source1_count
  1175             .checked_add(value.source2_count)
  1176             .and_then(|count| count.checked_sub(value.overlap_count))
  1177             .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
  1178                 operation: "ISX overlap ratio",
  1179             })?;
  1180         let half_union = value
  1181             .source1_half_count
  1182             .checked_add(value.source2_half_count)
  1183             .and_then(|count| count.checked_sub(value.overlap_half_count))
  1184             .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
  1185                 operation: "ISX half-overlap ratio",
  1186             })?;
  1187         overlap_ratio.push(if union == 0 {
  1188             0.0
  1189         } else {
  1190             value.overlap_count as f64 / union as f64
  1191         });
  1192         overlap_half_ratio.push(if half_union == 0 {
  1193             0.0
  1194         } else {
  1195             value.overlap_half_count as f64 / half_union as f64
  1196         });
  1197         if let Some(slope) = scaling_slope(value.source1_count, value.source1_half_count) {
  1198             source1_slopes.push(slope);
  1199         }
  1200         if let Some(slope) = scaling_slope(value.source2_count, value.source2_half_count) {
  1201             source2_slopes.push(slope);
  1202         }
  1203         terms.push(value.term_nats);
  1204     }
  1205     for values in [
  1206         &mut radii,
  1207         &mut overlap_ratio,
  1208         &mut overlap_half_ratio,
  1209         &mut source1_slopes,
  1210         &mut source2_slopes,
  1211         &mut terms,
  1212     ] {
  1213         values.sort_unstable_by(f64::total_cmp);
  1214     }
  1215     for values in [
  1216         &mut source_union,
  1217         &mut target,
  1218         &mut source1,
  1219         &mut source2,
  1220         &mut overlap,
  1221         &mut overlap_half,
  1222     ] {
  1223         values.sort_unstable();
  1224     }
  1225     Ok(IsxLocalDiagnosticsSummary {
  1226         joint_radius: value_quantiles(&radii)?,
  1227         source_union_count: count_quantiles(&source_union)?,
  1228         target_count: count_quantiles(&target)?,
  1229         source1_count: count_quantiles(&source1)?,
  1230         source2_count: count_quantiles(&source2)?,
  1231         overlap_count: count_quantiles(&overlap)?,
  1232         overlap_half_radius_count: count_quantiles(&overlap_half)?,
  1233         overlap_ratio: value_quantiles(&overlap_ratio)?,
  1234         overlap_half_radius_ratio: value_quantiles(&overlap_half_ratio)?,
  1235         source1_scaling_slope: (!source1_slopes.is_empty())
  1236             .then(|| value_quantiles(&source1_slopes))
  1237             .transpose()?,
  1238         source2_scaling_slope: (!source2_slopes.is_empty())
  1239             .then(|| value_quantiles(&source2_slopes))
  1240             .transpose()?,
  1241         undefined_source1_slopes: local.len() - source1_slopes.len(),
  1242         undefined_source2_slopes: local.len() - source2_slopes.len(),
  1243         local_redundancy_nats: value_quantiles(&terms)?,
  1244     })
  1245 }
  1246 
  1247 fn scaling_slope(full_count: usize, half_count: usize) -> Option<f64> {
  1248     (full_count > 0 && half_count > 0 && full_count >= half_count)
  1249         .then(|| (full_count as f64 / half_count as f64).ln() / 2.0_f64.ln())
  1250 }
  1251 
  1252 fn isx_assumption_ledger(
  1253     provenance: &IsxProvenance,
  1254     budget: ResourceBudget,
  1255 ) -> PidResult<Vec<AssumptionLedgerEntry>> {
  1256     let mut ledger = try_vec_with_capacity("ISX assumption ledger", 12, budget)?;
  1257     let separated_splits = provenance.training_split_id.is_some()
  1258         && provenance.evaluation_split_id.is_some()
  1259         && provenance.training_split_id != provenance.evaluation_split_id;
  1260     ledger.extend([
  1261         AssumptionLedgerEntry {
  1262             assumption: Assumption::RegularContinuousOrManifoldLaw,
  1263             state: AssumptionState::AssumptionsDeclared,
  1264             note: "caller assertion; sample diagnostics cannot prove population support",
  1265         },
  1266         AssumptionLedgerEntry {
  1267             assumption: Assumption::FixedLocalDimension,
  1268             state: AssumptionState::WarningPresent,

  1333 #[cfg(feature = "experimental-heuristics")]
  1334 fn isx_redundancy_disjunction_from_local_mi(
  1335     s1: MatRef<'_>,
  1336     s2: MatRef<'_>,
  1337     t: MatRef<'_>,
  1338     cfg: &IsxConfig,
  1339     budget: ResourceBudget,
  1340 ) -> PidResult<f64> {
  1341     if s1.nrows() != s2.nrows() || s1.nrows() != t.nrows() {
  1342         return Err(PidError::RowCountMismatch {
  1343             context: "isx_redundancy_disjunction_from_local_mi",
  1344             left_rows: s1.nrows(),
  1345             // Report the count that actually mismatches s1 (s2's if it differs, else t's).
  1346             right_rows: if s2.nrows() != s1.nrows() {
  1347                 s2.nrows()
  1348             } else {
  1349                 t.nrows()
  1350             },
  1351         });
  1352     }
  1353     let n = s1.nrows();
  1354     let k = cfg.k;
  1355     if k == 0 || n <= k {
  1356         return Err(PidError::InvalidK { k, n_samples: n });
  1357     }
  1358 
  1359     let ksg_cfg = KsgConfig {
  1360         k: cfg.k,
  1361         metric: cfg.metric,
  1362         tie_epsilon: cfg.tie_epsilon,
  1363         negative_handling: NegativeHandling::Allow,
  1364         support_contract: cfg.support_contract,
  1365     };
  1366 
  1367     let mut i1 = ksg_local_mi_terms_with_budget(s1, t, &ksg_cfg, budget)?;
  1368     let i2 = ksg_local_mi_terms_with_budget(s2, t, &ksg_cfg, budget)?;
  1369     let i12 = ksg_local_mi_terms_xblocks_with_budget(&[s1, s2], t, &ksg_cfg, budget)?;
  1370 
  1371     for ((a, &b), &c) in i1.iter_mut().zip(i2.iter()).zip(i12.iter()) {
  1372         // Compute: log(exp(a)+exp(b)-exp(c)) stably.
  1373         let m = (*a).max(b).max(c);
  1374         let sa = (*a - m).exp();
  1375         let sb = (b - m).exp();
  1376         let sc = (c - m).exp();
  1377         let s = sa + sb - sc;
  1378         if !s.is_finite() || s <= 0.0 {
  1379             return Err(PidError::NumericalInstability {
  1380                 context:
  1381                     "isx_redundancy_disjunction_from_local_mi: disjunction argument is non-positive",
  1382             });
  1383         }
  1384         *a = m + s.ln();
  1385     }
  1386 
  1387     Ok(compensated_sum(i1) / (n as f64))
  1388 }

  1437 #[cfg(feature = "experimental-heuristics")]
  1438 fn isx_redundancy_heuristic_sketch(
  1439     s1: MatRef<'_>,
  1440     s2: MatRef<'_>,
  1441     t: MatRef<'_>,
  1442     cfg: &IsxConfig,
  1443     budget: ResourceBudget,
  1444 ) -> PidResult<f64> {
  1445     if s1.nrows() != s2.nrows() || s1.nrows() != t.nrows() {
  1446         return Err(PidError::RowCountMismatch {
  1447             context: "isx_redundancy_heuristic_sketch",
  1448             left_rows: s1.nrows(),
  1449             // Report the count that actually mismatches s1 (s2's if it differs, else t's).
  1450             right_rows: if s2.nrows() != s1.nrows() {
  1451                 s2.nrows()
  1452             } else {
  1453                 t.nrows()
  1454             },
  1455         });
  1456     }
  1457     let n = s1.nrows();
  1458     let k = cfg.k;
  1459     if k == 0 || n <= k {
  1460         return Err(PidError::InvalidK { k, n_samples: n });
  1461     }
  1462 
  1463     // 1) Per-sample kNN radii in the (S1,T) and (S2,T) joint spaces. (Steps 2–3 use only
  1464     //    these two and their samplewise min; no (S1,S2,T) joint radius enters the estimate.)
  1465     let mut eps_s1_t = try_vec_filled("experimental ISX source1 radii", n, 0.0f64, budget)?;
  1466     let mut eps_s2_t = try_vec_filled("experimental ISX source2 radii", n, 0.0f64, budget)?;
  1467 
  1468     let mut scratch = try_vec_with_capacity(
  1469         "experimental ISX distance scratch",
  1470         n.saturating_sub(1),
  1471         budget,
  1472     )?;
  1473     for i in 0..n {
  1474         let e1 =
  1475             kth_neighbor_distance_joint_max_with_scratch(&[s1, t], i, k, cfg.metric, &mut scratch)?;
  1476         if e1 == 0.0 {
  1477             return Err(PidError::NumericalInstability {
  1478                 context: "isx_redundancy_heuristic_sketch: kNN radius collapsed to 0; jitter changes the estimated distribution and is valid only under an explicit observation-noise model or a reported noise-scale sensitivity analysis; otherwise use a discrete, quantized, or mixed-support estimator",
  1479             });
  1480         }
  1481         let (interior_count, boundary_count) =
  1482             kth_neighbor_shell_counts(scratch.iter().copied(), e1);
  1483         validate_kth_neighbor_shell(
  1484             "isx_redundancy_heuristic_sketch (s1,target)",
  1485             i,
  1486             k,
  1487             e1,
  1488             interior_count,
  1489             boundary_count,
  1490         )?;
  1491         eps_s1_t[i] = e1;
  1492 
  1493         let e2 =
  1494             kth_neighbor_distance_joint_max_with_scratch(&[s2, t], i, k, cfg.metric, &mut scratch)?;
  1495         if e2 == 0.0 {
  1496             return Err(PidError::NumericalInstability {
  1497                 context: "isx_redundancy_heuristic_sketch: kNN radius collapsed to 0; jitter changes the estimated distribution and is valid only under an explicit observation-noise model or a reported noise-scale sensitivity analysis; otherwise use a discrete, quantized, or mixed-support estimator",
  1498             });
  1499         }
  1500         let (interior_count, boundary_count) =
  1501             kth_neighbor_shell_counts(scratch.iter().copied(), e2);
  1502         validate_kth_neighbor_shell(
  1503             "isx_redundancy_heuristic_sketch (s2,target)",
  1504             i,
  1505             k,
  1506             e2,
  1507             interior_count,
  1508             boundary_count,
  1509         )?;
  1510         eps_s2_t[i] = e2;
  1511     }
  1512 
  1513     // 2) Count neighbors in target space within the respective radii.
  1514     let mut n_t_s1 = try_vec_filled("experimental ISX source1 target counts", n, 0usize, budget)?;
  1515     let mut n_t_s2 = try_vec_filled("experimental ISX source2 target counts", n, 0usize, budget)?;
  1516     let mut n_t_shared =
  1517         try_vec_filled("experimental ISX shared target counts", n, 0usize, budget)?;
  1518 
  1519     for i in 0..n {
  1520         let e1_raw = eps_s1_t[i];
  1521         let e2_raw = eps_s2_t[i];
  1522 
  1523         let e1 = strict_radius(e1_raw);
  1524         let e2 = strict_radius(e2_raw);
  1525         let es = strict_radius(e1_raw.min(e2_raw));
  1526 
  1527         n_t_s1[i] = count_neighbors_within(t, i, e1, cfg.metric)?;
  1528         n_t_s2[i] = count_neighbors_within(t, i, e2, cfg.metric)?;
  1529         n_t_shared[i] = count_neighbors_within(t, i, es, cfg.metric)?;
  1530     }
  1531 
  1532     // 3) Experimental heuristic sketch estimator.
  1533     let psi_k = digamma(k as f64);
  1534     let psi_n = digamma(n as f64);
  1535     let psi_int = digamma_int_table(n)?;
  1536 
  1537     let avg_term = compensated_sum((0..n).map(|i| {
  1538         let psi_shared = psi_int[n_t_shared[i] + 1];
  1539         let psi_s1 = psi_int[n_t_s1[i] + 1];
  1540         let psi_s2 = psi_int[n_t_s2[i] + 1];
  1541         psi_shared - 0.5 * (psi_s1 + psi_s2)
  1542     })) / (n as f64);
  1543 
  1544     let redundancy = psi_k + psi_n + avg_term;
  1545     Ok(redundancy)
  1546 }

     1 //! Three-source continuous shared-exclusions availability diagnostics and research reproduction.
     2 //!
     3 //! # Method provenance and availability
     4 //!
     5 //! **PROJECT-DEFINED DIAGNOSTIC.** The `experimental-continuous` incomplete API computes only
     6 //! ambient-dimension-compatible redundancy coordinates and exact atom combinations whose required
     7 //! coordinates all exist. It deliberately does not impute a complete 18-atom PID and has no
     8 //! dedicated paper method cited by pid-rs.
     9 //!
    10 //! Method catalog: pid.incomplete-continuous-pid3
    11 //!
    12 //! **PAPER-DEFINED RESEARCH REPRODUCTION.** The full lattice follows the shared-exclusions
    13 //! construction but compares singleton and pair-source neighborhoods with different ambient
    14 //! dimensions. It is available only with `research-mixed-dimension-pid3` plus a runtime opt-in.
    15 //! A finite-union small-ball bound shows that, under positive regular branch expansions in one raw
    16 //! radius, the union has the smallest branch exponent. Branches with larger exponents then have
    17 //! vanishing relative mass. This standard consequence identifies raw-radius branch-weight
    18 //! collapse. It does not prove that the published estimator is inconsistent. Such a claim would
    19 //! also require an estimator-specific result for the random neighbor radius, local uniformity,
    20 //! boundaries, count corrections, and bias. pid-rs supplies no such mixed-dimensional consistency
    21 //! result. Dimension-normalized or probability-content gauges are not implemented because they
    22 //! require a separate derivation and can define a different estimand.
    23 //!
    24 //! Method catalog: pid.mixed-dimension-pid3
    25 //!
    26 //! **NO GENERAL IMPLEMENTATION.** Schick-Poland et al. define a measure-theoretic
    27 //! shared-exclusions PID functional for arbitrary variable types, but pid-rs implements no
    28 //! practical general estimator for atomic, mixed, singular, stratified, or otherwise incompatible
    29 //! support. Barà et al. (2025) provide a restricted nearest-neighbor PID for a discrete target and
    30 //! continuous sources; that method is also not implemented here and does not close the general
    31 //! arbitrary-support gap. Typed support contracts reject or flag incompatible inputs; callers must
    32 //! route them to a matching estimand rather than treating the research PID3 path as a solution.
    33 //!
    34 //! Method catalog: unsupported.mixed-support-continuous-pid

   105 /// A 3-source antichain on indices {0,1,2}, represented as up to 3 conjunction masks.
   106 ///
   107 /// Each mask is a non-zero subset bitmask over {0,1,2}:
   108 /// - bit 0 => source 0
   109 /// - bit 1 => source 1
   110 /// - bit 2 => source 2
   111 ///
   112 /// Example: `{ {0}, {1,2} }` is encoded as `[0b001, 0b110]`.
   113 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
   114 pub struct Antichain3 {
   115     sets: [u8; 3],
   116     len: u8,
   117 }
   118 
   119 impl Antichain3 {
   120     pub fn sets(&self) -> &[u8] {
   121         &self.sets[..(self.len as usize)]
   122     }
   123 
   124     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
   125         self.len as usize
   126     }
   127 
   128     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
   129         self.len == 0
   130     }
   131 
   132     /// Create an antichain from a list of non-empty subset masks over {0,1,2}.
   133     ///
   134     /// The input is canonicalized (sorted ascending) and validated to satisfy the
   135     /// antichain property (no set is a subset of another).
   136     pub fn try_from_sets(sets: &[u8]) -> PidResult<Self> {
   137         if sets.is_empty() || sets.len() > 3 {
   138             return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   139                 context: "Antichain3::try_from_sets",
   140                 message: "need 1..=3 sets",
   141             });
   142         }
   143 
   144         let mut out = [0u8; 3];
   145         for (idx, &m) in sets.iter().enumerate() {
   146             if m == 0 || m > 0b111 {
   147                 return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   148                     context: "Antichain3::try_from_sets",
   149                     message: "set masks must be in 1..=0b111",
   150                 });
   151             }
   152             out[idx] = m;
   153         }
   154 
   155         let len = sets.len();
   156         out[..len].sort_unstable();
   157 
   158         for i in 0..len {
   159             for j in (i + 1)..len {
   160                 let a = out[i];
   161                 let b = out[j];
   162                 if a == b {
   163                     return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   164                         context: "Antichain3::try_from_sets",
   165                         message: "duplicate set mask",
   166                     });
   167                 }
   168                 if (a & b) == a || (a & b) == b {
   169                     return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   170                         context: "Antichain3::try_from_sets",
   171                         message: "not an antichain (subset relation present)",
   172                     });
   173                 }
   174             }
   175         }
   176 
   177         Ok(Self {
   178             sets: out,
   179             len: len as u8,
   180         })
   181     }
   182 }
   183 
   184 impl Ord for Antichain3 {
   185     fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> std::cmp::Ordering {
   186         self.len
   187             .cmp(&other.len)
   188             .then_with(|| self.sets().cmp(other.sets()))
   189     }
   190 }
   191 
   192 impl PartialOrd for Antichain3 {
   193     fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<std::cmp::Ordering> {
   194         Some(self.cmp(other))
   195     }
   196 }

   250 /// Structurally checked, caller-declared provenance for a full `Pid3Report`.
   251 ///
   252 /// Separate source descriptions are required because relative source scaling changes the
   253 /// shared-exclusions estimand. Construction checks only nonemptiness, not truth or adequacy.
   254 #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   255 #[non_exhaustive]
   256 pub struct Pid3Provenance {
   257     source1_preprocessing_description: String,
   258     source2_preprocessing_description: String,
   259     source3_preprocessing_description: String,
   260     target_preprocessing_description: String,
   261     observation_model_description: String,
   262 }
   263 
   264 impl Pid3Provenance {
   265     pub fn new(
   266         source1_preprocessing_description: impl AsRef<str>,
   267         source2_preprocessing_description: impl AsRef<str>,
   268         source3_preprocessing_description: impl AsRef<str>,
   269         target_preprocessing_description: impl AsRef<str>,
   270         observation_model_description: impl AsRef<str>,
   271     ) -> PidResult<Self> {
   272         let source1_preprocessing_description = source1_preprocessing_description.as_ref();
   273         let source2_preprocessing_description = source2_preprocessing_description.as_ref();
   274         let source3_preprocessing_description = source3_preprocessing_description.as_ref();
   275         let target_preprocessing_description = target_preprocessing_description.as_ref();
   276         let observation_model_description = observation_model_description.as_ref();
   277         for (description, message) in [
   278             (
   279                 source1_preprocessing_description,
   280                 "source1_preprocessing_description must be nonempty",
   281             ),
   282             (
   283                 source2_preprocessing_description,
   284                 "source2_preprocessing_description must be nonempty",
   285             ),
   286             (
   287                 source3_preprocessing_description,
   288                 "source3_preprocessing_description must be nonempty",
   289             ),
   290             (
   291                 target_preprocessing_description,
   292                 "target_preprocessing_description must be nonempty",
   293             ),
   294             (
   295                 observation_model_description,
   296                 "observation_model_description must be nonempty",
   297             ),
   298         ] {
   299             if description.trim().is_empty() || description.len() > 16 * 1024 {
   300                 return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   301                     context: "Pid3Provenance::new",
   302                     message: match message {
   303                         "source1_preprocessing_description must be nonempty" => {
   304                             "source1_preprocessing_description must be nonempty and at most 16 KiB"
   305                         }
   306                         "source2_preprocessing_description must be nonempty" => {
   307                             "source2_preprocessing_description must be nonempty and at most 16 KiB"
   308                         }
   309                         "source3_preprocessing_description must be nonempty" => {
   310                             "source3_preprocessing_description must be nonempty and at most 16 KiB"
   311                         }
   312                         "target_preprocessing_description must be nonempty" => {
   313                             "target_preprocessing_description must be nonempty and at most 16 KiB"
   314                         }
   315                         _ => "observation_model_description must be nonempty and at most 16 KiB",
   316                     },
   317                 });
   318             }
   319         }
   320         Ok(Self {
   321             source1_preprocessing_description: try_owned_text(
   322                 "PID3 provenance",
   323                 source1_preprocessing_description,
   324             )?,
   325             source2_preprocessing_description: try_owned_text(
   326                 "PID3 provenance",
   327                 source2_preprocessing_description,
   328             )?,
   329             source3_preprocessing_description: try_owned_text(
   330                 "PID3 provenance",
   331                 source3_preprocessing_description,
   332             )?,
   333             target_preprocessing_description: try_owned_text(
   334                 "PID3 provenance",
   335                 target_preprocessing_description,
   336             )?,
   337             observation_model_description: try_owned_text(
   338                 "PID3 provenance",
   339                 observation_model_description,
   340             )?,
   341         })
   342     }
   343 
   344     pub fn source1_preprocessing_description(&self) -> &str {
   345         &self.source1_preprocessing_description
   346     }
   347 
   348     pub fn source2_preprocessing_description(&self) -> &str {
   349         &self.source2_preprocessing_description
   350     }
   351 
   352     pub fn source3_preprocessing_description(&self) -> &str {
   353         &self.source3_preprocessing_description
   354     }
   355 
   356     pub fn target_preprocessing_description(&self) -> &str {
   357         &self.target_preprocessing_description
   358     }
   359 
   360     pub fn observation_model_description(&self) -> &str {
   361         &self.observation_model_description
   362     }
   363 
   364     fn heap_bytes(&self) -> PidResult<u128> {
   365         [
   366             self.source1_preprocessing_description.as_str(),
   367             self.source2_preprocessing_description.as_str(),
   368             self.source3_preprocessing_description.as_str(),
   369             self.target_preprocessing_description.as_str(),
   370             self.observation_model_description.as_str(),
   371         ]
   372         .into_iter()
   373         .try_fold(0u128, |total, value| {
   374             total
   375                 .checked_add(value.len() as u128)
   376                 .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   377                     operation: "PID3 provenance",
   378                 })
   379         })
   380     }
   381 
   382     fn try_clone_for_report(&self) -> PidResult<Self> {
   383         Ok(Self {
   384             source1_preprocessing_description: try_owned_text(
   385                 "PID3 report provenance",
   386                 &self.source1_preprocessing_description,
   387             )?,
   388             source2_preprocessing_description: try_owned_text(
   389                 "PID3 report provenance",
   390                 &self.source2_preprocessing_description,
   391             )?,
   392             source3_preprocessing_description: try_owned_text(
   393                 "PID3 report provenance",
   394                 &self.source3_preprocessing_description,
   395             )?,
   396             target_preprocessing_description: try_owned_text(
   397                 "PID3 report provenance",
   398                 &self.target_preprocessing_description,
   399             )?,
   400             observation_model_description: try_owned_text(
   401                 "PID3 report provenance",
   402                 &self.observation_model_description,
   403             )?,
   404         })
   405     }
   406 }
   407 
   408 fn try_owned_text(operation: &'static str, value: &str) -> PidResult<String> {
   409     let mut owned = String::new();
   410     owned
   411         .try_reserve_exact(value.len())
   412         .map_err(|_| PidError::AllocationFailed {
   413             operation,
   414             requested_bytes: value.len() as u128,
   415         })?;
   416     owned.push_str(value);
   417     Ok(owned)
   418 }

   531 /// Full 3-source continuous SxPID using shared exclusions (Ehrlich et al. 2024).
   532 ///
   533 /// Computes all 18 PID atoms for three sources by:
   534 /// 1) Estimating `I^sx_∩(T : α)` for every non-empty antichain α on {0,1,2} using the kNN estimator
   535 ///    (a KSG-style construction with disjunction neighborhoods).
   536 /// 2) Applying Möbius inversion on the redundancy lattice to obtain the PID atoms Π^sx(α).
   537 ///
   538 /// Units: nats (natural logarithm).
   539 ///
   540 /// # Experimental mixed-dimensional lattice
   541 ///
   542 /// A full three-source lattice necessarily includes singleton-vs-pair antichains such as
   543 /// `{{S0}, {S1,S2}}`. Their source neighborhoods live in different ambient dimensions, so their
   544 /// raw small-ball radii do not share a dimension-independent reference scaling. Consequently this
   545 /// entry point rejects the default configuration. Set
   546 /// [`Pid3Config::experimental_allow_mixed_dimension_lattice`] to `true` only to reproduce reference
   547 /// fixtures or run explicitly labelled diagnostics. That opt-in does not make the resulting atoms
   548 /// validated mixed-dimensional scientific estimates. Equal dimensions among the three singleton
   549 /// source matrices would not remove the singleton-vs-pair mismatch, nor prove compatible intrinsic
   550 /// dimensions or reference measures.
   551 ///
   552 /// Relative source units/preprocessing are part of the continuous shared-exclusions estimand;
   553 /// record them and do not compare atoms across schemes. Exact deterministic continuous maps have
   554 /// infinite MI and require a justified noise model or a suitable discrete/mixed estimator.
   555 /// Collapsed or ambiguous positive k-th-neighbor shells are rejected rather than assigned a silent
   556 /// tie convention.
   557 #[cfg(feature = "research-mixed-dimension-pid3")]
   558 pub fn pid3_isx(
   559     s0: MatRef<'_>,
   560     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   561     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   562     t: MatRef<'_>,
   563     cfg: &Pid3Config,
   564 ) -> PidResult<Pid3Result> {
   565     pid3_isx_with_budget(s0, s1, s2, t, cfg, ResourceBudget::default())
   566 }
   567 
   568 /// Full research PID3 under an explicit aggregate memory, work, and thread budget.
   569 #[cfg(feature = "research-mixed-dimension-pid3")]
   570 pub fn pid3_isx_with_budget(
   571     s0: MatRef<'_>,
   572     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   573     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   574     t: MatRef<'_>,
   575     cfg: &Pid3Config,
   576     budget: ResourceBudget,
   577 ) -> PidResult<Pid3Result> {
   578     validate_pid3_common("pid3_isx", s0, s1, s2, t, cfg)?;
   579     if !cfg.experimental_allow_mixed_dimension_lattice {
   580         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
   581             context: "pid3_isx",
   582             message: "the full continuous PID3 lattice compares mixed-dimensional singleton and pair source neighborhoods; set experimental_allow_mixed_dimension_lattice=true only for reference reproduction or explicitly labelled diagnostics",
   583         });
   584     }
   585     let n = t.nrows();
   586     validate_support_contract("pid3_isx", cfg.support_contract, cfg.metric)?;
   587     let threads = effective_thread_count(budget.max_threads, n);
   588     let estimate = pid3_resource_estimate_for_threads(s0, s1, s2, t, cfg, threads)?;
   589     budget.check("pid3_isx", estimate)?;
   590     validate_observed_sample_conditions_with_budget(
   591         "pid3_isx",
   592         cfg.support_contract,
   593         &[s0, s1, s2, t],
   594         budget,
   595     )?;
   596     crate::par::with_thread_budget(threads, || {
   597         pid3_isx_prevalidated(s0, s1, s2, t, cfg, budget)
   598     })
   599 }
   600 
   601 #[cfg(feature = "research-mixed-dimension-pid3")]
   602 fn pid3_isx_prevalidated(
   603     s0: MatRef<'_>,
   604     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   605     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   606     t: MatRef<'_>,
   607     cfg: &Pid3Config,
   608     budget: ResourceBudget,
   609 ) -> PidResult<Pid3Result> {
   610     let n = t.nrows();
   611     let k = cfg.k;
   612 
   613     let sources = [
   614         symmetric_distances_with_budget(s0, cfg.metric, budget)?,
   615         symmetric_distances_with_budget(s1, cfg.metric, budget)?,
   616         symmetric_distances_with_budget(s2, cfg.metric, budget)?,
   617     ];
   618     let target = symmetric_distances_with_budget(t, cfg.metric, budget)?;
   619 
   620     let antichains = antichains_3();
   621     let mut redundancies = try_vec_with_capacity("PID3 redundancies", antichains.len(), budget)?;
   622     for &a in antichains {
   623         let val = redundancy_for_antichain("pid3_isx", &sources, &target, a, cfg, budget)?;
   624         redundancies.push(Pid3Redundancy {
   625             antichain: a,
   626             value: val,
   627         });
   628     }
   629 
   630     let atoms = mobius_inversion_atoms(antichains, &redundancies, budget)?;
   631     let mut warnings = try_vec_with_capacity("PID3 warnings", FULL_PID3_WARNINGS.len(), budget)?;
   632     warnings.extend(FULL_PID3_WARNINGS);
   633     Ok(Pid3Result {
   634         n_samples: n,
   635         k,
   636         metric: cfg.metric,
   637         support_contract: cfg.support_contract,
   638         source_ambient_dimensions: [s0.ncols(), s1.ncols(), s2.ncols()],
   639         target_ambient_dimension: t.ncols(),
   640         method_status: Pid3MethodStatus::ExperimentalMixedDimension,
   641         warnings,
   642         redundancies,
   643         atoms,
   644     })
   645 }

   647 /// Compute full experimental PID3 while preserving caller-declared provenance.
   648 ///
   649 /// Provenance construction checks only for nonempty descriptions. Neither that structural check
   650 /// nor this wrapper validates the mixed-dimensional estimator, population support, preprocessing
   651 /// choice, or observation model.
   652 #[cfg(feature = "research-mixed-dimension-pid3")]
   653 pub fn pid3_isx_report(
   654     s0: MatRef<'_>,
   655     s1: MatRef<'_>,

   662 }

   664 /// Full research PID3 report under an explicit aggregate resource budget.
   665 #[cfg(feature = "research-mixed-dimension-pid3")]
   666 pub fn pid3_isx_report_with_budget(
   667     s0: MatRef<'_>,
   668     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   669     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   670     t: MatRef<'_>,
   671     cfg: &Pid3Config,
   672     provenance: &Pid3Provenance,
