   677     let resource_estimate = pid3_report_resource_estimate(s0, s1, s2, t, cfg, provenance, threads)?;
   678     budget.check("pid3_isx_report", resource_estimate)?;
   679     Ok(Pid3Report {
   680         result: pid3_isx_with_budget(s0, s1, s2, t, cfg, budget)?,
   681         provenance: provenance.try_clone_for_report()?,
   682         resource_estimate,
   683         resource_budget: budget,
   684     })
   685 }
   686 
   687 /// Estimate only the ambient-dimension-compatible coordinates of continuous three-source PID.
   688 ///
   689 /// For each redundancy antichain, the ambient dimension of a branch is the sum of the column
   690 /// counts of the sources in that branch. A redundancy is estimated only when all of its branches
   691 /// have the same dimension. Each atom is then expanded exactly as an integer linear combination
   692 /// of redundancy coordinates by Möbius inversion. Its value is returned only when every
   693 /// non-zero-coefficient dependency is available; otherwise `value` is `None` and
   694 /// [`IncompletePid3Atom::unavailable_redundancies`] lists the exact missing coordinates.
   695 ///
   696 /// This is a conservative availability API, not a proof of estimator consistency. Equal ambient
   697 /// dimensions do not establish equal intrinsic dimensions, compatible reference measures, or
   698 /// regular leading-order intersections. The declared support contract remains a caller assertion,
   699 /// and observations with exact ties are conservatively rejected as incompatible with ideal
   700 /// i.i.d., unrounded continuous-sample conditions, without inferring their cause or population
   701 /// support.
   702 ///
   703 /// # Errors
   704 ///
   705 /// Returns an error for incompatible shapes or configuration, an unsupported or unspecified
   706 /// support contract, observations incompatible with ideal continuous-sample conditions, invalid
   707 /// `k`, or degenerate or ambiguous k-nearest-neighbor geometry in any redundancy that is actually
   708 /// estimated.
   709 pub fn incomplete_pid3_diagnostic(
   710     s0: MatRef<'_>,
   711     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   712     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   713     t: MatRef<'_>,
   714     cfg: &Pid3Config,
   715 ) -> PidResult<IncompletePid3Diagnostic> {
   716     incomplete_pid3_diagnostic_with_budget(s0, s1, s2, t, cfg, ResourceBudget::default())
   717 }
   718 
   719 /// Incomplete PID3 diagnostic under an explicit aggregate resource budget.
   720 pub fn incomplete_pid3_diagnostic_with_budget(
   721     s0: MatRef<'_>,
   722     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   723     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   724     t: MatRef<'_>,
   725     cfg: &Pid3Config,
   726     budget: ResourceBudget,
   727 ) -> PidResult<IncompletePid3Diagnostic> {
   728     const CONTEXT: &str = "incomplete_pid3_diagnostic";
   729 
   730     validate_pid3_common(CONTEXT, s0, s1, s2, t, cfg)?;
   731     let n = t.nrows();
   732     validate_support_contract(CONTEXT, cfg.support_contract, cfg.metric)?;
   733     let threads = effective_thread_count(budget.max_threads, n);
   734     let estimate = incomplete_pid3_resource_estimate_for_threads(s0, s1, s2, t, cfg, threads)?;
   735     budget.check(CONTEXT, estimate)?;
   736     validate_observed_sample_conditions_with_budget(
   737         CONTEXT,
   738         cfg.support_contract,
   739         &[s0, s1, s2, t],
   740         budget,
   741     )?;
   742     crate::par::with_thread_budget(threads, || {
   743         incomplete_pid3_prevalidated(s0, s1, s2, t, cfg, budget)
   744     })
   745 }
   746 
   747 fn incomplete_pid3_prevalidated(
   748     s0: MatRef<'_>,
   749     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   750     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   751     t: MatRef<'_>,
   752     cfg: &Pid3Config,
   753     budget: ResourceBudget,
   754 ) -> PidResult<IncompletePid3Diagnostic> {
   755     const CONTEXT: &str = "incomplete_pid3_diagnostic";
   756     let n = t.nrows();
   757     let k = cfg.k;
   758 
   759     let sources = [
   760         symmetric_distances_with_budget(s0, cfg.metric, budget)?,
   761         symmetric_distances_with_budget(s1, cfg.metric, budget)?,
   762         symmetric_distances_with_budget(s2, cfg.metric, budget)?,
   763     ];
   764     let target = symmetric_distances_with_budget(t, cfg.metric, budget)?;
   765     let source_dimensions = [s0.ncols(), s1.ncols(), s2.ncols()];
   766     let antichains = antichains_3();
   767 
   768     let mut redundancies =
   769         try_vec_with_capacity("incomplete PID3 redundancies", antichains.len(), budget)?;
   770     for &antichain in antichains {
   771         let branch_dimensions = antichain_branch_dimensions(antichain, source_dimensions, budget)?;
   772         let compatible = branch_dimensions
   773             .windows(2)
   774             .all(|dimensions| dimensions[0] == dimensions[1]);
   775         let value = if compatible {
   776             Some(redundancy_for_antichain(
   777                 CONTEXT, &sources, &target, antichain, cfg, budget,
   778             )?)
   779         } else {
   780             None
   781         };
   782         redundancies.push(IncompletePid3Redundancy {
   783             antichain,
   784             branch_dimensions,
   785             value,
   786         });
   787     }
   788 
   789     let atoms = partial_mobius_inversion_atoms(antichains, &redundancies, budget)?;
   790     let mut warnings = try_vec_with_capacity(
   791         "incomplete PID3 warnings",
   792         PARTIAL_PID3_WARNINGS.len(),
   793         budget,
   794     )?;
   795     warnings.extend(PARTIAL_PID3_WARNINGS);
   796     Ok(IncompletePid3Diagnostic {
   797         n_samples: n,
   798         k,
   799         metric: cfg.metric,
   800         support_contract: cfg.support_contract,
   801         source_ambient_dimensions: source_dimensions,
   802         target_ambient_dimension: t.ncols(),
   803         status: IncompletePid3Status::AmbientDimensionCompatibleButUnvalidated,
   804         warnings,
   805         redundancies,
   806         atoms,
   807     })
   808 }

   810 /// Compute the conservative partial PID3 surface while preserving caller-declared provenance.
   811 ///
   812 /// Provenance is checked only for nonempty descriptions and does not establish estimator
   813 /// consistency, support, preprocessing validity, or an observation model.
   814 pub fn incomplete_pid3_report(
   815     s0: MatRef<'_>,
   816     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   817     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   818     t: MatRef<'_>,
   819     cfg: &Pid3Config,
   820     provenance: &Pid3Provenance,
   821 ) -> PidResult<IncompletePid3Report> {
   822     incomplete_pid3_report_with_budget(s0, s1, s2, t, cfg, provenance, ResourceBudget::default())
   823 }
   824 
   825 /// Incomplete PID3 report under an explicit aggregate resource budget.
   826 pub fn incomplete_pid3_report_with_budget(
   827     s0: MatRef<'_>,
   828     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   829     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   830     t: MatRef<'_>,
   831     cfg: &Pid3Config,
   832     provenance: &Pid3Provenance,
   833     budget: ResourceBudget,
   834 ) -> PidResult<IncompletePid3Report> {
   835     validate_pid3_common("incomplete_pid3_diagnostic", s0, s1, s2, t, cfg)?;
   836     let threads = effective_thread_count(budget.max_threads, t.nrows());
   837     let resource_estimate =
   838         incomplete_pid3_report_resource_estimate(s0, s1, s2, t, cfg, provenance, threads)?;
   839     budget.check("incomplete_pid3_report", resource_estimate)?;
   840     Ok(IncompletePid3Report {
   841         result: incomplete_pid3_diagnostic_with_budget(s0, s1, s2, t, cfg, budget)?,
   842         provenance: provenance.try_clone_for_report()?,
   843         resource_estimate,
   844         resource_budget: budget,
   845     })
   846 }

   848 /// Conservative preflight for the complete four-matrix continuous PID3 working set.
   849 #[cfg(feature = "research-mixed-dimension-pid3")]
   850 pub fn pid3_resource_estimate(
   851     s0: MatRef<'_>,
   852     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   853     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   854     t: MatRef<'_>,
   855     cfg: &Pid3Config,
   856 ) -> PidResult<ResourceEstimate> {
   857     pid3_resource_estimate_for_threads(
   858         s0,
   859         s1,
   860         s2,
   861         t,
   862         cfg,
   863         effective_thread_count(ResourceBudget::default().max_threads, t.nrows()),
   864     )
   865 }
   866 
   867 /// PID3 preflight including simultaneous matrices and per-worker stack/scratch reservations.
   868 #[cfg_attr(
   869     not(feature = "research-mixed-dimension-pid3"),
   870     expect(
   871         unreachable_pub,
   872         reason = "shared implementation is public only when the full research surface is enabled"
   873     )
   874 )]
   875 pub fn pid3_resource_estimate_for_threads(
   876     s0: MatRef<'_>,
   877     s1: MatRef<'_>,
   878     s2: MatRef<'_>,
   879     t: MatRef<'_>,
   880     _cfg: &Pid3Config,
   881     max_threads: usize,
   882 ) -> PidResult<ResourceEstimate> {
   883     const OPERATION: &str = "continuous PID3";
   884     if max_threads == 0 {
   885         return Err(PidError::ResourceLimitExceeded {
   886             operation: OPERATION,
   887             resource: "threads",
   888             requested: 1,
   889             limit: 0,
   890         });
   891     }
   892     if s0.nrows() != s1.nrows() || s0.nrows() != s2.nrows() || s0.nrows() != t.nrows() {
   893         return Err(PidError::RowCountMismatch {
   894             context: OPERATION,
   895             left_rows: s0.nrows(),
   896             right_rows: if s1.nrows() != s0.nrows() {
   897                 s1.nrows()
   898             } else if s2.nrows() != s0.nrows() {
   899                 s2.nrows()
   900             } else {
   901                 t.nrows()
   902             },
   903         });
   904     }
   905     let n_usize = t.nrows();
   906     let n = n_usize as u128;
   907     let pairs = n
   908         .checked_mul(n.saturating_sub(1))
   909         .and_then(|value| value.checked_div(2))
   910         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   911             operation: OPERATION,
   912         })?;
   913     let dimensions = [s0, s1, s2, t]
   914         .into_iter()
   915         .try_fold(0u128, |total, input| {
   916             total
   917                 .checked_add(input.ncols() as u128)
   918                 .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   919                     operation: OPERATION,
   920                 })
   921         })?;
   922     let matrix_bytes = pairs
   923         .checked_mul(4)
   924         .and_then(|value| value.checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<f64>() as u128))
   925         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   926             operation: OPERATION,
   927         })?;
   928     // Every continuous PID3 redundancy term uses the coefficient-cancelling integer KSG form;
   929     // shifted harmonic prefixes retain the previous n+1 binary64 allocation shape.
   930     let harmonic_bytes = n
   931         .checked_add(1)
   932         .and_then(|value| value.checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<f64>() as u128))
   933         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   934             operation: OPERATION,
   935         })?;
   936     let active_threads = effective_thread_count(max_threads, n_usize) as u128;
   937     let worker_scratch = active_threads
   938         .checked_mul(n.saturating_sub(1))
   939         .and_then(|value| value.checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<DistIsx3>() as u128))
   940         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   941             operation: OPERATION,
   942         })?;
   943     #[cfg(feature = "parallel")]
   944     let worker_stacks = active_threads
   945         .checked_mul(WORKER_STACK_BYTES as u128)
   946         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   947             operation: OPERATION,
   948         })?;
   949     #[cfg(not(feature = "parallel"))]
   950     let worker_stacks = 0;
   951     #[cfg(feature = "parallel")]
   952     let ordered_map_intermediate = n
   953         .checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<PidResult<f64>>() as u128)
   954         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   955             operation: OPERATION,
   956         })?;
   957     #[cfg(not(feature = "parallel"))]
   958     let ordered_map_intermediate = 0;
   959     let local_terms =
   960         n.checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<f64>() as u128)
   961             .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   962                 operation: OPERATION,
   963             })?;
   964     let lattice_len = antichains_3().len() as u128;
   965     let lattice_workspace = lattice_len
   966         .checked_mul(lattice_len)
   967         .and_then(|value| value.checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<i64>() as u128))
   968         .and_then(|value| {
   969             value.checked_add(lattice_len.checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<Vec<i64>>() as u128)?)
   970         })
   971         .and_then(|value| {
   972             value.checked_add(
   973                 lattice_len
   974                     .checked_mul(lattice_len)?
   975                     .checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<Antichain3>() as u128)?,
   976             )
   977         })
   978         .and_then(|value| {
   979             value.checked_add(lattice_len.checked_mul(
   980                 (std::mem::size_of::<IncompletePid3Redundancy>()
   981                     + std::mem::size_of::<IncompletePid3Atom>()) as u128,
   982             )?)
   983         })
   984         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   985             operation: OPERATION,
   986         })?;
   987     let estimator_peak = matrix_bytes
   988         .checked_add(harmonic_bytes)
   989         .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(worker_scratch))
   990         .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(worker_stacks))
   991         .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(ordered_map_intermediate))
   992         .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(local_terms))
   993         .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(lattice_workspace))
   994         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
   995             operation: OPERATION,
   996         })?;
   997     let support_peak = [s0, s1, s2, t]
   998         .into_iter()
   999         .map(pid3_cardinality_estimate)
  1000         .try_fold(ResourceEstimate::ZERO, |peak, estimate| {
  1001             let estimate = estimate?;
  1002             Ok::<_, PidError>(ResourceEstimate {
  1003                 estimated_bytes: peak.estimated_bytes.max(estimate.estimated_bytes),
  1004                 pairwise_distances: 0,
  1005                 operations_hint: peak
  1006                     .operations_hint
  1007                     .checked_add(estimate.operations_hint)
  1008                     .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
  1009                         operation: OPERATION,
  1010                     })?,
  1011             })
  1012         })?;
  1013     let distance_operations = pairs
  1014         .checked_mul(dimensions)
  1015         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
  1016             operation: OPERATION,
  1017         })?;
  1018     let redundancy_operations = pairs
  1019         .checked_mul(2)
  1020         .and_then(|value| value.checked_mul(lattice_len))
  1021         .and_then(|value| value.checked_mul(18))
  1022         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
  1023             operation: OPERATION,
  1024         })?;
  1025     Ok(ResourceEstimate {
  1026         estimated_bytes: estimator_peak.max(support_peak.estimated_bytes),
  1027         pairwise_distances: pairs.checked_mul(4).ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
  1028             operation: OPERATION,
  1029         })?,
  1030         operations_hint: distance_operations
  1031             .checked_add(redundancy_operations)
  1032             .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(support_peak.operations_hint))
  1033             .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(lattice_len.pow(3)))
  1034             .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
  1035                 operation: OPERATION,
  1036             })?,
  1037     })
  1038 }
  1039

  1059 pub fn incomplete_pid3_resource_estimate_for_threads(

  1066 ) -> PidResult<ResourceEstimate> {

  1068     // lattice keeps preflight valid even if future availability rules admit more coordinates.
  1069     pid3_resource_estimate_for_threads(s0, s1, s2, t, cfg, max_threads)
  1070 }

  1094     t: MatRef<'_>,

  1107 fn add_pid3_report_retained(
  1108     operation: &'static str,
  1109     mut estimate: ResourceEstimate,
  1110     provenance: &Pid3Provenance,
  1111     report_size: usize,
  1112 ) -> PidResult<ResourceEstimate> {
  1113     estimate.estimated_bytes = estimate
  1114         .estimated_bytes
  1115         .checked_add(provenance.heap_bytes()?)
  1116         .and_then(|value| value.checked_add(report_size as u128))
  1117         .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow { operation })?;
  1118     Ok(estimate)
  1119 }
  1120 
  1121 fn pid3_cardinality_estimate(input: MatRef<'_>) -> PidResult<ResourceEstimate> {
  1122     const OPERATION: &str = "PID3 support cardinalities";
  1123     let n = input.nrows() as u128;
  1124     let dimensions = input.ncols() as u128;
  1125     let coordinates = n.checked_mul(dimensions).ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
  1126         operation: OPERATION,
  1127     })?;
  1128     let log_n = if input.nrows() <= 1 {
  1129         1u128
  1130     } else {
  1131         (usize::BITS - (input.nrows() - 1).leading_zeros()) as u128
  1132     };
  1133     Ok(ResourceEstimate {
  1134         estimated_bytes: coordinates
  1135             .checked_mul(2 * std::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u128)
  1136             .and_then(|value| {
  1137                 value.checked_add(n.checked_mul(std::mem::size_of::<Vec<u64>>() as u128)?)
  1138             })
  1139             .and_then(|value| {
  1140                 value.checked_add(
  1141                     dimensions.checked_mul(
  1142                         std::mem::size_of::<CoordinateCardinalityDiagnostics>() as u128,
  1143                     )?,
  1144                 )
  1145             })
  1146             .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
  1147                 operation: OPERATION,
  1148             })?,
  1149         pairwise_distances: 0,
  1150         operations_hint: coordinates
  1151             .checked_mul(log_n)
  1152             .and_then(|value| value.checked_mul(2))
  1153             .ok_or(PidError::SizeOverflow {
  1154                 operation: OPERATION,
  1155             })?,
  1156     })
  1157 }
  1158 
  1159 fn validate_pid3_common(
  1160     context: &'static str,
  1161     s0: MatRef<'_>,
  1162     s1: MatRef<'_>,
  1163     s2: MatRef<'_>,
  1164     t: MatRef<'_>,
  1165     cfg: &Pid3Config,
  1166 ) -> PidResult<()> {
  1167     if s0.nrows() != s1.nrows() || s0.nrows() != s2.nrows() || s0.nrows() != t.nrows() {
  1168         let n = s0.nrows();
  1169         let right_rows = if s1.nrows() != n {
  1170             s1.nrows()
  1171         } else if s2.nrows() != n {
  1172             s2.nrows()
  1173         } else {
  1174             t.nrows()
  1175         };
  1176         return Err(PidError::RowCountMismatch {
  1177             context,
  1178             left_rows: n,
  1179             right_rows,
  1180         });
  1181     }
  1182     if s0.ncols() == 0 || s1.ncols() == 0 || s2.ncols() == 0 || t.ncols() == 0 {
  1183         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
  1184             context,
  1185             message: "inputs must have at least 1 column",
  1186         });
  1187     }
  1188     if cfg.tie_epsilon != 0.0 {
  1189         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
  1190             context,
  1191             message: "tie_epsilon must be exactly 0; strict counting uses next-down semantics",
  1192         });
  1193     }
  1194     if cfg.k == 0 || s0.nrows() <= cfg.k {
  1195         return Err(PidError::InvalidK {
  1196             k: cfg.k,
  1197             n_samples: s0.nrows(),
  1198         });
  1199     }
  1200     if cfg.metric != Metric::Chebyshev {
  1201         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
  1202             context,
  1203             message: "PID3 ISX is restricted to the cited Metric::Chebyshev (L∞) convention; other metrics are research-gated",
  1204         });
  1205     }
  1206     Ok(())
  1207 }
  1208 
  1209 fn antichain_branch_dimensions(
  1210     antichain: Antichain3,
  1211     source_dimensions: [usize; 3],
  1212     budget: ResourceBudget,
  1213 ) -> PidResult<Vec<usize>> {
  1214     let mut dimensions = try_vec_with_capacity("PID3 branch dimensions", antichain.len(), budget)?;
  1215     for &source_set in antichain.sets() {
  1216         let mut dimension = 0usize;
  1217         for (source, &source_dimension) in source_dimensions.iter().enumerate() {
  1218             if source_set & (1u8 << source) != 0 {
  1219                 dimension =
  1220                     dimension
  1221                         .checked_add(source_dimension)
  1222                         .ok_or(PidError::InvalidConfig {
  1223                             context: "incomplete_pid3_diagnostic",
  1224                             message: "source branch dimension overflow",
  1225                         })?;
  1226             }
  1227         }
  1228         dimensions.push(dimension);
  1229     }
  1230     Ok(dimensions)
  1231 }
  1232 
  1233 fn redundancy_for_antichain(
  1234     context: &'static str,
  1235     sources: &[SymmetricDistanceMatrix; 3],
  1236     target: &SymmetricDistanceMatrix,
  1237     antichain: Antichain3,
  1238     cfg: &Pid3Config,
  1239     budget: ResourceBudget,
  1240 ) -> PidResult<f64> {
  1241     let n = target.n();
  1242     let k = cfg.k;
  1243     let kth = k - 1;
  1244 
  1245     let shifted_harmonics = shifted_harmonic_table(n)?;
  1246 
  1247     // Per-point local term. Each point reads the shared (immutable) distance matrices and
  1248     // allocates its own scratch, so the closure is pure and order-independent. Terms are
  1249     // collected **in index order** and summed left-to-right exactly as the serial loop did,
  1250     // so the `parallel` path is bit-for-bit identical to serial (see `par::map_index_ordered`).
  1251     let local = |i: usize| -> PidResult<f64> {
  1252         let mut scratch = try_vec_with_capacity(
  1253             "PID3 per-query distance scratch",
  1254             n.saturating_sub(1),
  1255             budget,
  1256         )?;
  1257         for j in 0..n {
  1258             if i == j {
  1259                 continue;
  1260             }
  1261             let d0 = sources[0].get(i, j);
  1262             let d1 = sources[1].get(i, j);
  1263             let d2 = sources[2].get(i, j);
  1264             let ds_disj = source_disjunction_distance(antichain, d0, d1, d2);
  1265             let dt_ij = target.get(i, j);
  1266             scratch.push(DistIsx3 {
  1267                 joint: dt_ij.max(ds_disj),
  1268                 ds: ds_disj,
  1269                 dt: dt_ij,
  1270             });
  1271         }
  1272 
  1273         scratch.select_nth_unstable_by(kth, |a, b| a.joint.total_cmp(&b.joint));
  1274         let eps_raw = scratch[kth].joint;
  1275         if eps_raw == 0.0 {
  1276             return Err(PidError::NumericalInstability {
  1277                 context: pid3_non_positive_radius_context(context),
  1278             });
  1279         }
  1280         let (interior_count, boundary_count) =
  1281             kth_neighbor_shell_counts(scratch.iter().map(|distance| distance.joint), eps_raw);
  1282         validate_kth_neighbor_shell(context, i, k, eps_raw, interior_count, boundary_count)?;
  1283         let eps = strict_radius(eps_raw);
  1284 
  1285         // Counts exclude self; estimator uses inclusive counts.
  1286         let mut n_alpha = 1usize;
  1287         let mut n_t = 1usize;
  1288         for d in &scratch {
  1289             if d.ds <= eps {
  1290                 n_alpha += 1;
  1291             }
  1292             if d.dt <= eps {
  1293                 n_t += 1;
  1294             }
  1295         }
  1296 
  1297         Ok(ksg_local_harmonic_term(
  1298             &shifted_harmonics,
  1299             k,
  1300             n,
  1301             n_alpha,
  1302             n_t,
  1303         ))
  1304     };
  1305 
  1306     let terms = crate::par::map_index_ordered(n, local)?;
  1307     let sum = compensated_sum(terms.iter().copied());
  1308     Ok(sum / (n as f64))
  1309 }
  1310 
  1311 fn pid3_non_positive_radius_context(context: &'static str) -> &'static str {
  1312     match context {
  1313         "incomplete_pid3_diagnostic" => "incomplete_pid3_diagnostic: kNN radius is non-positive; jitter changes the estimated distribution and is valid only under an explicit observation-noise model or a reported noise-scale sensitivity analysis; otherwise use a discrete, quantized, or mixed-support estimator",
  1314         _ => "pid3_isx: kNN radius is non-positive; jitter changes the estimated distribution and is valid only under an explicit observation-noise model or a reported noise-scale sensitivity analysis; otherwise use a discrete, quantized, or mixed-support estimator",
  1315     }
  1316 }
  1317 
  1318 #[inline]
  1319 fn source_disjunction_distance(antichain: Antichain3, d0: f64, d1: f64, d2: f64) -> f64 {
  1320     let mut best = f64::INFINITY;
  1321     for &m in antichain.sets() {
  1322         let mut v = 0.0f64;
  1323         if (m & 0b001) != 0 {
  1324             v = v.max(d0);
  1325         }
  1326         if (m & 0b010) != 0 {
  1327             v = v.max(d1);
  1328         }
  1329         if (m & 0b100) != 0 {
  1330             v = v.max(d2);
  1331         }
  1332         best = best.min(v);
  1333     }
  1334     best
  1335 }

  1337 #[cfg(feature = "research-mixed-dimension-pid3")]
  1338 fn mobius_inversion_atoms(
  1339     antichains: &[Antichain3],
  1340     redundancies: &[Pid3Redundancy],
  1341     budget: ResourceBudget,
  1342 ) -> PidResult<Vec<Pid3Atom>> {
  1343     if antichains.len() != redundancies.len() {
  1344         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
  1345             context: "mobius_inversion_atoms",
  1346             message: "antichains/redundancies length mismatch",
  1347         });
  1348     }
  1349     let coefficients = mobius_redundancy_coefficients(antichains, budget)?;
  1350     let mut atoms = try_vec_with_capacity("PID3 atoms", antichains.len(), budget)?;
  1351     for (idx, &a) in antichains.iter().enumerate() {
  1352         let value = compensated_sum(
  1353             coefficients[idx]
  1354                 .iter()
  1355                 .zip(redundancies)
  1356                 .filter(|(coefficient, _)| **coefficient != 0)
  1357                 .map(|(&coefficient, redundancy)| coefficient as f64 * redundancy.value),
  1358         );
  1359         if !value.is_finite() {
  1360             return Err(PidError::NumericalInstability {
  1361                 context: "mobius_inversion_atoms",
  1362             });
  1363         }
  1364         atoms.push(Pid3Atom {
  1365             antichain: a,
  1366             value,
  1367         });
  1368     }
  1369     Ok(atoms)
  1370 }
  1371 
  1372 fn partial_mobius_inversion_atoms(
  1373     antichains: &[Antichain3],
  1374     redundancies: &[IncompletePid3Redundancy],
  1375     budget: ResourceBudget,
  1376 ) -> PidResult<Vec<IncompletePid3Atom>> {
  1377     if antichains.len() != redundancies.len() {
  1378         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
  1379             context: "partial_mobius_inversion_atoms",
  1380             message: "antichains/redundancies length mismatch",
  1381         });
  1382     }
  1383 
  1384     let coefficients = mobius_redundancy_coefficients(antichains, budget)?;
  1385     let mut atoms = try_vec_with_capacity("incomplete PID3 atoms", antichains.len(), budget)?;
  1386     for (atom_index, &antichain) in antichains.iter().enumerate() {
  1387         let mut unavailable_redundancies = try_vec_with_capacity(
  1388             "incomplete PID3 unavailable dependencies",
  1389             antichains.len(),
  1390             budget,
  1391         )?;
  1392         for (redundancy_index, &coefficient) in coefficients[atom_index].iter().enumerate() {
  1393             if coefficient != 0 && redundancies[redundancy_index].value.is_none() {
  1394                 unavailable_redundancies.push(antichains[redundancy_index]);
  1395             }
  1396         }
  1397 
  1398         let value = if unavailable_redundancies.is_empty() {
  1399             let mut terms =
  1400                 try_vec_with_capacity("incomplete PID3 Mobius terms", antichains.len(), budget)?;
  1401             for (redundancy_index, &coefficient) in coefficients[atom_index].iter().enumerate() {
  1402                 if coefficient == 0 {
  1403                     continue;
  1404                 }
  1405                 let value =
  1406                     redundancies[redundancy_index]
  1407                         .value
  1408                         .ok_or(PidError::InvalidConfig {
  1409                             context: "partial_mobius_inversion_atoms",
  1410                             message: "available atom has an unavailable redundancy dependency",
  1411                         })?;
  1412                 terms.push((coefficient as f64) * value);
  1413             }
  1414             Some(compensated_sum(terms))
  1415         } else {
  1416             None
  1417         };
  1418 
  1419         atoms.push(IncompletePid3Atom {
  1420             antichain,
  1421             value,
  1422             unavailable_redundancies,
  1423         });
  1424     }
  1425     Ok(atoms)
  1426 }
  1427 
  1428 fn mobius_redundancy_coefficients(
  1429     antichains: &[Antichain3],
  1430     budget: ResourceBudget,
  1431 ) -> PidResult<Vec<Vec<i64>>> {
  1432     let n = antichains.len();
  1433     let topo = topo_order(antichains, budget)?;
  1434     if topo.len() != n {
  1435         return Err(PidError::InvalidConfig {
  1436             context: "mobius_redundancy_coefficients",
  1437             message: "topological sort failed",
  1438         });
  1439     }
  1440 
  1441     let mut coefficients = try_vec_with_capacity("PID3 Mobius coefficient rows", n, budget)?;
  1442     for _ in 0..n {
  1443         coefficients.push(try_vec_filled(
  1444             "PID3 Mobius coefficient row",
  1445             n,
  1446             0i64,
  1447             budget,
  1448         )?);
  1449     }
  1450     for (position, &atom_index) in topo.iter().enumerate() {
  1451         coefficients[atom_index][atom_index] = 1;
  1452         for &lower_atom_index in &topo[..position] {
  1453             if !leq(antichains[lower_atom_index], antichains[atom_index]) {
  1454                 continue;
  1455             }
  1456             let (atom_coefficients, lower_atom_coefficients) = if atom_index < lower_atom_index {
  1457                 let (before_lower, from_lower) = coefficients.split_at_mut(lower_atom_index);
  1458                 (&mut before_lower[atom_index], &from_lower[0])
  1459             } else {
  1460                 let (before_atom, from_atom) = coefficients.split_at_mut(atom_index);
  1461                 (&mut from_atom[0], &before_atom[lower_atom_index])
  1462             };
  1463             for (atom_coefficient, &lower_atom_coefficient) in atom_coefficients
  1464                 .iter_mut()
  1465                 .zip(lower_atom_coefficients.iter())
  1466             {
  1467                 *atom_coefficient = atom_coefficient.checked_sub(lower_atom_coefficient).ok_or(
  1468                     PidError::InvalidConfig {
  1469                         context: "mobius_redundancy_coefficients",
  1470                         message: "integer coefficient overflow",
  1471                     },
  1472                 )?;
  1473             }
  1474         }
  1475     }
  1476     Ok(coefficients)
  1477 }
  1478 
  1479 fn topo_order(antichains: &[Antichain3], budget: ResourceBudget) -> PidResult<Vec<usize>> {
  1480     let mut remaining =
  1481         try_vec_with_capacity("PID3 topological remaining set", antichains.len(), budget)?;
  1482     remaining.extend(0..antichains.len());
  1483     let mut out = try_vec_with_capacity("PID3 topological order", remaining.len(), budget)?;
  1484     while !remaining.is_empty() {
  1485         let mut mins = try_vec_with_capacity("PID3 topological minima", remaining.len(), budget)?;
  1486         'outer: for &i in &remaining {
  1487             for &j in &remaining {
  1488                 if i == j {
  1489                     continue;
  1490                 }
  1491                 if leq(antichains[j], antichains[i]) {
  1492                     continue 'outer;
  1493                 }
  1494             }
  1495             mins.push(i);
  1496         }
  1497         mins.sort_unstable_by(|&a, &b| antichains[a].cmp(&antichains[b]));
  1498         let chosen = *mins.first().ok_or(PidError::InvalidConfig {
  1499             context: "mobius_redundancy_coefficients",
  1500             message: "topological sort found no minimal antichain",
  1501         })?;
  1502         out.push(chosen);
  1503         remaining.retain(|&x| x != chosen);
  1504     }
  1505     Ok(out)
  1506 }
  1507 
  1508 #[inline]
  1509 fn leq(a: Antichain3, b: Antichain3) -> bool {
  1510     // a ⪯ b iff for every set B in b, there exists A in a with A ⊆ B.
  1511     for &b_set in b.sets() {
  1512         let mut found = false;
  1513         for &a_set in a.sets() {
  1514             if (a_set & b_set) == a_set {
  1515                 found = true;
  1516                 break;
  1517             }
  1518         }
  1519         if !found {
  1520             return false;
  1521         }
  1522     }
  1523     true
  1524 }

    45 #[test]
    46 fn ksg_exclusive_counts_reach_the_exact_integer_harmonic_local_term() {
    47     // This fixed sample is a count/arithmetic conformance witness, not evidence for a population
    48     // support model or estimator calibration. Every coordinate and joint row is unique, and each
    49     // k=2 joint shell has exactly one strict-interior and one boundary neighbor.
    50     let x: [f64; 8] = [7.0, 194.0, 144.0, 75.0, 61.0, 138.0, 38.0, 9.0];
    51     let y: [f64; 8] = [17.0, 48.0, 166.0, 120.0, 2.0, 199.0, 43.0, 93.0];
    52     let expected_counts = [
    53         (54.0, 2, 3),
    54         (119.0, 2, 6),
    55         (69.0, 2, 2),
    56         (69.0, 5, 2),
    57         (54.0, 3, 3),
    58         (79.0, 4, 1),
    59         (41.0, 4, 2),
    60         (66.0, 3, 3),
    61     ];
    62 
    63     for query in 0..x.len() {
    64         let mut joint_distances = Vec::with_capacity(x.len() - 1);
    65         for neighbor in 0..x.len() {
    66             if query != neighbor {
    67                 let dx = (x[query] - x[neighbor]).abs();
    68                 let dy = (y[query] - y[neighbor]).abs();
    69                 joint_distances.push(dx.max(dy));
    70             }
    71         }
    72         joint_distances.sort_by(f64::total_cmp);
    73         let radius = joint_distances[1];
    74         let interior = joint_distances
    75             .iter()
    76             .filter(|&&distance| distance < radius)
    77             .count();
    78         let boundary = joint_distances
    79             .iter()
    80             .filter(|&&distance| distance == radius)
    81             .count();
    82         let nx = (0..x.len())
    83             .filter(|&neighbor| query != neighbor && (x[query] - x[neighbor]).abs() < radius)
    84             .count();
    85         let ny = (0..y.len())
    86             .filter(|&neighbor| query != neighbor && (y[query] - y[neighbor]).abs() < radius)
    87             .count();
    88 
    89         assert_eq!((interior, boundary), (1, 1), "query {query}");
    90         assert_eq!((radius, nx, ny), expected_counts[query], "query {query}");
    91     }
    92

    96         .with_k(2)
    97         .with_negative_handling(NegativeHandling::Allow);

   200     let mi_hat = ksg_mi(x.as_ref(), y.as_ref(), &cfg).unwrap();
   201 
   202     let rho = 1.0 / ((1.0 + sigma_x * sigma_x) * (1.0 + sigma_y * sigma_y)).sqrt();
   203     let mi_true = gaussian_mi_from_corr(rho);
   204 
   205     assert!(mi_hat.is_finite());
   206     // The tolerance must stay BELOW the effect size (mi_true ≈ 0.33 nats) or the check is
   207     // vacuous — a dead-zero estimator, a 2× scale bug, and a bits-for-nats mixup would all
   208     // pass at 0.35. 0.12 nats is comfortably above the KSG finite-sample error here while
   209     // excluding all three failure modes; the second assertion pins the zero-collapse case.
   210     assert!(
   211         (mi_hat - mi_true).abs() < 0.12,
   212         "MI mismatch: estimated={mi_hat:.4} true={mi_true:.4} rho={rho:.4}"
   213     );
   214     assert!(
   215         mi_hat > 0.5 * mi_true,
   216         "MI collapsed toward zero: estimated={mi_hat:.4} true={mi_true:.4}"
   217     );
   218 }

   220 #[test]
   221 fn exp0_strong_dependence_gaussian_channel_sweep_smoke() {
   222     // Strong dependence (very large true MI) can break kNN MI even at low dimension.
   223     // This test is not asserting "perfect accuracy"; it checks:
   224     // - finiteness (no NaNs/Infs)
   225     // - broadly increasing MI as sigma shrinks
   226     // - rough agreement with the analytic Gaussian-channel MI at moderate MI values
   227     //
   228     // Analytic: X ~ N(0,1), Y = X + σN, N~N(0,1): I(X;Y) = 0.5 ln(1 + 1/σ²).
   229     let mut rng = Rng64::new(0x51A7_2026);
   230     let n = 800;
   231 
   232     let mut x_raw = Vec::with_capacity(n);
   233     let mut noise = Vec::with_capacity(n);
   234     for _ in 0..n {
   235         x_raw.push(rng.normal());
   236         noise.push(rng.normal());
   237     }
   238 
   239     let x = MatRef::new(&x_raw, n, 1).unwrap();
   240     let (x, _) = Standardizer::fit_transform(x, ConstantColumnPolicy::Error).unwrap();
   241 
   242     let cfg = KsgConfig::assume_regular_full_dimensional()
   243         .with_k(3)
   244         .with_negative_handling(NegativeHandling::Allow);
   245 
   246     let sigmas = [1.0, 0.3, 0.1];
   247     let mut last = None;
   248     for &sigma in &sigmas {
   249         let y_raw: Vec<f64> = x_raw
   250             .iter()
   251             .zip(noise.iter())
   252             .map(|(&xi, &ni)| xi + sigma * ni)
   253             .collect();
   254 
   255         let y = MatRef::new(&y_raw, n, 1).unwrap();
   256         let (y, _) = Standardizer::fit_transform(y, ConstantColumnPolicy::Error).unwrap();
   257 
   258         let mi_hat = ksg_mi(x.as_ref(), y.as_ref(), &cfg).unwrap();
   259         let mi_true = gaussian_channel_mi(sigma);
   260 
   261         assert!(mi_hat.is_finite(), "sigma={sigma} mi_hat={mi_hat}");
   262 
   263         if let Some(prev) = last {
   264             assert!(
   265                 mi_hat >= prev - 0.25,
   266                 "expected MI to increase as sigma shrinks: sigma={sigma} mi_hat={mi_hat} prev={prev}"
   267             );
   268         }
   269         last = Some(mi_hat);
   270 
   271         assert!(
   272             (mi_hat - mi_true).abs() < 1.0,
   273             "MI mismatch: sigma={sigma} estimated={mi_hat:.4} true={mi_true:.4}"
   274         );
   275     }
   276 }

   304 #[test]
   305 fn co_information_matches_gaussian_sum_channel_approximately() {
   306     // S1,S2 ~ N(0,1) independent. T = S1 + S2 + N, N~N(0, sigma^2).
   307     //
   308     // Analytic:
   309     // I(S1;T) = -0.5 ln((1+sigma^2)/(2+sigma^2))
   310     // I(S1,S2;T) = 0.5 ln((2+sigma^2)/sigma^2)
   311     // CI = I(S1;T)+I(S2;T)-I(S1,S2;T)
   312     let mut rng = Rng64::new(2027);
   313     let n = 700;
   314     let sigma = 0.6;
   315     let sigma2 = sigma * sigma;
   316 
   317     let mut s1 = Vec::with_capacity(n);
   318     let mut s2 = Vec::with_capacity(n);
   319     let mut t = Vec::with_capacity(n);
   320     for _ in 0..n {
   321         let a = rng.normal();
   322         let b = rng.normal();
   323         let noise = sigma * rng.normal();
   324         s1.push(a);
   325         s2.push(b);
   326         t.push(a + b + noise);
   327     }
   328 
   329     let s1 = MatRef::new(&s1, n, 1).unwrap();
   330     let s2 = MatRef::new(&s2, n, 1).unwrap();
   331     let t = MatRef::new(&t, n, 1).unwrap();
   332     let (s1, _) = Standardizer::fit_transform(s1, ConstantColumnPolicy::Error).unwrap();
   333     let (s2, _) = Standardizer::fit_transform(s2, ConstantColumnPolicy::Error).unwrap();
   334     let (t, _) = Standardizer::fit_transform(t, ConstantColumnPolicy::Error).unwrap();
   335 
   336     let cfg = KsgConfig::assume_regular_full_dimensional()
   337         .with_k(3)
   338         .with_negative_handling(NegativeHandling::Allow);
   339     let ci_hat = co_information_pairwise(s1.as_ref(), s2.as_ref(), t.as_ref(), &cfg).unwrap();
   340 
   341     let i_s1_t = -0.5 * ((1.0 + sigma2) / (2.0 + sigma2)).ln();
   342     let i_s1s2_t = 0.5 * ((2.0 + sigma2) / sigma2).ln();
   343     let ci_true = 2.0 * i_s1_t - i_s1s2_t;
   344 
   345     assert!(ci_hat.is_finite());
   346     // Same principle as the MI test above: tolerance below the effect size (|ci_true| ≈ 0.39
   347     // nats), plus an explicit bound that excludes a zero-collapsed estimator and pins the sign.
   348     assert!(
   349         (ci_hat - ci_true).abs() < 0.20,
   350         "CI mismatch: estimated={ci_hat:.4} true={ci_true:.4}"
   351     );
   352     assert!(
   353         ci_hat < 0.5 * ci_true,
   354         "CI collapsed toward zero (should be clearly negative): estimated={ci_hat:.4} true={ci_true:.4}"
   355     );
   356 }

   440 #[test]
   441 fn ksg_handles_heavily_quantized_data_cleanly() {
   442     // Stress test: feed heavily-quantized data so that many points coincide exactly
   443     // (the realistic failure mode when continuous signals are rounded to a coarse grid
   444     // or recorded by a low-resolution sensor). The contract is that the estimator must
   445     // EITHER reject a collapsed or ambiguous kNN shell with its structured error OR return a
   446     // finite, stable estimate — but never panic, never produce NaN/Inf, and never silently report
   447     // a value that pretends the data was continuous.
   448     //
   449     // We sweep quantization coarseness from very coarse (few levels → many exact ties)
   450     // to fairly fine (few ties). At every coarseness, both outcomes are acceptable; we
   451     // only forbid panics and non-finite "successes".
   452     let mut rng = Rng64::new(0xC0FFEE);
   453     let n = 200;
   454 
   455     let mut x_cont = Vec::with_capacity(n);
   456     let mut y_cont = Vec::with_capacity(n);
   457     for _ in 0..n {
   458         let base = rng.normal();
   459         x_cont.push(base);
   460         y_cont.push(base + 0.3 * rng.normal());
   461     }
   462 
   463     let cfg = KsgConfig::default()
   464         .with_k(3)
   465         .with_negative_handling(NegativeHandling::Allow)
   466         .with_support_contract(SupportContract::KnownQuantized);
   467 
   468     // levels=2 is extremely coarse (data collapses onto ~2 grid points per axis →
   469     // heavy duplication); levels=64 is fine enough that ties are rare.
   470     for &levels in &[2.0f64, 3.0, 5.0, 16.0, 64.0] {
   471         let quantize = |v: f64| -> f64 { (v * levels).round() / levels };
   472         let xq: Vec<f64> = x_cont.iter().map(|&v| quantize(v)).collect();
   473         let yq: Vec<f64> = y_cont.iter().map(|&v| quantize(v)).collect();
   474 
   475         let x = MatRef::new(&xq, n, 1).unwrap();
   476         let y = MatRef::new(&yq, n, 1).unwrap();
   477 
   478         assert!(matches!(
   479             ksg_mi(x, y, &cfg),
   480             Err(PidError::UnsupportedSupportContract {
   481                 contract: SupportContract::KnownQuantized,
   482                 ..
   483             })
   484         ));
   485     }
   486 }

    41 #[test]
    42 fn ehrlich_public_redundancy_propagates_the_inclusive_count_witness() {
    43     // The private isx.rs regression pins every radius/count and the exact row-5 local term. This
    44     // integration assertion separately pins the public, index-ordered compensated reduction. It
    45     // is implementation conformance on fixed rows, not population-support or calibration evidence.
    46     let s1_data: [f64; 8] = [7.0, 194.0, 144.0, 75.0, 61.0, 138.0, 38.0, 9.0];
    47     let target_data: [f64; 8] = [17.0, 48.0, 166.0, 120.0, 2.0, 199.0, 43.0, 93.0];
    48     let s2_data: [f64; 8] = std::array::from_fn(|index| 1_000.0 * s1_data[index] + index as f64);
    49     let s1 = MatRef::new(&s1_data, 8, 1).unwrap();
    50     let s2 = MatRef::new(&s2_data, 8, 1).unwrap();
    51     let target = MatRef::new(&target_data, 8, 1).unwrap();
    52     let config = IsxConfig {
    53         k: 2,
    54         ..IsxConfig::assume_regular_full_dimensional()
    55     };
    56 
    57     let redundancy = isx_redundancy(s1, s2, target, &config).unwrap();
    58 
    59     assert_eq!(redundancy.to_bits(), 0x3fb5_a35a_35a3_5a3e);
    60     let correctly_rounded_exact_mean = 71.0_f64 / 840.0;
    61     assert_eq!(
    62         correctly_rounded_exact_mean.to_bits(),
    63         0x3fb5_a35a_35a3_5a36
    64     );
    65     assert_ne!(
    66         redundancy.to_bits(),
    67         correctly_rounded_exact_mean.to_bits(),
    68         "the public reduction is a frozen implementation value, not a correct-rounding claim"
    69     );
    70 }

   401 #[test]
   402 fn ehrlich_ksg_matches_pinned_csxpid_on_committed_fixture() {
   403     // Generated by scripts/generate-csxpid-reference.py from the authors' public csxpid
   404     // implementation. The JSON records the upstream commit, exact scientific Python
   405     // environment, SciPy kd-tree backend, complete input rows, bit-to-nat conversion, and output
   406     // hash. It is therefore an external cross-check rather than a self-generated regression pin.
   407     let reference = csxpid_reference();
   408     assert_eq!(
   409         reference["provenance"]["upstream"]["commit"].as_str(),
   410         Some("7bb984611a422cf7944ece68993fe3a27e2eadec")
   411     );
   412 
   413     let case = &reference["cases"]["bivariate"];
   414     let rows = case["rows"].as_array().unwrap();
   415     let n = rows.len();
   416     let mut s1 = Vec::with_capacity(n);
   417     let mut s2 = Vec::with_capacity(n);
   418     let mut t = Vec::with_capacity(n);
   419     for row in rows {
   420         let row = row.as_array().unwrap();
   421         assert_eq!(row.len(), 3);
   422         s1.push(row[0].as_f64().unwrap());
   423         s2.push(row[1].as_f64().unwrap());
   424         t.push(row[2].as_f64().unwrap());
   425     }
   426 
   427     let s1 = MatRef::new(&s1, n, 1).unwrap();
   428     let s2 = MatRef::new(&s2, n, 1).unwrap();
   429     let t = MatRef::new(&t, n, 1).unwrap();
   430 
   431     let cfg = IsxConfig {
   432         k: 3,
   433         method: IsxMethod::EhrlichKsg,
   434         ..IsxConfig::assume_regular_full_dimensional()
   435     };
   436 
   437     let red = isx_redundancy(s1, s2, t, &cfg).unwrap();
   438     let expected = case["redundancy_bits"].as_f64().unwrap() * std::f64::consts::LN_2;
   439     let stored_nats = case["redundancy_nats"].as_f64().unwrap();
   440     assert!(
   441         (stored_nats - expected).abs() < 1e-15,
   442         "invalid bit-to-nat conversion in pinned csxpid fixture: bits*ln(2)={expected:.15e} stored={stored_nats:.15e}"
   443     );
   444 
   445     assert!(red.is_finite());
   446     assert!(
   447         (red - expected).abs() < 1e-12,
   448         "I^sx mismatch against pinned csxpid: estimated={red:.15e} expected={expected:.15e}"
   449     );
   450 }

    20 struct Rng(u64);

    22 impl Rng {
    23     fn next_f64(&mut self) -> f64 {
    24         let mut x = self.0;
    25         x ^= x >> 12;
    26         x ^= x << 25;
    27         x ^= x >> 27;
    28         self.0 = x;
    29         (x.wrapping_mul(0x2545_F491_4F6C_DD1D) >> 11) as f64 / (1_u64 << 53) as f64
    30     }
    31 }
    32 
    33 fn euclidean_data(n: usize) -> (Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>) {
    34     let mut rng = Rng(0xC0DE_5EED_1234_5678);
    35     let mut x = Vec::with_capacity(2 * n);
    36     let mut y = Vec::with_capacity(n);
    37     for _ in 0..n {
    38         let a = rng.next_f64();
    39         let b = rng.next_f64();
    40         x.extend_from_slice(&[a, b]);
    41         y.push(0.3 * a + 0.2 * b + rng.next_f64());
    42     }
    43     (x, y)
    44 }

     1 #![cfg(feature = "experimental-pipelines")]
     2 
     3 //! Serial == parallel **bit-identity** guard.
     4 //!
     5 //! The `parallel` (rayon) feature is required to be bit-for-bit identical to the serial path
     6 //! (`f64::to_bits` equality) — a non-negotiable project convention. This test pins that
     7 //! contract for every estimator that the `parallel` feature touches:
     8 //!
     9 //! - `ksg_local_mi_terms` (the per-point KSG local MI contributions),
    10 //! - the 2-source PID atoms (`pid2_isx`),
    11 //! - the 3-source PID atoms / redundancies (`pid3_isx`, whose `redundancy_for_antichain` is
    12 //!   the parallelized hot loop),
    13 //! - the continuous `I^sx_∩` redundancy (`isx_redundancy`, `IsxMethod::EhrlichKsg`), and
    14 //! - a block-bootstrap result (`block_bootstrap`).
    15 //!
    16 //! Strategy: the expected values below are **frozen `f64::to_bits` patterns captured from the
    17 //! serial build**
    18 //! (`cargo test -p pid-core --features experimental-pipelines --test parallel_bit_identity`).
    19 //! The same test then runs under
    20 //! `cargo test -p pid-core --features experimental-pipelines,parallel --test parallel_bit_identity`;
    21 //! if any parallelized path changed a single bit, the corresponding `assert_eq!` on `to_bits()`
    22 //! fails. Running it in *both* configurations is what makes it a serial==parallel guard: the
    23 //! serial run proves the frozen constants are the serial truth, the parallel run proves the
    24 //! parallel path reproduces them exactly.
    25 //!
    26 //! The constants are NOT scientific ground truth — they are whatever the (unchanged) serial
    27 //! estimator produces on this fixed synthetic dataset; the test's only job is to detect any
    28 //! serial/parallel divergence (or any accidental change to the serial numbers).
    29 //!
    30 //! The count-based tests use a deliberately non-uniform empirical distribution and compare
    31 //! repeated calls with `f64::to_bits`. Those paths do not use Rayon; their guard catches
    32 //! iteration-order nondeterminism in histogram accumulation across invocations.
    33

    53 /// Deterministic synthetic system: V and L share a latent signal that drives the target A;
    54 /// D is an independent noisy copy. Fixed seed, so the data is identical on every run and in
    55 /// both feature configurations.
    56 fn make_system(n: usize, seed: u64) -> (MatOwned, MatOwned, MatOwned, MatOwned) {
    57     let mut rng = Rng64::new(seed);
    58     let mut s1 = Vec::with_capacity(n * 2);
    59     let mut s2 = Vec::with_capacity(n * 2);
    60     let mut s3 = Vec::with_capacity(n);
    61     let mut t = Vec::with_capacity(n);
    62     for _ in 0..n {
    63         let signal = rng.normal();
    64         s1.push(signal + 0.2 * rng.normal());
    65         s1.push(0.5 * rng.normal());
    66         s2.push(signal + 0.3 * rng.normal());
    67         s2.push(0.5 * rng.normal());
    68         s3.push(0.7 * signal + 0.7 * rng.normal());
    69         t.push(signal + 0.1 * rng.normal());
    70     }
    71     (
    72         MatOwned::new(s1, n, 2).unwrap(),
    73         MatOwned::new(s2, n, 2).unwrap(),
    74         MatOwned::new(s3, n, 1).unwrap(),
    75         MatOwned::new(t, n, 1).unwrap(),
    76     )
    77 }
    78 
    79 const N: usize = 120;
    80 const SEED: u64 = 20240917;
    81 const THREAD_BUDGET_N: usize = 48;
    82 
    83 fn ksg_cfg() -> KsgConfig {
    84     KsgConfig::assume_regular_full_dimensional()
    85         .with_k(4)
    86         .with_negative_handling(NegativeHandling::Allow)
    87 }
    88 
    89 /// An irregular empirical PMF with many distinct probabilities. Using uniform logic-gate data
    90 /// here would let reordered floating-point accumulation accidentally produce the same bits.
    91 fn nonuniform_discrete_labels() -> [Vec<u32>; 4] {
    92     let states = [
    93         (0, 4, 1, 9, 17),
    94         (0, 2, 1, 8, 5),
    95         (1, 4, 0, 8, 13),
    96         (1, 2, 2, 7, 7),
    97         (2, 3, 0, 7, 11),
    98         (2, 3, 2, 6, 3),
    99         (3, 1, 1, 6, 19),
   100         (3, 0, 2, 5, 2),
   101         (4, 1, 3, 5, 23),
   102         (4, 0, 3, 4, 6),
   103         (5, 2, 4, 4, 29),
   104         (5, 4, 0, 9, 4),
   105     ];
   106     let n = states.iter().map(|state| state.4).sum();
   107     let mut labels = std::array::from_fn(|_| Vec::with_capacity(n));
   108     for &(x, y, z, w, count) in &states {
   109         for _ in 0..count {
   110             labels[0].push(x);
   111             labels[1].push(y);
   112             labels[2].push(z);
   113             labels[3].push(w);
   114         }
   115     }
   116     labels
   117 }
   118 
   119 fn discrete_pid2_bits(result: &IminPid2Result) -> [u64; 7] {
   120     [
   121         result.redundancy.to_bits(),
   122         result.unique_s1.to_bits(),
   123         result.unique_s2.to_bits(),
   124         result.synergy.to_bits(),
   125         result.mi_s1_t.to_bits(),
   126         result.mi_s2_t.to_bits(),
   127         result.mi_s1s2_t.to_bits(),
   128     ]
   129 }
   130 
   131 fn thread_limits_through_available_maximum() -> Vec<usize> {
   132     let mut limits = vec![1, 2, 3, 4, ResourceBudget::default().max_threads];
   133     limits.sort_unstable();
   134     limits.dedup();
   135     limits
   136 }
   137 
   138 fn budget_with_threads(max_threads: usize) -> ResourceBudget {
   139     let mut budget = ResourceBudget::default();
   140     budget.max_threads = max_threads;
   141     budget
   142 }
   143 
   144 fn normalize_ksg_resource_accounting(report: &mut KsgMiReport) {
   145     report.resource_budget = budget_with_threads(1);
   146     report.resource_estimate = ResourceEstimate::ZERO;
   147 }
   148 
   149 fn pid3_bits(result: &pid_core::experimental::mixed_dimension_pid3::Pid3Result) -> Vec<u64> {
   150     result
   151         .redundancies
   152         .iter()
   153         .map(|entry| entry.value.to_bits())
   154         .chain(result.atoms.iter().map(|entry| entry.value.to_bits()))
   155         .collect()
   156 }
   157 
   158 fn bootstrap_result_bits(result: &pid_core::experimental::pipelines::BootstrapResult) -> Vec<u64> {
   159     let mut bits = vec![result.point_estimate.to_bits()];
   160     let summary = result
   161         .summary
   162         .as_ref()
   163         .expect("the deterministic statistic must complete for every replicate");
   164     bits.extend([
   165         summary.resample_mean.to_bits(),
   166         summary.resample_standard_deviation.to_bits(),
   167         summary.percentile_lower.to_bits(),
   168         summary.percentile_upper.to_bits(),
   169     ]);
   170     for outcome in &result.replicates {
   171         bits.push(outcome.replicate_index as u64);
   172         match &outcome.status {
   173             BootstrapReplicateStatus::Complete { value } => bits.push(value.to_bits()),
   174             BootstrapReplicateStatus::Failed { error } => {
   175                 panic!("deterministic bootstrap replicate failed: {error}")
   176             }
   177             _ => panic!("unexpected future bootstrap replicate status"),
   178         }
   179     }
   180     bits
   181 }

   326     assert_eq!(terms.len(), N);
   327     // Frozen reference: bit-pattern checksum + the first/last/mid term bits. We XOR-fold all
   328     // term bits into one u64 so a divergence at any index trips the checksum, then also pin a
   329     // few individual terms to localize a failure.
   330     let checksum = terms.iter().fold(0u64, |acc, &x| acc ^ x.to_bits());

   390     let r = pid3_isx(s1.as_ref(), s2.as_ref(), s3.as_ref(), t.as_ref(), &cfg).unwrap();
   391     assert_eq!(r.atoms.len(), 18);
   392     // XOR-fold every atom's bits (order is the canonical antichain order, fixed) and every
   393     // redundancy's bits — `redundancy_for_antichain` is the parallelized loop.
   394     let atom_checksum = r.atoms.iter().fold(0u64, |acc, a| acc ^ a.value.to_bits());
   395     let red_checksum = r
   396         .redundancies
   397         .iter()
   398         .fold(0u64, |acc, x| acc ^ x.value.to_bits());
   399     // Pin two individual atoms to localize a failure.
   400     let unq_s1 = r
   401         .atom(Antichain3::try_from_sets(&[0b001]).unwrap())
   402         .unwrap();
   403     let full_syn = r
   404         .atom(Antichain3::try_from_sets(&[0b111]).unwrap())
   405         .unwrap();
   406     assert_eq!(
   407         [
   408             atom_checksum,
   409             red_checksum,
   410             unq_s1.to_bits(),
   411             full_syn.to_bits(),
   412         ],
   413         [
   414             PID3_ATOM_CHECKSUM,
   415             PID3_RED_CHECKSUM,
   416             PID3_ATOM_001_BITS,
   417             PID3_ATOM_111_BITS,
   418         ],
   419         "pid3 bits diverged"
   420     );
   421 }

   426     // in `block_bootstrap`) with a non-trivial, RNG-order-sensitive statistic. Unlike continuous
   427     // kNN estimators, the mean remains defined when with-replacement resampling duplicates rows.
   428     // Use exactly represented binary-rational inputs. The estimator fixtures above intentionally
   429     // exercise transcendental RNG output, but a frozen bootstrap *mean* must not depend on a
   430     // platform libm's last bits before the serial/parallel comparison even begins.
   431     let data: Vec<f64> = (0..N)

   100 EXPECTED_EXACT_STRICT_EPSILON_MULTIPLIER_TEXT = "9.761311"

   122 class CheckError(RuntimeError):
   123     """The enclosure, custody, metric separation, or frozen observations failed."""
   124 
   125 
   126 class Row(NamedTuple):
   127     """One independently reconstructed fixture row."""
   128 
   129     sample_count: int
   130     k: int
   131     x_count: int
   132     y_count: int
   133 
   134 
   135 class ErrorInterval(NamedTuple):
   136     """Directed Decimal enclosure of one absolute binary64 error."""
   137 
   138     lower: Decimal
   139     upper: Decimal
   140 
   141 
   142 def require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
   143     if not condition:
   144         raise CheckError(message)
   145 
   146 
   147 def require_exact_int_field(
   148     mapping: dict[str, Any],
   149     key: str,
   150     expected: int,
   151     label: str,
   152 ) -> None:
   153     value = mapping.get(key)
   154     require(
   155         type(value) is int and value == expected,
   156         f"{label} changed or is not a JSON integer",
   157     )
   158 
   159 
   160 def sha256(raw: bytes) -> str:
   161     return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
   162 
   163 
   164 def reject_duplicate_keys(pairs: list[tuple[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   165     result: dict[str, Any] = {}
   166     for key, value in pairs:
   167         if key in result:
   168             raise CheckError(f"duplicate JSON key: {key!r}")
   169         result[key] = value
   170     return result
   171 
   172 
   173 def reject_nonfinite_json(token: str) -> None:
   174     raise CheckError(f"non-finite JSON token: {token}")
   175 
   176 
   177 def canonical_json_bytes(value: Any) -> bytes:
   178     return (
   179         json.dumps(
   180             value,
   181             ensure_ascii=True,
   182             indent=2,
   183             sort_keys=True,
   184             allow_nan=False,
   185         )
   186         + "\n"
   187     ).encode("utf-8")
   188 
   189 
   190 def parse_canonical_json(raw: bytes, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
   191     try:
   192         value = json.loads(
   193             raw,
   194             object_pairs_hook=reject_duplicate_keys,
   195             parse_constant=reject_nonfinite_json,
   196         )
   197     except (UnicodeError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as error:
   198         raise CheckError(f"{label} is not finite UTF-8 JSON: {error}") from error
   199     require(isinstance(value, dict), f"{label} top level is not an object")
   200     require(raw == canonical_json_bytes(value), f"{label} is not canonical JSON")
   201     return value
   202 
   203 
   204 def reconstruct_rows() -> tuple[list[Row], int]:
   205     exhaustive = [
   206         Row(sample_count, k, x_count, y_count)
   207         for sample_count in range(2, EXHAUSTIVE_MAX_SAMPLES + 1)
   208         for k in range(1, sample_count)
   209         for x_count in range(k - 1, sample_count)
   210         for y_count in range(k - 1, sample_count)
   211     ]
   212     stress: list[Row] = []
   213     for sample_count in STRESS_SAMPLE_SIZES:
   214         k_values = sorted(
   215             {
   216                 value
   217                 for value in (
   218                     1,
   219                     2,
   220                     3,
   221                     4,
   222                     8,
   223                     16,
   224                     64,
   225                     sample_count // 2,
   226                     sample_count - 1,
   227                 )
   228                 if 1 <= value < sample_count
   229             }
   230         )
   231         for k in k_values:
   232             count_values = sorted(
   233                 {
   234                     k - 1,
   235                     min(k, sample_count - 1),
   236                     (k + sample_count - 1) // 2,
   237                     sample_count - 2,
   238                     sample_count - 1,
   239                 }
   240             )
   241             for x_count in count_values:
   242                 for y_count in count_values:
   243                     stress.append(Row(sample_count, k, x_count, y_count))
   244 
   245     require(len(exhaustive) == EXHAUSTIVE_ROW_COUNT, "exhaustive row count changed")
   246     require(len(stress) == STRESS_ROW_COUNT, "stress row count changed")
   247     rows = exhaustive + stress
   248     require(len(rows) == ROW_COUNT, "total row count changed")
   249     require(len(rows) == len(set(rows)), "reconstructed rows are not unique")
   250     return rows, len(exhaustive)
   251 
   252 
   253 def is_endpoint(row: Row) -> bool:
   254     return (row.x_count, row.y_count) in (
   255         (row.k - 1, row.sample_count - 1),
   256         (row.sample_count - 1, row.k - 1),
   257     )
   258

   260 def decimal_from_fixture(text: Any, row_index: int) -> Decimal:
   261     require(type(text) is str, f"row {row_index}: expected_nats is not a string")
   262     try:
   263         value = Decimal(text)
   264     except InvalidOperation as error:
   265         raise CheckError(f"row {row_index}: expected_nats is not Decimal") from error
   266     require(value.is_finite(), f"row {row_index}: expected_nats is not finite")
   267     require(str(value) == text, f"row {row_index}: expected_nats is not canonical Decimal text")
   268     return value
   269

   271 def load_digest_bound_fixture(
   272     repo_root: Path,
   273 ) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], list[Row], list[Decimal]]:
   274     fixture_path = repo_root / FIXTURE_RELATIVE_PATH
   275     sidecar_path = repo_root / SIDECAR_RELATIVE_PATH
   276     generator_path = repo_root / GENERATOR_RELATIVE_PATH
   277 
   278     fixture_raw = fixture_path.read_bytes()
   279     require(
   280         sha256(fixture_raw) == EXPECTED_FIXTURE_SHA256,
   281         "fixture bytes changed from the frozen schema-2 digest",
   282     )
   283     fixture = parse_canonical_json(fixture_raw, "fixture")
   284     require(
   285         sidecar_path.read_bytes() == EXPECTED_SIDECAR_TEXT.encode("ascii"),
   286         "fixture SHA-256 sidecar changed",
   287     )
   288     require(
   289         sha256(generator_path.read_bytes()) == EXPECTED_GENERATOR_SHA256,
   290         "fixture generator bytes changed from the frozen digest",
   291     )
   292 
   293     require(fixture.get("schema") == FIXTURE_SCHEMA, "fixture schema changed")
   294     require_exact_int_field(
   295         fixture,
   296         "schema_revision",
   297         FIXTURE_SCHEMA_REVISION,
   298         "fixture schema revision",
   299     )
   300     generator = fixture.get("generator")
   301     require(type(generator) is dict, "fixture generator metadata is absent")
   302     require(generator.get("path") == GENERATOR_RELATIVE_PATH, "fixture generator path changed")
   303     require(
   304         generator.get("sha256") == EXPECTED_GENERATOR_SHA256,
   305         "fixture generator metadata digest changed",
   306     )
   307     require(generator.get("imports_pid_rs") is False, "fixture declares a pid-rs import")
   308     require(
   309         generator.get("third_party_dependencies") == [],
   310         "fixture declares a third-party generator dependency",
   311     )
   312 
   313     arithmetic = fixture.get("arithmetic")
   314     bounds = fixture.get("bounds")
   315     require(type(arithmetic) is dict, "fixture arithmetic metadata is absent")
   316     require(type(bounds) is dict, "fixture bounds metadata is absent")
   317     require_exact_int_field(
   318         arithmetic,
   319         "decimal_precision_digits",
   320         REFERENCE_ROUNDING_PRECISION,
   321         "fixture Decimal precision",
   322     )
   323     require(
   324         arithmetic.get("exact_identity")
   325         == "H_(k-1) + H_(n-1) - H_(nx) - H_(ny)",
   326         "fixture exact identity changed",
   327     )
   328     require(arithmetic.get("logarithm_unit") == "nats", "fixture unit changed")
   329     require_exact_int_field(
   330         arithmetic,
   331         "endpoint_cancellation_exact_zero_case_count",
   332         ENDPOINT_COUNT,
   333         "fixture endpoint total",
   334     )
   335     require_exact_int_field(
   336         arithmetic,
   337         "endpoint_cancellation_exact_zero_exhaustive_case_count",
   338         EXHAUSTIVE_ENDPOINT_COUNT,
   339         "fixture exhaustive endpoint total",
   340     )
   341     require_exact_int_field(
   342         arithmetic,
   343         "endpoint_cancellation_exact_zero_stress_case_count",
   344         STRESS_ENDPOINT_COUNT,
   345         "fixture stress endpoint total",
   346     )
   347     require_exact_int_field(
   348         bounds,
   349         "exhaustive_case_count",
   350         EXHAUSTIVE_ROW_COUNT,
   351         "fixture exhaustive row count",
   352     )
   353     require_exact_int_field(
   354         bounds,
   355         "exhaustive_max_samples",
   356         EXHAUSTIVE_MAX_SAMPLES,
   357         "fixture exhaustive bound",
   358     )
   359     require_exact_int_field(
   360         bounds,
   361         "stress_case_count",
   362         STRESS_ROW_COUNT,
   363         "fixture stress row count",
   364     )
   365     stress_sample_sizes = bounds.get("stress_sample_sizes")
   366     require(
   367         type(stress_sample_sizes) is list
   368         and all(type(value) is int for value in stress_sample_sizes)
   369         and tuple(stress_sample_sizes) == STRESS_SAMPLE_SIZES,
   370         "fixture stress sample sizes changed or contain a non-integer",
   371     )
   372 
   373     rows, exhaustive_cut = reconstruct_rows()
   374     cases = fixture.get("cases")
   375     require(type(cases) is list, "fixture cases are absent")
   376     require(len(cases) == len(rows), "fixture row count differs from reconstruction")
   377     stored_values: list[Decimal] = []
   378     expected_keys = {"expected_nats", "k", "sample_count", "x_count", "y_count"}
   379     for row_index, (case, row) in enumerate(zip(cases, rows, strict=True)):
   380         require(type(case) is dict, f"row {row_index}: case is not an object")
   381         require(set(case) == expected_keys, f"row {row_index}: case fields changed")
   382         for field, expected in (
   383             ("sample_count", row.sample_count),
   384             ("k", row.k),
   385             ("x_count", row.x_count),
   386             ("y_count", row.y_count),
   387         ):
   388             require(type(case[field]) is int, f"row {row_index}: {field} is not an integer")
   389             require(case[field] == expected, f"row {row_index}: reconstructed order changed")
   390         require(
   391             1 <= row.k < row.sample_count
   392             and row.k - 1 <= row.x_count < row.sample_count
   393             and row.k - 1 <= row.y_count < row.sample_count,
   394             f"row {row_index}: count tuple is outside the exact identity domain",
   395         )
   396         stored_values.append(decimal_from_fixture(case["expected_nats"], row_index))
   397 
   398     exhaustive_endpoints = sum(is_endpoint(row) for row in rows[:exhaustive_cut])
   399     stress_endpoints = sum(is_endpoint(row) for row in rows[exhaustive_cut:])
   400     require(
   401         exhaustive_endpoints == EXHAUSTIVE_ENDPOINT_COUNT,
   402         "reconstructed exhaustive endpoint count changed",
   403     )
   404     require(
   405         stress_endpoints == STRESS_ENDPOINT_COUNT,
   406         "reconstructed stress endpoint count changed",
   407     )
   408     require(
   409         max(
   410             index
   411             for row in rows
   412             for index in (
   413                 row.k - 1,
   414                 row.sample_count - 1,
   415                 row.x_count,
   416                 row.y_count,
   417             )
   418         )
   419         == MAXIMUM_RECIPROCAL_SUMMAND_INDEX,
   420         "maximum reciprocal summand index changed",
   421     )
   422     return fixture, rows, stored_values
   423
