  1943 def validate_identity_firewall() -> None:
  1944     relative = "crates/pid-core/identity/software-identity-reference-v1.json"
  1945     candidate = canonical_json_from_bytes(
  1946         read_candidate_bytes(relative), label=relative
  1947     )
  1948     baseline = canonical_json_from_bytes(
  1949         git_blob_at(SCIENTIFIC_BASELINE, relative),
  1950         label=f"{relative}@scientific-baseline",
  1951     )
  1952     require(
  1953         isinstance(candidate, dict) and isinstance(baseline, dict),
  1954         "software identity roots must be objects",
  1955     )
  1956     candidate_artifacts = candidate.get("reference_artifacts")
  1957     baseline_artifacts = baseline.get("reference_artifacts")
  1958     require(
  1959         isinstance(candidate_artifacts, list)
  1960         and isinstance(baseline_artifacts, list)
  1961         and len(candidate_artifacts) == len(baseline_artifacts) == 2,
  1962         "software identity must retain exactly two reference artifacts",
  1963     )
  1964     normalized = json.loads(json.dumps(candidate))
  1965     expected_digests = {
  1966         "method_catalog": hashlib.sha256(
  1967             read_candidate_bytes("method-catalog.json")
  1968         ).hexdigest(),
  1969         "proposed_release_scope": hashlib.sha256(
  1970             read_candidate_bytes("release-scope-1.0.json")
  1971         ).hexdigest(),
  1972     }
  1973     for index, (actual, historical) in enumerate(
  1974         zip(candidate_artifacts, baseline_artifacts, strict=True)
  1975     ):
  1976         require(
  1977             isinstance(actual, dict) and isinstance(historical, dict),
  1978             f"software identity artifact {index} must be an object",
  1979         )
  1980         kind = actual.get("kind")
  1981         require(
  1982             isinstance(kind, str) and kind in expected_digests,
  1983             f"software identity artifact {index} has an unauthorized kind",
  1984         )
  1985         require(
  1986             actual.get("canonical_json_sha256") == expected_digests[kind],
  1987             f"software identity artifact {kind!r} does not bind current canonical bytes",
  1988         )
  1989         normalized["reference_artifacts"][index]["canonical_json_sha256"] = (
  1990             historical.get("canonical_json_sha256")
  1991         )
  1992     require(
  1993         normalized == baseline,
  1994         "software identity changed outside the two authorized forensic digests",
  1995     )

  1998 def validate_changed_path_firewall(paths: Iterable[str]) -> None:
  1999     for path in paths:
  2000         lower = path.lower()
  2001         require(
  2002             path not in FORBIDDEN_EXACT_CHANGED_PATHS,
  2003             f"forbidden later-wave path entered KSG phase: {path}",
  2004         )
  2005         require(
  2006             not any(
  2007                 path.startswith(prefix) for prefix in FORBIDDEN_CHANGED_PATH_PREFIXES
  2008             ),
  2009             f"forbidden later-wave path prefix entered KSG phase: {path}",
  2010         )
  2011         require(
  2012             not any(fragment in lower for fragment in FORBIDDEN_CHANGED_PATH_FRAGMENTS),
  2013             f"forbidden later-wave path token entered KSG phase: {path}",
  2014         )
  2015         require(
  2016             not lower.endswith((".pdf", ".tex")),
  2017             f"unrelated PDF/TeX path entered KSG phase: {path}",
  2018         )
  2019         if path.startswith("audit/formal/"):
  2020             require(
  2021                 path.startswith("audit/formal/lean-ksg-harmonic/")
  2022                 or path.startswith("audit/formal/z3-ksg-harmonic/"),
  2023                 f"unrelated formal path entered KSG phase: {path}",
  2024             )
  2025

  2027 def validate_checker_source_model() -> None:
  2028     try:
  2029         source = SCRIPT_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
  2030         tree = ast.parse(source, filename=str(SCRIPT_PATH))
  2031     except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, SyntaxError) as error:
  2032         raise PhaseIsolationError(
  2033             f"cannot inspect checker source model: {error}"
  2034         ) from error
  2035     assert_nodes = [node for node in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(node, ast.Assert)]
  2036     require(
  2037         not assert_nodes,
  2038         "checker source contains an optimization-removable assert statement",
  2039     )
  2040     require(
  2041         tuple(sorted(EXPECTED_CHANGED_PATHS)) == EXPECTED_CHANGED_PATHS
  2042         and len(EXPECTED_CHANGED_PATHS) == len(set(EXPECTED_CHANGED_PATHS)),
  2043         "generated changed-path allowlist is not sorted and duplicate-free",
  2044     )
  2045     require(
  2046         tuple(sorted(BOUND_ALLOWED_PATHS)) == BOUND_ALLOWED_PATHS
  2047         and len(BOUND_ALLOWED_PATHS) == len(set(BOUND_ALLOWED_PATHS)),
  2048         "reviewed full-blob path inventory is not sorted and duplicate-free",
  2049     )
  2050     require(
  2051         SELF_UNHASHED_PATHS
  2052         == frozenset(
  2053             {
  2054                 "scripts/check-ksg-phase-isolation-self-test.py",
  2055                 "scripts/check-ksg-phase-isolation.py",
  2056             }
  2057         ),
  2058         "cyclic self-unhashed inventory changed",
  2059     )
  2060     phase_functions = [
  2061         node
  2062         for node in tree.body
  2063         if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef))
  2064         and node.name == "validate_phase"
  2065     ]
  2066     require(
  2067         len(phase_functions) == 1, "checker does not uniquely define validate_phase"
  2068     )
  2069     critical_names = set(EXPECTED_CRITICAL_GATE_SEQUENCE)
  2070 
  2071     def direct_statement_call(statement: ast.stmt) -> str | None:
  2072         value: ast.expr | None = None
  2073         if isinstance(statement, ast.Expr):
  2074             value = statement.value
  2075         elif isinstance(statement, (ast.Assign, ast.AnnAssign)):
  2076             value = statement.value
  2077         if (
  2078             isinstance(value, ast.Call)
  2079             and isinstance(value.func, ast.Name)
  2080             and value.func.id in critical_names
  2081         ):
  2082             return value.func.id
  2083         return None
  2084 
  2085     observed_direct = tuple(
  2086         name
  2087         for statement in phase_functions[0].body
  2088         if (name := direct_statement_call(statement)) is not None
  2089     )
  2090     require(
  2091         observed_direct == EXPECTED_CRITICAL_GATE_SEQUENCE,
  2092         "checker direct top-level critical gate sequence changed",
  2093     )
  2094     observed_recursive = [
  2095         node.func.id
  2096         for node in ast.walk(phase_functions[0])
  2097         if isinstance(node, ast.Call)
  2098         and isinstance(node.func, ast.Name)
  2099         and node.func.id in critical_names
  2100     ]
  2101     for critical in critical_names:
  2102         require(
  2103             observed_recursive.count(critical)
  2104             == EXPECTED_CRITICAL_GATE_SEQUENCE.count(critical),
  2105             f"checker recursive critical gate inventory changed: {critical}",
  2106         )
  2107

  2109 def validate_effective_attributes(paths: Iterable[str]) -> None:
  2110     ordered = tuple(sorted(paths))
  2111     if not ordered:
  2112         return
  2113     payload = b"".join(path.encode("utf-8") + b"\0" for path in ordered)
  2114     process = git_process(
  2115         "check-attr",
  2116         "-z",
  2117         "--stdin",
  2118         "filter",
  2119         "working-tree-encoding",
  2120         input_bytes=payload,
  2121     )
  2122     fields = process.stdout.split(b"\0")
  2123     if fields and not fields[-1]:
  2124         fields.pop()
  2125     require(
  2126         len(fields) == len(ordered) * 2 * 3,
  2127         "cannot parse effective Git attributes for candidate delta",
  2128     )
  2129     for index in range(0, len(fields), 3):
  2130         path = canonical_relative_path(fields[index], label="Git attribute path")
  2131         attribute = fields[index + 1].decode("ascii", errors="strict")
  2132         value = fields[index + 2].decode("utf-8", errors="strict")
  2133         require(
  2134             value == "unspecified",
  2135             f"{path!r}: effective {attribute} attribute is forbidden ({value!r})",
  2136         )
  2137

  2139 def current_facts(
  2140     baseline: dict[str, GitEntry],
  2141     anchor: dict[str, GitEntry],
  2142     snapshot: CandidateSnapshot,
  2143     context: RepositoryContext,
  2144 ) -> dict[str, Any]:
  2145     actual_changed = changed_paths(baseline, snapshot.entries)
  2146     anchor_delta = classified_delta(anchor, snapshot.entries)
  2147     protected = tuple(sorted(set(baseline).difference(actual_changed)))
  2148     bound: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
  2149     for path in BOUND_ALLOWED_PATHS:
  2150         entry = snapshot.entries.get(path)
  2151         require(entry is not None, f"reviewed full-blob path is missing: {path}")
  2152         bound[path] = [entry.mode, entry.sha256]
  2153     return {
  2154         "allowlist_sha256": allowlist_digest(actual_changed),
  2155         "baseline_path_count": len(baseline),
  2156         "bound_allowed_blobs": bound,
  2157         "anchor_delta": [
  2158             {"path": path, "status": status_value}
  2159             for path, status_value in anchor_delta
  2160         ],
  2161         "anchor_delta_path_count": len(anchor_delta),
  2162         "changed_paths": list(actual_changed),
  2163         "changed_projection_sha256": changed_projection(
  2164             baseline, snapshot.entries, actual_changed
  2165         ),
  2166         "current_anchor": CURRENT_ANCHOR,
  2167         "current_anchor_tree": CURRENT_ANCHOR_TREE,
  2168         "current_head": snapshot.head,
  2169         "diagnostic_only": True,
  2170         "git_tcb": {
  2171             "executable": context.git_binary.executable.path,
  2172             "executable_sha256": context.git_binary.executable.sha256,
  2173             "version": context.git_binary.version,
  2174         },
  2175         "git_context": {
  2176             "common_git_dir": context.common_git_dir,
  2177             "git_dir": context.git_dir,
  2178             "info_attributes_absent": context.info_attributes_absent,
  2179             "local_config_semantics_sha256": (context.local_config_semantics_sha256),
  2180             "local_config_sha256": context.local_config.sha256,
  2181             "replacement_refs_sha256": context.replacement_refs_sha256,
  2182             "worktree_config_absent": context.worktree_config_absent,
  2183         },
  2184         "lifecycle": (
  2185             "precommit-worktree"
  2186             if snapshot.head == CURRENT_ANCHOR
  2187             else "committed-descendant"
  2188         ),
  2189         "phase_path_policy": PHASE_PATH_POLICY,
  2190         "phase_path_policy_sha256": hashlib.sha256(
  2191             read_candidate_bytes(PHASE_PATH_POLICY)
  2192         ).hexdigest(),
  2193         "precommit_tracked_modifications": list(snapshot.tracked_modifications),
  2194         "precommit_untracked_deliverables": list(snapshot.untracked),
  2195         "protected_path_count": len(protected),
  2196         "protected_projection_sha256": path_projection(baseline, protected),
  2197         "schema": "pid-rs/ksg-phase-current-facts",
  2198         "schema_revision": 1,
  2199         "self_unhashed_paths": sorted(SELF_UNHASHED_PATHS),
  2200     }

  2203 def render_tuple(name: str, values: list[str]) -> list[str]:
  2204     lines = [f"{name} = ("]
  2205     lines.extend(f"    {value!r}," for value in values)
  2206     lines.append(")")
  2207     return lines

  2210 def render_generated_block(facts: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
  2211     lines = ["# BEGIN GENERATED PHASE FACTS"]
  2212     lines.extend(
  2213         render_tuple("EXPECTED_CHANGED_PATHS: tuple[str, ...]", facts["changed_paths"])
  2214     )
  2215     lines.extend(
  2216         render_tuple(
  2217             "EXPECTED_PRECOMMIT_TRACKED_MODIFICATIONS: tuple[str, ...]",
  2218             facts["precommit_tracked_modifications"],
  2219         )
  2220     )
  2221     lines.extend(
  2222         render_tuple(
  2223             "EXPECTED_PRECOMMIT_UNTRACKED_DELIVERABLES: tuple[str, ...]",
  2224             facts["precommit_untracked_deliverables"],
  2225         )
  2226     )
  2227     lines.append(f"EXPECTED_ALLOWLIST_SHA256 = {facts['allowlist_sha256']!r}")
  2228     lines.append(
  2229         f"EXPECTED_CHANGED_PROJECTION_SHA256 = {facts['changed_projection_sha256']!r}"
  2230     )
  2231     lines.append(
  2232         "EXPECTED_PROTECTED_PROJECTION_SHA256 = "
  2233         f"{facts['protected_projection_sha256']!r}"
  2234     )
  2235     lines.append(f"EXPECTED_BASELINE_PATH_COUNT = {facts['baseline_path_count']}")
  2236     lines.append(f"EXPECTED_PROTECTED_PATH_COUNT = {facts['protected_path_count']}")
  2237     lines.append("EXPECTED_BOUND_ALLOWED_BLOBS: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {")
  2238     for path, (mode, digest) in facts["bound_allowed_blobs"].items():
  2239         lines.append(f"    {path!r}: ({mode!r}, {digest!r}),")
  2240     lines.append("}")
  2241     lines.append("# END GENERATED PHASE FACTS")
  2242     return "\n".join(lines)

  2245 def validate_phase(
  2246     *,
  2247     expected_candidate_tree: str | None,
  2248     checkpoint_commit: str | None,
  2249 ) -> tuple[str, int, int, int, int, str | None, GitBinaryIdentity]:
  2250     validate_checker_source_model()
  2251     repository_context = validate_repository_context()
  2252     snapshot = collect_candidate_snapshot()
  2253     validate_commit_envelope(snapshot.head)
  2254     baseline = hydrate_tree(parse_tree(SCIENTIFIC_BASELINE))
  2255     anchor = hydrate_tree(parse_tree(CURRENT_ANCHOR))
  2256     policy_entries = validate_phase_path_policy(snapshot, anchor)
  2257     custody = validate_staged_tree_custody(
  2258         snapshot,
  2259         expected_candidate_tree,
  2260         checkpoint_commit,
  2261     )
  2262     if snapshot.head != CURRENT_ANCHOR:
  2263         require(
  2264             expected_candidate_tree is not None and checkpoint_commit == snapshot.head,
  2265             (
  2266                 "committed lifecycle requires --expected-candidate-tree and "
  2267                 "--checkpoint-commit equal to exact HEAD"
  2268             ),
  2269         )
  2270     delivery = hydrate_tree(parse_tree(DELIVERY_PARENT))
  2271     require(
  2272         len(baseline) == EXPECTED_BASELINE_PATH_COUNT,
  2273         "scientific baseline path count changed",
  2274     )
  2275     tracked_ignore_sources = tuple(
  2276         path
  2277         for path in sorted(snapshot.entries)
  2278         if path == ".gitignore" or path.endswith("/.gitignore")
  2279     )
  2280     require(
  2281         tracked_ignore_sources == (".gitignore",),
  2282         "candidate must contain exactly one root .gitignore visibility source",
  2283     )
  2284 
  2285     delivery_changed = changed_paths(baseline, delivery)
  2286     require(
  2287         delivery_changed == tuple(sorted(DELIVERY_CHANGED_BLOBS)),
  2288         "delivery commit changed-path envelope mismatch",
  2289     )
  2290     for path, (mode, digest) in DELIVERY_CHANGED_BLOBS.items():
  2291         entry = delivery.get(path)
  2292         require(
  2293             entry is not None and (entry.mode, entry.sha256) == (mode, digest),
  2294             f"delivery commit blob pin mismatch: {path}",
  2295         )
  2296 
  2297     actual_changed = changed_paths(baseline, snapshot.entries)
  2298     require(
  2299         allowlist_digest(EXPECTED_CHANGED_PATHS) == EXPECTED_ALLOWLIST_SHA256,
  2300         "reviewed allowlist digest does not match checker constants",
  2301     )
  2302     require(
  2303         actual_changed == EXPECTED_CHANGED_PATHS,
  2304         "candidate changed-path set differs from the exact KSG allowlist",
  2305     )
  2306     require(
  2307         changed_projection(baseline, snapshot.entries, actual_changed)
  2308         == EXPECTED_CHANGED_PROJECTION_SHA256,
  2309         "candidate changed-byte projection digest mismatch",
  2310     )
  2311 
  2312     protected = tuple(sorted(set(baseline).difference(EXPECTED_CHANGED_PATHS)))
  2313     require(
  2314         len(protected) == EXPECTED_PROTECTED_PATH_COUNT,
  2315         "protected path count changed",
  2316     )
  2317     require(
  2318         path_projection(baseline, protected) == EXPECTED_PROTECTED_PROJECTION_SHA256,
  2319         "scientific-baseline protected projection pin mismatch",
  2320     )
  2321     for path in protected:
  2322         left = baseline[path]
  2323         right = snapshot.entries.get(path)
  2324         require(
  2325             right is not None
  2326             and (right.mode, right.kind, right.sha256)
  2327             == (left.mode, left.kind, left.sha256),
  2328             f"protected path mode/type/blob changed: {path}",
  2329         )
  2330     for path, (mode, digest) in PINNED_PROTECTED_BLOBS.items():
  2331         baseline_entry = baseline.get(path)
  2332         candidate_entry = snapshot.entries.get(path)
  2333         require(
  2334             baseline_entry is not None
  2335             and (baseline_entry.mode, baseline_entry.sha256) == (mode, digest),
  2336             f"pinned protected baseline fact mismatch: {path}",
  2337         )
  2338         require(
  2339             candidate_entry is not None
  2340             and (candidate_entry.mode, candidate_entry.sha256) == (mode, digest),
  2341             f"pinned protected candidate blob changed: {path}",
  2342         )
  2343 
  2344     require(
  2345         set(EXPECTED_BOUND_ALLOWED_BLOBS) == set(BOUND_ALLOWED_PATHS),
  2346         "reviewed full-blob pin inventory does not match its path inventory",
  2347     )
  2348     for path, expected in EXPECTED_BOUND_ALLOWED_BLOBS.items():
  2349         entry = snapshot.entries.get(path)
  2350         require(
  2351             entry is not None and (entry.mode, entry.sha256) == expected,
  2352             f"reviewed full candidate blob changed: {path}",
  2353         )
  2354 
  2355     if snapshot.head == CURRENT_ANCHOR:
  2356         lifecycle = "precommit-worktree"
  2357         require(
  2358             snapshot.tracked_modifications == EXPECTED_PRECOMMIT_TRACKED_MODIFICATIONS,
  2359             "precommit tracked-modification partition changed",
  2360         )
  2361         require(
  2362             snapshot.untracked == EXPECTED_PRECOMMIT_UNTRACKED_DELIVERABLES,
  2363             "precommit untracked-deliverable partition changed",
  2364         )
  2365     else:
  2366         lifecycle = "committed-descendant"
  2367         require(
  2368             not snapshot.tracked_modifications and not snapshot.untracked,
  2369             "committed phase requires a clean tracked/untracked worktree",
  2370         )
  2371 
  2372     validate_effective_attributes(entry.path for entry in policy_entries)
  2373     validate_changed_path_firewall(actual_changed)
  2374     validate_stats_firewall()
  2375     validate_parallel_semantics()
  2376     validate_release_firewall()
  2377     validate_identity_firewall()
  2378 
  2379     replay_context = validate_repository_context()
  2380     replay = collect_candidate_snapshot()
  2381     replay_custody = validate_staged_tree_custody(
  2382         replay,
  2383         expected_candidate_tree,
  2384         checkpoint_commit,
  2385     )
  2386     require(
  2387         replay_context == repository_context,
  2388         "Git executable, configuration, metadata, or visibility context changed during replay",
  2389     )
  2390     require(
  2391         replay == snapshot, "candidate filesystem or Git inputs changed during replay"
  2392     )
  2393     require(
  2394         replay_custody == custody, "external staged-tree custody changed during replay"
  2395     )
  2396     return (
  2397         lifecycle,
  2398         len(actual_changed),
  2399         len(protected),
  2400         len(snapshot.tracked_modifications),
  2401         len(snapshot.untracked),
  2402         custody[0],
  2403         repository_context.git_binary,
  2404     )
  2405 
  2406 
  2407 DESCRIPTION = """\
  2408 Validate KSG revision-4 Git phase provenance on the Git-visible candidate
  2409 snapshot (HEAD-tracked files plus untracked deliverables not excluded by the
  2410 exact protected root .gitignore).
  2411 
  2412 On success this proves only the pinned baseline -> delivery -> formal-anchor
  2413 single-parent envelope, the exact reviewed candidate delta, byte/mode/type
  2414 identity of protected paths, complete-byte pins for reviewed high-risk paths,
  2415 exact anchor/absent -> final-byte monotonicity of every reachable post-anchor
  2416 tree, and the bounded KSG-vs-later-wave firewall encoded here.
  2417 
  2418 It does NOT prove arithmetic, formal-statement adequacy, Rust/compiler
  2419 conformance, estimator accuracy, support assumptions, PID validity,
  2420 statistical calibration, publication quality, remote/push state,
  2421 authenticity, trustworthiness of the identified Git executable, or absence of
  2422 hash collisions. Every path ignored by the protected root .gitignore,
  2423 including credentials, secrets, build products, caches, and editor state, is
  2424 outside the candidate snapshot; local info/exclude bytes are deliberately not
  2425 an input. No gate may silently depend on an ignored path. The checker and
  2426 self-test bytes are intentionally outside the self-stored digest projection.
  2427 Use the external tree/commit hooks to bind them to a separately reviewed
  2428 staged tree; that custody is still not an authenticity proof.
  2429 """
  2430 
  2431 
  2432 def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
  2433     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
  2434         description=DESCRIPTION,
  2435         formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
  2436     )
  2437     group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
  2438     group.add_argument(
  2439         "--emit-current-facts-json",
  2440         action="store_true",
  2441         help=(
  2442             "print canonical diagnostic facts for the current snapshot; this "
  2443             "does not validate the reviewed constants"
  2444         ),
  2445     )
  2446     group.add_argument(

  2448         action="store_true",
  2449         help=(
  2450             "print a mechanically replaceable generated-constant block; this "

  2452         ),

  2454     parser.add_argument(
  2455         "--expected-candidate-tree",
  2456         metavar="TREE",
  2457         help=(
  2458             "require the complete candidate snapshot, including the two "
  2459             "self-unhashed scripts, to equal this externally created Git tree"
  2460         ),
  2461     )
  2462     parser.add_argument(
  2463         "--checkpoint-commit",
  2464         metavar="COMMIT",
  2465         help=(
  2466             "additionally require this detached checkpoint commit to carry "
  2467             "the supplied candidate tree and be HEAD or an exact child of HEAD"
  2468         ),
  2469     )
  2470     return parser.parse_args()

  2473 def main() -> int:
  2474     args = parse_args()
  2475     try:
  2476         if args.emit_current_facts_json or args.emit_current_facts_python:
  2477             validate_checker_source_model()
  2478             context = validate_repository_context()
  2479             snapshot = collect_candidate_snapshot()
  2480             validate_commit_envelope(snapshot.head)
  2481             baseline = hydrate_tree(parse_tree(SCIENTIFIC_BASELINE))
  2482             anchor = hydrate_tree(parse_tree(CURRENT_ANCHOR))
  2483             validate_phase_path_policy(snapshot, anchor)
  2484             validate_staged_tree_custody(
  2485                 snapshot,
  2486                 args.expected_candidate_tree,
  2487                 args.checkpoint_commit,
  2488             )
  2489             facts = current_facts(baseline, anchor, snapshot, context)
  2490             if args.emit_current_facts_json:
  2491                 print(json.dumps(facts, indent=2, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=True))
  2492             else:
  2493                 print(render_generated_block(facts))
  2494             return 0
  2495         (
  2496             lifecycle,
  2497             changed,
  2498             protected,
  2499             tracked,
  2500             untracked,
  2501             candidate_tree,
  2502             git_binary,
  2503         ) = validate_phase(
  2504             expected_candidate_tree=args.expected_candidate_tree,
  2505             checkpoint_commit=args.checkpoint_commit,
  2506         )
  2507     except PhaseIsolationError as error:
  2508         print(f"ERROR: KSG phase isolation: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
  2509         return 1
  2510     print(
  2511         "OK: KSG phase provenance only; "
  2512         f"lifecycle={lifecycle}; changed={changed}; protected={protected}; "
  2513         f"tracked-worktree={tracked}; untracked-deliverables={untracked}; "
  2514         f"baseline={SCIENTIFIC_BASELINE}; delivery={DELIVERY_PARENT}; "
  2515         f"anchor={CURRENT_ANCHOR}; self-unhashed={len(SELF_UNHASHED_PATHS)}; "
  2516         f"candidate-tree={candidate_tree or 'not-requested'}; "
  2517         f"git={git_binary.executable.path}; "
  2518         f"git-sha256={git_binary.executable.sha256}; "
  2519         f"git-version={git_binary.version!r}. "
  2520         "No arithmetic, estimator, PID, statistical, remote, or authenticity "
  2521         "claim is implied."
  2522     )
  2523     return 0
  2524 
  2525 
  2526 if __name__ == "__main__":
  2527     raise SystemExit(main())
  2528

   108 def mask_lean_comments_and_strings(text: str) -> str:
   109     masked = list(text)
   110     index = 0
   111     block_depth = 0
   112     in_string = False
   113     while index < len(text):
   114         if block_depth:
   115             if text.startswith("/-", index):
   116                 masked[index : index + 2] = (" ", " ")
   117                 block_depth += 1
   118                 index += 2
   119             elif text.startswith("-/", index):
   120                 masked[index : index + 2] = (" ", " ")
   121                 block_depth -= 1
   122                 index += 2
   123             else:
   124                 if text[index] != "\n":
   125                     masked[index] = " "
   126                 index += 1
   127         elif in_string:
   128             if text[index] == "\\":
   129                 masked[index] = " "
   130                 index += 1
   131                 if index < len(text):
   132                     if text[index] != "\n":
   133                         masked[index] = " "
   134                     index += 1
   135             elif text[index] == '"':
   136                 masked[index] = " "
   137                 in_string = False
   138                 index += 1
   139             else:
   140                 if text[index] != "\n":
   141                     masked[index] = " "
   142                 index += 1
   143         elif text.startswith("/-", index):
   144             masked[index : index + 2] = (" ", " ")
   145             block_depth = 1
   146             index += 2
   147         elif text.startswith("--", index):
   148             while index < len(text) and text[index] != "\n":
   149                 masked[index] = " "
   150                 index += 1
   151         elif text[index] == '"':
   152             masked[index] = " "
   153             in_string = True
   154             index += 1
   155         else:
   156             index += 1
   157     require(block_depth == 0, "Lean source contains an unterminated block comment")
   158     require(not in_string, "Lean source contains an unterminated string")
   159     return "".join(masked)

   162 def parse_axiom_inventory(output: str) -> dict[str, frozenset[str]]:
   163     pattern = re.compile(
   164         r"'([^']+)' (?:depends on axioms: \[(.*?)\]|does not depend on any axioms)",
   165         re.DOTALL,
   166     )
   167     inventory: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {}
   168     for match in pattern.finditer(output):
   169         payload = match.group(2)
   170         axioms = (
   171             frozenset()
   172             if payload is None
   173             else frozenset(part.strip() for part in payload.split(",") if part.strip())
   174         )
   175         inventory[match.group(1)] = axioms
   176     return inventory

   275 def verify_environment_and_source() -> tuple[str, str]:
   276     require(sha256(SOURCE) == EXPECTED_SOURCE_SHA256, "Lean source digest drifted")

   293     )
   294     require(

   296         "Lean toolchain file digest drifted",
   297     )
   298     require(

   300         "Lake configuration digest drifted",
   301     )
   302     require(
   303         (PROJECT / "lean-toolchain").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
   304         == EXPECTED_TOOLCHAIN,
   305         "Lean toolchain identifier drifted",
   306     )
   307     verify_dependency_checkouts()

   309     source_text = SOURCE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
   310     imports = tuple(
   311         line for line in source_text.splitlines() if line.startswith("import ")
   312     )
   313     require(imports == EXPECTED_IMPORTS, f"Lean import inventory drifted: {imports}")
   314     source_code = mask_lean_comments_and_strings(source_text)
   315     require(
   316         PROHIBITED_SOURCE.search(source_code) is None,
   317         "Lean source contains a prohibited proof escape",

   319     for sentinel in REQUIRED_SCOPE_SENTINELS:
   320         require(sentinel in source_text, f"Lean scope sentinel is absent: {sentinel}")
   321     for theorem in THEOREMS:
   322         short_name = theorem.rsplit(".", maxsplit=1)[1]
   323         require(
   324             len(re.findall(rf"\btheorem\s+{re.escape(short_name)}\b", source_code))
   325             == 1,
   326             f"Lean theorem declaration is absent or ambiguous: {theorem}",

   329     lake = shutil.which("lake")

   331     version = subprocess.run(

   337         check=False,

   341     require(not version.stderr, f"Lean version probe emitted stderr: {version.stderr}")
   342     require("Lean (version 4.32.0" in version.stdout, "unexpected Lean version")
   343     require(

   350 def main() -> int:

   358             + "\n"

   360         with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="pid-ksg-harmonic-lean-") as directory:
   361             query_path = Path(directory) / "PidKsgIntegerHarmonicCheck.lean"

   370         inventory = parse_axiom_inventory(checked.stdout)
   371         require(set(inventory) == set(THEOREMS), "Lean theorem axiom inventory changed")
   372         for theorem, axioms in inventory.items():

   388             "lean_toolchain": EXPECTED_TOOLCHAIN,

   391             "permitted_axioms": sorted(PERMITTED_AXIOMS),
   392             "axiom_inventory": {
   393                 theorem: sorted(inventory[theorem]) for theorem in THEOREMS
   394             },
   395             "typed_unproved_premise": (
   396                 "PositiveIntegerDigammaPremise: for each positive integer m used, "
   397                 "psi(m)=H_(m-1)-eulerConstant"
   398             ),
   399             "boundary": (
   400                 "Exact finite-sum/monotonicity/cancellation/index/range/symmetry, rational-tail "
   401                 "bounds, and the explicit rational-to-real bounded-combination theorem only. "
   402                 "The analytic digamma premise, count geometry, binary64, estimators, support, "
   403                 "PID semantics, Rust refinement, calibration, and consumers remain outside scope."
   404             ),

   406         print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))
   407         return 0

```text
     1 #!/usr/bin/env python3
     2 """Check separately encoded exact KSG harmonic/index obligations with pinned Z3.
     3 
     4 The SMT route proves four-term cancellation under explicit positive-integer digamma instances,
     5 the min/max range identity and source symmetry for an arbitrary harmonic-value function, the
     6 exclusive/inclusive index maps, and the local full-tail bound under explicit harmonic-order
     7 instances. It does not prove the digamma premise, define or prove monotonicity of harmonic finite
     8 sums, or establish neighbor geometry, estimator behavior, support, floating point, PID semantics,
     9 or Rust refinement. The finite-sum definition, recurrence, monotonicity, and unconditional
    10 rational harmonic bound are checked separately by Lean.
    11 """
    12 
    13 from __future__ import annotations
    14 
    15 from dataclasses import dataclass
    16 import hashlib
    17 import json
    18 import os
    19 from pathlib import Path
    20 import shutil
    21 import subprocess
    22 import sys

    27 PROOF_DIR = ROOT / "audit/formal/z3-ksg-harmonic"
    28 EXPECTED_Z3_VERSION = "Z3 version 4.16.0 - 64 bit"
    29 TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30
    30 COUNTEREXAMPLE_ASSERTION = b"(assert (not theorem_holds))"
    31 POSITIVE_ASSERTION = b"(assert theorem_holds)"

    34 class Z3KsgHarmonicError(RuntimeError):
    35     """A source, pin, satisfiability preflight, or exact UNSAT check failed."""
    36 
    37 
    38 @dataclass(frozen=True)
    39 class ProofSpec:
    40     filename: str
    41     sha256: str
    42     obligation: str
    43     typed_premise: str
    44

    46 PROOFS = (

    48         filename="ksg-digamma-cancellation.smt2",
    49         sha256="8ae66c11fb66541bc47766b2682cf1e53d9b656aa0fa12e6945ac22057816ed4",
    50         obligation="four-term exact-real cancellation at four positive integer arguments",
    51         typed_premise=(
    52             "four asserted instances psi(m)=harmonic(m-1)-euler_constant; analytic truth open"
    53         ),
    54     ),
    55     ProofSpec(
    56         filename="ksg-index-maps.smt2",
    57         sha256="71ea8db97df43f51da89496a5e799bedc6216f9ede40368207d2ffed8df40fe1",
    58         obligation="exclusive count+1 and anchor-inclusive identity maps with exact domains",
    59         typed_premise="declared integer count bounds; neighbor production and geometry open",
    60     ),
    61     ProofSpec(
    62         filename="ksg-local-bound-v4.smt2",
    63         sha256="33c9bb7a13c9e8c0cc88ca1750b9510481b3f64ea4ecac8c7497e16d6850df31",
    64         obligation=(
    65             "direct/range equality and full-tail bound under explicit local harmonic-order premises"
    66         ),
    67         typed_premise=(
    68             "H(k-1)<=H(min-1)<=H(max-1)<=H(n-1); universal harmonic monotonicity is proved in Lean"
    69         ),
    70     ),
    71     ProofSpec(
    72         filename="ksg-symmetric-range.smt2",
    73         sha256="add0fc3a371c65433fdfd8b1e51d3182c6ef78db0cfd1d372f461f1d030e19a9",
    74         obligation="min/max range reassociation and source exchange for arbitrary harmonic values",
    75         typed_premise="positive integer index order only; harmonic values are uninterpreted",
    76     ),
    77 )
    78 
    79 
    80 def file_sha256(raw: bytes) -> str:
    81     return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
    82 
    83 
    84 def require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    85     if not condition:
    86         raise Z3KsgHarmonicError(message)
    87 
    88 
    89 def find_z3(explicit: str | None = None) -> Path:
    90     candidate = explicit if explicit is not None else shutil.which("z3")
    91     require(candidate is not None, "z3 executable was not found on PATH")
    92     path = Path(candidate).expanduser().resolve()
    93     require(
    94         path.is_file() and os.access(path, os.X_OK), f"z3 is not executable: {path}"
    95     )
    96     return path
    97 
    98 
    99 def z3_version(z3: Path) -> str:
   100     process = subprocess.run(
   101         [str(z3), "--version"],
   102         capture_output=True,
   103         text=True,
   104         timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   105         check=False,
   106     )
   107     require(
   108         process.returncode == 0
   109         and process.stdout == EXPECTED_Z3_VERSION + "\n"
   110         and process.stderr == "",
   111         "unexpected z3 version result: "
   112         f"exit={process.returncode}, stdout={process.stdout!r}, stderr={process.stderr!r}",
   113     )
   114     return process.stdout.strip()
   115 
   116 
   117 def require_exact_proof_set() -> None:
   118     require(
   119         PROOF_DIR.is_dir() and not PROOF_DIR.is_symlink(),
   120         f"proof directory is missing or symlinked: {PROOF_DIR}",
   121     )
   122     expected = {spec.filename for spec in PROOFS}
   123     actual = {entry.name for entry in PROOF_DIR.iterdir()}
   124     require(
   125         actual == expected,
   126         f"proof manifest mismatch: missing={sorted(expected - actual)}, "
   127         f"unexpected={sorted(actual - expected)}",
   128     )
   129 
   130 
   131 def validate_proof_source(path: Path, expected_sha256: str) -> bytes:
   132     require(
   133         path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink(), f"proof is not a regular file: {path}"
   134     )
   135     raw = path.read_bytes()
   136     require(
   137         file_sha256(raw) == expected_sha256,
   138         f"proof digest mismatch for {path.name}: got {file_sha256(raw)}",
   139     )
   140     try:
   141         source = raw.decode("utf-8", errors="strict")
   142     except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
   143         raise Z3KsgHarmonicError(f"proof is not UTF-8: {path}") from error
   144     required_counts = {
   145         "(set-logic QF_UFLIRA)": 1,
   146         "(define-fun theorem_holds () Bool": 1,
   147         COUNTEREXAMPLE_ASSERTION.decode("ascii"): 1,
   148         "(check-sat)": 1,
   149         "(exit)": 1,
   150     }
   151     for marker, expected_count in required_counts.items():
   152         require(
   153             source.count(marker) == expected_count,
   154             f"{path.name}: expected {expected_count} occurrence of {marker!r}, "
   155             f"got {source.count(marker)}",
   156         )
   157     forbidden = (
   158         "(forall",
   159         "(exists",
   160         "(check-sat-assuming",
   161         "(get-model",
   162         "(get-proof",
   163         "(include",
   164         "(push",
   165         "(pop",
   166         "(reset",
   167     )
   168     present = [marker for marker in forbidden if marker in source]
   169     require(not present, f"{path.name} contains forbidden solver commands: {present}")
   170     require("(assert" in source, f"{path.name} contains no assertion")
   171     return raw
   172 
   173 
   174 def run_z3(z3: Path, proof: Path) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
   175     return subprocess.run(
   176         [str(z3), "-smt2", str(proof)],
   177         capture_output=True,
   178         text=True,
   179         timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   180         check=False,
   181     )
   182 
   183 
   184 def require_exact_result(
   185     process: subprocess.CompletedProcess[str],
   186     expected: str,
   187     label: str,
   188 ) -> None:
   189     require(
   190         process.returncode == 0
   191         and process.stdout == expected + "\n"
   192         and process.stderr == "",
   193         f"{label} did not return exact {expected.upper()}: "
   194         f"exit={process.returncode}, stdout={process.stdout!r}, stderr={process.stderr!r}",
   195     )
   196 
   197 
   198 def require_unsat(z3: Path, proof: Path) -> None:
   199     require_exact_result(run_z3(z3, proof), "unsat", proof.name)
   200 
   201 
   202 def require_satisfiable_positive_preflight(z3: Path, path: Path, raw: bytes) -> None:
   203     require(
   204         raw.count(COUNTEREXAMPLE_ASSERTION) == 1,
   205         f"{path.name}: counterexample assertion is absent or ambiguous",
   206     )
   207     positive = raw.replace(COUNTEREXAMPLE_ASSERTION, POSITIVE_ASSERTION, 1)
   208     with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="pid-ksg-z3-positive-") as directory:
   209         candidate = Path(directory) / path.name
   210         candidate.write_bytes(positive)
   211         require_exact_result(
   212             run_z3(z3, candidate), "sat", f"{path.name} positive preflight"
   213         )
   214 
   215 
   216 def verify_all(z3: Path) -> str:
   217     version = z3_version(z3)
   218     require_exact_proof_set()
   219     for spec in PROOFS:
   220         path = PROOF_DIR / spec.filename
   221         raw = validate_proof_source(path, spec.sha256)
   222         require_satisfiable_positive_preflight(z3, path, raw)
   223         require_unsat(z3, path)
   224     return version
   225 
   226 
   227 def main() -> int:
   228     try:
   229         z3 = find_z3()
   230         version = verify_all(z3)
   231         result = {
   232             "schema": "pid-rs/z3-ksg-integer-harmonic-check/v2",
   233             "status": "passed",
   234             "z3_version": version,
   235             "checker_source_sha256": file_sha256(Path(__file__).resolve().read_bytes()),
   236             "proofs": [
   237                 {
   238                     "filename": spec.filename,
   239                     "sha256": spec.sha256,
   240                     "obligation": spec.obligation,
   241                     "typed_premise": spec.typed_premise,
   242                     "positive_preflight": "sat",
   243                     "negated_obligation": "unsat",
   244                 }
   245                 for spec in PROOFS
   246             ],
   247             "boundary": (
   248                 "Quantifier-free exact Int/Real/uninterpreted-function obligations only. The "
   249                 "local bound uses explicit harmonic-order premises; finite-sum recurrence and "
   250                 "universal rational harmonic monotonicity are separately kernel-checked in Lean; "
   251                 "the statements, signs, maps, and analytic premise remain shared human cuts. "
   252                 "Digamma truth, count geometry, binary64, estimators, support, PID semantics, "
   253                 "Rust refinement, calibration, and consumers remain outside scope."
   254             ),
   255         }
   256         print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))
   257         return 0
   258     except (
   259         OSError,
   260         subprocess.SubprocessError,
   261         Z3KsgHarmonicError,
   262     ) as error:
   263         print(f"Z3 KSG integer-harmonic check failed: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
   264         return 1
   265 
   266 
   267 if __name__ == "__main__":
   268     raise SystemExit(main())
   269 
```

## Pattern excerpt: README.md

Whole-file SHA-256: `35350882ed54700fb8639bb9b251fadc0589b31bdc75efe315ee805f3928ad25`; bytes: 63485

```text
42-It also supplies diagnostics and statistics needed to assess a result: geometry checks, Shannon
43-invariants, explicitly declared resampling distributions, typed permutation/surrogate nulls,
44-multiple-testing correction, preprocessing, and structured run-logs. Generic resampling summaries
45-are descriptive unless a statistic-specific calibration theorem is supplied. The estimator core is
46-safe Rust (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`) and reports all information quantities in nats.
47-
48-## Method provenance and claim boundary
49-
50-**“New in pid-rs” means an implementation, API, composition, diagnostic, or engineering contribution
51-new to this repository; it is not a claim of scientific novelty.** The exhaustive, versioned map
52-from methods to papers, external reference code, Rust/Python entry points, feature gates, repository
53-contributions, and unsupported requests is [`METHODS.md`](METHODS.md). Its machine-readable source
54-is [`method-catalog.json`](method-catalog.json).
55-
56:The [ecosystem capability and gap matrix](ECOSYSTEM_CAPABILITIES.md) projects this catalog and the
57-assurance registry onto four exact historical consumer snapshots. Its
58:[machine-readable contract](ecosystem-capabilities.json) records retained boundaries and missing
59-evidence. Every consumer integration remains `not_claimed`. The matrix does not establish current
60-compatibility, integration, qualification, operational validation, or application validity.
61-
62-The catalog uses these distinctions consistently:
63-
64-| Label | Meaning |
65-|---|---|
66-| Paper-defined | The mathematical quantity or estimator is defined in a cited publication. |
67-| Paper-derived | pid-rs composes published quantities or algorithms; the composition itself may have no dedicated paper or theorem. |
68-| Project-defined | The diagnostic, contract, report, or workflow is specified by this repository and is not presented as a published mathematical method. |
69-| External reference code | A cited authors' or independent implementation is used for bounded comparison; it is not vendored or silently treated as proof. |
70-| No implementation | The request is explicitly unsupported; no feature flag or status label implies hidden code. |
71-
72-Selected boundaries that are easy to confuse:
```

10-- **Paper-derived** means the implementation composes or adapts published components; the exact composition is not asserted to be a published estimator.
11-- **Project-defined** means a local diagnostic, workflow, API contract, adapter, or software facility.
12-- **Implementation origin** is `local-implementation` for code written in this repository, `binding` for a language wrapper, `external` for pinned validation-only code, and `not-implemented` for an explicit negative capability.
13-- For software references, the displayed year is the year of the pinned validation revision, not a claim about project inception.
14-- **`depends_on` semantics:** depends_on lists curated method-level dependencies whose estimand, implementation, or scientific status materially constrains the row; it is not an exhaustive source-level call graph. Stable rows may depend only on stable rows; experimental software can compose a research-only estimator only when the stricter scientific boundary is explicit in its constraints.
15-- **Rust entry-point semantics:** Rust entry points are curated public call sites for each scientific row, not an exhaustive API inventory. release-scope-1.0.json is authoritative for the complete exported-symbol set and its feature/stability boundary.
16-- **Python entry-point semantics:** Python entry points record callable, class, and policy-attribute availability. The pid_core_rs.experimental.migration surface is exhaustively inventoried in its software row; configurable wrappers may appear on multiple scientific rows, and that prefix denotes an experimental compatibility surface rather than the stability of the wrapped Rust family. cargo_features records pid-core gates; binding rows state the separate pid-python build feature in their constraints.
17-- **New in pid-rs** describes repository engineering and packaging only. Every row records `scientific_novelty_claim = none`.
18-- Validation levels are bounded evidence labels. Reference agreement, tests, and formal checks do not establish universal statistical or application validity.

The 8-epsilon rounded-reference comparator is not exact-rational error, an ULP claim, or a universal error theorem. The exact-rational enclosure trusts Python Decimal directed-rounding semantics; its exact Fraction containment cross-check covers the 6,920 exhaustive rows, while the 1,278 stress rows retain Decimal semantics as a computational premise. The Python binary64 replay does not prove Rust-source or compiled-binary refinement, portable identity, neighbor counts, population support, estimator consistency, the surrounding composition, an Ehrlich or Makkeh--Gutknecht--Wibral functional, PID atoms, or application assumptions; not every scalar exposed by a transitive surface changes. Lean and Z3 share the typed analytic digamma premise, human signs and index maps, and selected statements; neither formalizes Rust or binary64. The modular zero classification is corpus-only, and the three selected primes provide redundant fault diversity rather than CRT reconstruction or independent proofs. Same-repository digests, reviewed prose bytes, and no-write replay establish internal correspondence, not artifact authenticity or scientific truth.",
888:        "scope": "Gaussian closed forms, serial/parallel parity, support rejection, cancellation, and report coherence. Where this surface emits or composes an eligible KSG, Ehrlich shared-exclusions, or PID term, its integer-harmonic dependency is checked by the revision-4 exact 6,920-tuple route and the schema-revision-2 8,198-row 80-digit Decimal corpus with 354 structural exact-zero endpoints. On that frozen corpus, a separately implemented Python reproduction of the selected Neumaier-prefix/sorted-range binary64 association has two distinct reference results: its maximum difference from binary64(stored Decimal prefix text) is 8 * f64::EPSILON nats with 40 ties, while a 160-digit directed enclosure of the exact harmonic rational proves a unique maximum at zero-based row 7,673 with upper bound below 9.761311 * f64::EPSILON nats. Both are below the reviewed finite-corpus ceiling of 32 * f64::EPSILON nats. Exact-rounded 80-digit references differ textually on 6,509 rows and numerically on 5,934 rows, yet all 8,198 pairs convert to the same binary64 value. The exact-enclosure route checks exact Fraction containment on all 6,920 exhaustive rows and kills 29/29 registered mutations in normal and optimized Python. The revision-4 formal route kernel-checks 19 scoped Lean theorems and solver-checks four conditional Z3 obligations; the modular certificate classifies exact rational zeros only on the frozen 8,198-row corpus."

2738:        "scope": "Local-min formula identity, source symmetry across all three baselines, finite smoke checks, and shared shell rejection. On that frozen corpus, a separately implemented Python reproduction of the selected Neumaier-prefix/sorted-range binary64 association has two distinct reference results: its maximum difference from binary64(stored Decimal prefix text) is 8 * f64::EPSILON nats with 40 ties, while a 160-digit directed enclosure of the exact harmonic rational proves a unique maximum at zero-based row 7,673 with upper bound below 9.761311 * f64::EPSILON nats. Both are below the reviewed finite-corpus ceiling of 32 * f64::EPSILON nats. Exact-rounded 80-digit references differ textually on 6,509 rows and numerically on 5,934 rows, yet all 8,198 pairs convert to the same binary64 value. The exact-enclosure route checks exact Fraction containment on all 6,920 exhaustive rows and kills 29/29 registered mutations in normal and optimized Python. The revision-4 formal route kernel-checks 19 scoped Lean theorems and solver-checks four conditional Z3 obligations; the modular certificate classifies exact rational zeros only on the frozen 8,198-row corpus."

The outer box is not asserted to equal the runtime unique-shell image. Two finite-corpus comparators are intentionally distinct. First, the Python reproduction of the selected binary64 association differs from binary64(stored 80-digit Decimal prefix text) by at most 8 * f64::EPSILON nats; exactly 40 rows attain that maximum, first at zero-based row 7,598 with tuple (4,096, 1, 2,048, 2,048). This is the binary64-rounded-reference comparator. Second, 160-digit ROUND_FLOOR/ROUND_CEILING harmonic-prefix enclosures prove that the selected binary64 error against the exact harmonic rational has a unique maximum at zero-based row 7,673 with tuple (4,096, 4, 2,049, 2,049) and is strictly below 9.761311 * f64::EPSILON nats. Both observations are below the frozen absolute 32 * f64::EPSILON-nat review ceiling. The exact-rounded 80-digit Decimal vector differs from the stored prefix text on 6,509 rows and differs numerically on 5,934 rows, while all 8,198 binary64 conversions agree. All 6,920 exhaustive small rows additionally have exact Fraction containment witnesses. The exact-enclosure checker passes in normal and -O modes; its baseline-first self-test rejects 29 of 29 load-bearing mutations in each mode. The selected route has zero source-swap bit asymmetries and 354 canonical positive-zero structural endpoints with zero negative zeros, split 240/114 between exhaustive and stress rows. The modular certificate classifies exact zero versus nonzero only on the frozen rows; its three selected primes are redundant fault-diversity lanes, not a CRT theorem, and its baseline-first self-test rejects 28 of 28 registered faults in normal and -O modes. The two comparators share the digest-bound fixture and row order, exact harmonic identity, count maps, symbolic endpoint branch, and selected Python association; the exact-rational lane additionally trusts Python Decimal directed-rounding semantics and this host's Python binary64 operations. The exact-enclosure route does not inspect Rust source or a compiled binary. Neither observation is a ULP count, universal or cross-platform bound, Rust conformance result, neighbor-count proof, estimator validation, support result, continuous shared-exclusions or PID theorem, calibration result, or application qualification. 5202-            "claim": "Eligible positive-integer (+1,+1,-1,-1) local terms use a deterministic Neumaier-compensated shifted harmonic prefix and source-symmetric two-range association. The frozen schema-2 corpus has 8,198 unique ordered rows: 6,920 exhaustive rectangular-arithmetic outer-box rows through n=16 and 1,278 declared stress rows through n=1,000,000. The outer box is not asserted to equal the runtime unique-shell image. Two finite-corpus comparators are intentionally distinct. First, the Python reproduction of the selected binary64 association differs from binary64(stored 80-digit Decimal prefix text) by at most 8 * f64::EPSILON nats; exactly 40 rows attain that maximum, first at zero-based row 7,598 with tuple (4,096, 1, 2,048, 2,048). This is the binary64-rounded-reference comparator. Second, 160-digit ROUND_FLOOR/ROUND_CEILING harmonic-prefix enclosures prove that the selected binary64 error against the exact harmonic rational has a unique maximum at zero-based row 7,673 with tuple (4,096, 4, 2,049, 2,049) and is strictly below 9.761311 * f64::EPSILON nats. Both observations are below the frozen absolute 32 * f64::EPSILON-nat review ceiling. The exact-rounded 80-digit Decimal vector differs from the stored prefix text on 6,509 rows and differs numerically on 5,934 rows, while all 8,198 binary64 conversions agree. All 6,920 exhaustive small rows additionally have exact Fraction containment witnesses. The exact-enclosure checker passes in normal and -O modes; its baseline-first self-test rejects 29 of 29 load-bearing mutations in each mode. The selected route has zero source-swap bit asymmetries and 354 canonical positive-zero structural endpoints with zero negative zeros, split 240/114 between exhaustive and stress rows. The modular certificate classifies exact zero versus nonzero only on the frozen rows; its three selected primes are redundant fault-diversity lanes, not a CRT theorem, and its baseline-first self-test rejects 28 of 28 registered faults in normal and -O modes. The two comparators share the digest-bound fixture and row order, exact harmonic identity, count maps, symbolic endpoint branch, and selected Python association; the exact-rational lane additionally trusts Python Decimal directed-rounding semantics and this host's Python binary64 operations. The exact-enclosure route does not inspect Rust source or a compiled binary. Neither observation is a ULP count, universal or cross-platform bound, Rust conformance result, neighbor-count proof, estimator validation, support result, continuous shared-exclusions or PID theorem, calibration result, or application qualification. Repository/publication integration remains NO-GO pending complete isolated-tree closure.",

The outer box is not asserted to equal the runtime unique-shell image. Two finite-corpus comparators are intentionally distinct. First, the Python reproduction of the selected binary64 association differs from binary64(stored 80-digit Decimal prefix text) by at most 8 * f64::EPSILON nats; exactly 40 rows attain that maximum, first at zero-based row 7,598 with tuple (4,096, 1, 2,048, 2,048). This is the binary64-rounded-reference comparator. Second, 160-digit ROUND_FLOOR/ROUND_CEILING harmonic-prefix enclosures prove that the selected binary64 error against the exact harmonic rational has a unique maximum at zero-based row 7,673 with tuple (4,096, 4, 2,049, 2,049) and is strictly below 9.761311 * f64::EPSILON nats. Both observations are below the frozen absolute 32 * f64::EPSILON-nat review ceiling. The exact-rounded 80-digit Decimal vector differs from the stored prefix text on 6,509 rows and differs numerically on 5,934 rows, while all 8,198 binary64 conversions agree. All 6,920 exhaustive small rows additionally have exact Fraction containment witnesses. The exact-enclosure checker passes in normal and -O modes; its baseline-first self-test rejects 29 of 29 load-bearing mutations in each mode. The selected route has zero source-swap bit asymmetries and 354 canonical positive-zero structural endpoints with zero negative zeros, split 240/114 between exhaustive and stress rows. The modular certificate classifies exact zero versus nonzero only on the frozen rows; its three selected primes are redundant fault-diversity lanes, not a CRT theorem, and its baseline-first self-test rejects 28 of 28 registered faults in normal and -O modes. The two comparators share the digest-bound fixture and row order, exact harmonic identity, count maps, symbolic endpoint branch, and selected Python association; the exact-rational lane additionally trusts Python Decimal directed-rounding semantics and this host's Python binary64 operations. The exact-enclosure route does not inspect Rust source or a compiled binary. Neither observation is a ULP count, universal or cross-platform bound, Rust conformance result, neighbor-count proof, estimator validation, support result, continuous shared-exclusions or PID theorem, calibration result, or application qualification. 5893-            "claim": "Eligible positive-integer (+1,+1,-1,-1) local terms use a deterministic Neumaier-compensated shifted harmonic prefix and source-symmetric two-range association. The frozen schema-2 corpus has 8,198 unique ordered rows: 6,920 exhaustive rectangular-arithmetic outer-box rows through n=16 and 1,278 declared stress rows through n=1,000,000. The outer box is not asserted to equal the runtime unique-shell image. Two finite-corpus comparators are intentionally distinct. First, the Python reproduction of the selected binary64 association differs from binary64(stored 80-digit Decimal prefix text) by at most 8 * f64::EPSILON nats; exactly 40 rows attain that maximum, first at zero-based row 7,598 with tuple (4,096, 1, 2,048, 2,048). This is the binary64-rounded-reference comparator. Second, 160-digit ROUND_FLOOR/ROUND_CEILING harmonic-prefix enclosures prove that the selected binary64 error against the exact harmonic rational has a unique maximum at zero-based row 7,673 with tuple (4,096, 4, 2,049, 2,049) and is strictly below 9.761311 * f64::EPSILON nats. Both observations are below the frozen absolute 32 * f64::EPSILON-nat review ceiling. The exact-rounded 80-digit Decimal vector differs from the stored prefix text on 6,509 rows and differs numerically on 5,934 rows, while all 8,198 binary64 conversions agree. All 6,920 exhaustive small rows additionally have exact Fraction containment witnesses. The exact-enclosure checker passes in normal and -O modes; its baseline-first self-test rejects 29 of 29 load-bearing mutations in each mode. The selected route has zero source-swap bit asymmetries and 354 canonical positive-zero structural endpoints with zero negative zeros, split 240/114 between exhaustive and stress rows. The modular certificate classifies exact zero versus nonzero only on the frozen rows; its three selected primes are redundant fault-diversity lanes, not a CRT theorem, and its baseline-first self-test rejects 28 of 28 registered faults in normal and -O modes. The two comparators share the digest-bound fixture and row order, exact harmonic identity, count maps, symbolic endpoint branch, and selected Python association; the exact-rational lane additionally trusts Python Decimal directed-rounding semantics and this host's Python binary64 operations. The exact-enclosure route does not inspect Rust source or a compiled binary. Neither observation is a ULP count, universal or cross-platform bound, Rust conformance result, neighbor-count proof, estimator validation, support result, continuous shared-exclusions or PID theorem, calibration result, or application qualification. Repository/publication integration remains NO-GO pending complete isolated-tree closure.",

7664-          "assurance": {
7665-            "claim": "Eligible positive-integer (+1,+1,-1,-1) local terms use a deterministic Neumaier-compensated shifted harmonic prefix and source-symmetric two-range association. The frozen schema-2 corpus has 8,198 unique ordered rows: 6,920 exhaustive rectangular-arithmetic outer-box rows through n=16 and 1,278 declared stress rows through n=1,000,000. The outer box is not asserted to equal the runtime unique-shell image. Two finite-corpus comparators are intentionally distinct. First, the Python reproduction of the selected binary64 association differs from binary64(stored 80-digit Decimal prefix text) by at most 8 * f64::EPSILON nats; exactly 40 rows attain that maximum, first at zero-based row 7,598 with tuple (4,096, 1, 2,048, 2,048). This is the binary64-rounded-reference comparator. Second, 160-digit ROUND_FLOOR/ROUND_CEILING harmonic-prefix enclosures prove that the selected binary64 error against the exact harmonic rational has a unique maximum at zero-based row 7,673 with tuple (4,096, 4, 2,049, 2,049) and is strictly below 9.761311 * f64::EPSILON nats. Both observations are below the frozen absolute 32 * f64::EPSILON-nat review ceiling. The exact-rounded 80-digit Decimal vector differs from the stored prefix text on 6,509 rows and differs numerically on 5,934 rows, while all 8,198 binary64 conversions agree. All 6,920 exhaustive small rows additionally have exact Fraction containment witnesses. The exact-enclosure checker passes in normal and -O modes; its baseline-first self-test rejects 29 of 29 load-bearing mutations in each mode. The selected route has zero source-swap bit asymmetries and 354 canonical positive-zero structural endpoints with zero negative zeros, split 240/114 between exhaustive and stress rows. The modular certificate classifies exact zero versus nonzero only on the frozen rows; its three selected primes are redundant fault-diversity lanes, not a CRT theorem, and its baseline-first self-test rejects 28 of 28 registered faults in normal and -O modes. The two comparators share the digest-bound fixture and row order, exact harmonic identity, count maps, symbolic endpoint branch, and selected Python association; the exact-rational lane additionally trusts Python Decimal directed-rounding semantics and this host's Python binary64 operations. The exact-enclosure route does not inspect Rust source or a compiled binary. Neither observation is a ULP count, universal or cross-platform bound, Rust conformance result, neighbor-count proof, estimator validation, support result, continuous shared-exclusions or PID theorem, calibration result, or application qualification. Repository/publication integration remains NO-GO pending complete isolated-tree closure.",
